critics.systems_engineer: In a 180nm 1T1C COB capacitor scheme, integrating a Ta2O5/Al2O3 nanolaminate dielectric over deep crown cylindrical topologies requires tight control of parasitic series resistance and leakage current. Ta2O5 provides a high relative dielectric permittivity (k ~ 25) but exhibits a low bandgap (~4.5 eV) and low conduction band offset relative to TiN/poly-Si electrodes, resulting in intolerable Fowler-Nordheim and Poole-Frenkel leakage without wide-bandgap Al2O3 (k ~ 9, Eg ~ 8.7 eV) barrier interleaving. Total equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) must be constrained below 3.5 nm to secure >25 fF/cell storage capacitance across the 180nm node footprint while maintaining cell leakage <1 fA/cell at 1.0V V_cc/2 operation.
critics.domain_expert: Thermal ALD execution using Tantalum Ethoxide (Ta(OC2H5)5 / PET) or TBTEMT together with Trimethylaluminum (TMA) and H2O/O3 oxidizers requires precise purge duration calibration to prevent transition into CVD mode. Ta(OC2H5)5 vapor delivery lines must be heated uniformly to 120-130°C to avert precursor condensation without triggering premature thermal decomposition above 160°C. Al2O3 buffer layers (0.8-1.2 nm) deposited at the bottom interface suppress low-k interfacial SiO2 or TiOx growth, while laminate bilayer pulsing must avoid crystallization of Ta2O5 into orthorhombic phase prior to post-deposition annealing (PDA), preserving amorphous continuity across high aspect ratio crown sidewalls.
critics.supply_chain: Tantalum precursor supply (electronic grade Pentaethoxytantalum 99.999% metal basis) and Trimethylaluminum (TMA, electronic grade 99.9999%) involve single-source specialized packaging in hazardous bubblers. TMA is pyrophoric with long lead-time cylinder certification (UN 3394 cylinders), whereas PET requires dedicated high-temperature bubbler heaters with specialized low-dead-volume ALD valves. High-purity carrier gas (99.9999% Ar/N2 with point-of-use gate purifiers reducing H2O/O2 <1 ppb) is mandatory to avoid gas-line precursor degradation and bubbler clogging.
critics.laya_pm: Deposition throughput is a severe bottleneck for this work package. The nanolaminate sequence entails extensive precursor dose/purge cycling (estimated 120-180 cycles total) with conservative N2 purge times (4 to 8 s) to clear bulky PET molecules from 3D crown cavities, yielding recipe runtimes in excess of 90 minutes per batch. Process signoff must synchronize strictly with downstream TiN top-electrode CVD/ALD to avoid breaking vacuum or exceeding queue time, preventing atmospheric moisture absorption on Ta2O5 surfaces.
critical_failure_modes: Parasitic chemical vapor deposition (CVD) due to insufficient purge of PET precursor, causing step-coverage thinning (<85%) and pinhole leakage along high-aspect-ratio crown sidewalls.
Interfacial oxidation forming low-k sub-oxides (TiOx/TaSiOx) at bottom electrode interfaces, elevating cell EOT beyond 4.0 nm and dropping cell capacitance below the 25 fF retention threshold.
Precursor line cold-spot condensation resulting in particle showering, causing catastrophic micro-shorts between bottom crown storage nodes and top cell plates.

testcases.title: Crown Sidewall Conformality and Total Physical Thickness Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (J.A. Woollam M-2000) for planar monitor wafers and High-Resolution Cross-Sectional Transmission Electron Microscopy (HR-XTEM, FEI Titan 80-300 kV) with EDS line scan for patterned crown structures.
testcases.pre_conditions: ALD reaction chamber base pressure < 5e-7 Torr; deposition zone stabilized at 250°C ± 1.0°C; incoming wafer verified cleaned through dilute HF (100:1, 30s) dip and in-situ degas; precursor bubbler temperatures stabilized (TMA at 20°C, PET at 125°C).
testcases.procedure: 1. Load dual-layer monitor test wafer (100mm Si with 50nm TiN) and patterned 180nm crown capacitor wafer into ALD loadlock. 2. Execute recipe: 1.0 nm Al2O3 seed layer (10 cycles TMA/H2O), followed by 5 nm Ta2O5 core layer (60 cycles PET/H2O), interleaved with 0.8 nm Al2O3 laminate barrier (8 cycles TMA/H2O), topped with 3 nm Ta2O5 capping layer (36 cycles PET/H2O). 3. Transfer to cool-down station under continuous N2 flow (>10 slm) for 10 minutes. 4. Measure physical thickness across 9 site points on planar monitor via spectroscopic ellipsometry (wavelength 245-1000 nm). 5. Cleave patterned wafer along crown array dense center, prepare TEM lamella via FIB, and acquire high-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) TEM micrographs at top, middle, and bottom crown sidewalls.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Total physical thickness on planar monitor must be 9.8 nm ± 0.4 nm with within-wafer non-uniformity (1-sigma) < 1.5%. Patterned crown sidewall conformality (thickness at bottom interior sidewall divided by thickness at top planar region) must be >= 95.0% with zero observable voids or interfacial delamination.

testcases.title: Capacitor Area Capacitance and Dielectric Leakage Current Density Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Agilent/Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Parameter Analyzer coupled with Cascade Microtech Summit 12000 Semi-Automatic Probe Station in shielded dark box.
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafers must have completed in-situ ALD nanolaminate deposition followed by 40 nm TiN top electrode sputter deposition and standard 400°C 30-min forming gas anneal (N2/H2 95/5); probe tip contact resistance verified < 2.0 Ohm on calibration pad.
testcases.procedure: 1. Mount wafer onto thermal vacuum chuck maintained at 25°C ± 0.5°C in dry N2 purged enclosure. 2. Contact 100 x 100 um test capacitor array structures across 13 dies (center, mid-radius, edge). 3. Apply high-frequency Capacitance-Voltage (C-V) sweep from -2.0 V to +2.0 V at 100 kHz with AC small-signal amplitude of 30 mV to extract dielectric accumulation capacitance and Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT). 4. Perform Current-Voltage (I-V) staircase ramp from 0.0 V to +2.5 V in increments of 50 mV with 500 ms hold time, recording leakage current (I_leak) at operating bias V_cell = 1.0 V.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Effective Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) must be <= 3.2 nm (corresponding to dielectric capacitance density >= 10.8 fF/um^2). Leakage current density (J_leak) at |V_bias| = 1.0 V must be <= 1.0 x 10^-8 A/cm^2 across >= 95% of tested dies.

ppe_required: Level A/B chemical resistant suit with static dissipative properties during precursor cylinder exchange
Full-face supplied-air respirator (SAR) or self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA) for TMA bubbler connection
Butyl rubber outer gloves over secondary disposable nitrile inner gloves (double gloving)
Safety face shield conforming to ANSI Z87.1 combined with UV/impact safety glasses
Fire-resistant Nomex lab coat and ESD-safe static-dissipative steel-toe footwear

cas_chemicals.name: Deionized Precursor Water (Ultra-Pure H2O)
cas_chemicals.purity_grade: UPW Grade (18.2 MOhm-cm resistivity, TOC < 1 ppb)

ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: TMA is violently pyrophoric upon air contact and reacts explosively with water. For skin contact, do NOT use water directly on burning liquid; smother immediately with dry vermiculite, dry sand, or Class D dry powder extinguishant, then drench affected area with copious saline solution once flame is extinguished. Remove contaminated clothing instantly. In case of inhalation of decomposition fumes (aluminum oxides and ethane), move victim immediately to fresh air, administer 100% humidified oxygen, and seek emergency pulmonary medical support. For eye contact with PET/TMA vapor, flush eyes immediately with isotonic eye wash for at least 15 minutes, holding eyelids open.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Continuous scrubbed toxic gas exhaust ducting operating under negative pressure differential >= -0.5 in. w.g. Dedicated point-of-use burn-wet scrubber (thermal oxidizer operating at >= 800°C followed by acidic/caustic scrubbing stages) designed for metal alkyl abatement. Gas cabinet must maintain minimum face velocity of 100 FPM (0.51 m/s) with continuous pyrophoric gas monitoring and UV/IR flame detection interlocked to emergency shutoff pneumatic valves (ESV).
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Exhaust lines must be periodically flushed with dry nitrogen. Precursor unreacted effluent passed through burn box to convert TMA and PET into inert Al2O3 and Ta2O5 particulates. Wet scrubber sump wastewater neutralized with sodium hydroxide (NaOH) or sulfuric acid (H2SO4) to pH 6.5-8.5 and filtered through 0.5 um ceramic particulate filters to precipitate dissolved metal complexes prior to discharge into industrial wastewater system.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Freshly etched bottom TiN crown electrode surface, post-dilute HF/SC-1 cleaned, with native oxide thickness < 0.3 nm and zero particulate contamination (defect count < 10 at >0.15 um).
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: As-deposited amorphous Ta2O5/Al2O3 nanolaminate dielectric film, moisture-free, chemically passivated under nitrogen ambient, ready for TiN top electrode deposition without ambient air exposure.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding Q-time before ALD induces airborne moisture adsorption and native TiOx growth on TiN bottom electrodes, degrading interface states and causing high leakage. Exceeding Q-time post-ALD leads to atmospheric moisture and organic carbon uptake by Ta2O5, generating trap states that result in high retention loss, stress-induced leakage current (SILC), and premature dielectric breakdown.

expected_result.summary: Successful baseline execution of Ta2O5/Al2O3 nanolaminate atomic layer deposition within a 180nm crown capacitor integration stack, achieving conformal, pinhole-free dielectric layers with sub-3.5 nm EOT and low leakage current density meeting DRAM cell retention specifications.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
**Document ID:** `SOP-MET-180-HIK01`  
**Title:** High-k Dielectric EOT, Step Coverage & Leakage Metrology (XRR / TEM / C-V)  
**Node Generation:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (Gen 2 µm)  
**Process Step Category:** Metrology / Quality Inspection  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

## 1. Process Workflow Overview

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│  Wafer Infeed: Crown  │
│         Stack         │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│      XRR: Planar      │
│  Thickness & Density  │
│         Fitting       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│    FIB-TEM: Crown     │
│   Sidewall / Bottom   │
│     Step Coverage     │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│  C-V & I-V Probing:   │
│  EOT, Capacitance &   │
│     Leakage @ 85°C    │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│  Acceptance Gating &  │
│       Pass/Fail       │
│      Disposition      │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

## 2. Step-by-Step Metrology Procedure

### Step 1: Pre-Measurement Inspection & Lot Loading
1. Transfer post-ALD $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5 / \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ crown-capacitor lot to the metrology cleanroom bay under class 1 environment.
2. Verify wafer alignment notch/flat orientation and ensure surface particles do not contaminate probe pads or test monitor sites.

### Step 2: X-Ray Reflectometry (XRR) Thickness & Density Verification
1. Load test monitor wafer onto the high-resolution XRR stage.
2. Perform specular $\theta - 2\theta$ scans across grazing incident angles ($0.2^\circ \le \theta \le 4.0^\circ$) on planar scribe-line monitor pads.
3. Fit interference fringe periodicity and critical angle ($\theta_c$) to extract physical layer thickness ($t_{\text{phys}}$) and material density of the high-k stack ($\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5 / \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$).

### Step 3: Dual-Beam FIB Sample Prep & Cross-Sectional TEM Metrology
1. Target array test cell containing high-aspect-ratio crown-shaped stacked capacitors.
2. Deposit protective electron-beam followed by ion-beam Pt strap.
3. Perform focused ion beam (FIB) micro-milling to prepare an ultra-thin cross-sectional lamella (<50 nm thickness).
4. Transfer lamella to high-resolution Transmission Electron Microscope (TEM) operating at 200 kV.
5. Acquire bright-field and high-angle annular dark-field (HAADF-STEM) images across the crown top, sidewall (mid-depth), and bottom cup regions.
6. Calculate conformational step coverage:
   $$\text{Step Coverage (\%)} = \frac{t_{\text{bottom}}}{t_{\text{top}}} \times 100\%$$

### Step 4: C-V & I-V Electrical Parameter Extraction
1. Mount wafer onto thermal probe station chuck heated to $85^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ to replicate worst-case DRAM refresh conditions.
2. Connect Kelvin probes to memory array test capacitor test structures with top/bottom electrodes.
3. Execute high-frequency C-V sweep (100 kHz – 1 MHz, $-1.5\text{ V}$ to $+1.5\text{ V}$):
   - Measure accumulated cell capacitance ($C_{\text{cell}}$).
   - Extract Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT):
     $$\text{EOT} = t_{\text{high-k}} \cdot \frac{\kappa_{\text{SiO}_2}}{\kappa_{\text{high-k}}}$$
4. Perform DC I-V leakage characterization at operating bias conditions at $85^\circ\text{C}$:
   - Measure sub-threshold, junction, and capacitor dielectric leakage current per cell ($I_{\text{leak}}$).

---

## 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Exact Tolerance / Range | Measurement Tool | Physical Units |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT)** | $3.5\text{ nm}$ | $3\text{ to } 4\text{ nm}$ | C-V Prober / Quasistatic Extraction | $\text{nm}$ |
| **Cell Capacitance ($C_{\text{cell}}$)** | $\ge 28\text{ fF/cell}$ | Minimum $25\text{ to } 30\text{ fF/cell}$ | HF C-V Impedance Analyzer ($85^\circ\text{C}$) | $\text{fF/cell}$ |
| **Cell Leakage Current ($I_{\text{leak}}$)** | $< 1.0\text{ fA/cell}$ | Max $1.0\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ | Semiconductor Parameter Analyzer (I-V @ $85^\circ\text{C}$) | $\text{fA/cell}$ |
| **Dielectric Effective Permittivity ($\kappa_{\text{eff}}$)** | $> 15$ | $\kappa > 15$ | Derived from C-V + TEM Physical Thickness | Dimensionless |

---

## 4. Literature & Context Sources

- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - *Context:* Minimum capacitance budget of $28\text{ fF}$ per cell ensures noise immunity against alpha-particle soft errors and bitline coupling; $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5 / \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ high-k stack providing effective dielectric constant $\kappa > 15$; leakage current target kept below $1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ to maintain refresh retention intervals.
- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**
  - *Context:* Storage capacitor must maintain $25\text{ to } 30\text{ fF/cell}$ for retention time $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$; crown-type stacked capacitor high-k dielectric ($\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$) requires Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) around $3\text{ to } 4\text{ nm}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Metrology on 180nm crown capacitor high-k stacks (Ta2O5/Al2O3) must establish a direct closed loop between physical thickness/step coverage and electrical storage capacitance (minimum 28 fF/cell). Relying strictly on planar witness wafer XRR measurements introduces systemic error because 3D crown sidewall ALD growth dynamics experience localized precursor depletion and aspect-ratio-dependent steric hindrance. TEM lamella preparation via FIB must target the bottom corner and sidewall midpoint of high-aspect-ratio crown nodes rather than planar areas to ensure capacitance models do not overestimate actual charge retention margins.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: C-V metrology at 10 kHz and 1 MHz on Ta2O5/Al2O3 stacks is prone to severe frequency dispersion and misleading EOT extraction if series resistance (Rs) from the bottom electrode or W-plug is not de-embedded via Nicollian-Goetzberger or dual-frequency models. Furthermore, ALD Ta2O5 exhibits oxygen vacancies that behave as trap states; post-deposition annealing (PDA) in N2O or O2 is required to suppress Poole-Frenkel conduction. Leakage metrology (I-V) must quantify current density at both positive and negative polarities (at ±1.0 V and 85°C) to verify that leakage remains strictly below the 1.0 fA/cell (or ~1.0e-8 A/cm^2) limit required for the 64 ms refresh window.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Availability and turnaround time of aberration-corrected Cs-TEM/STEM and dual-beam FIB tools represent a severe bottleneck for open-source fab line qualification. To avoid production idling during inline crown capacitor optimization, high-resolution XRR and spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) must be cross-calibrated against reference TEM lamellae so that non-destructive optical/X-ray metrics serve as the primary daily lot-release gate, reserving destructive cross-sectional TEM for weekly drift audits.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Dual-path metrology signoff (in-line XRR/ellipsometry within 2 hours vs. ex-situ cross-sectional TEM within 48 hours) must be scheduled to prevent wafer queue-time violations before top electrode deposition. If the high-k dielectric sits in fab air for extended durations, moisture absorption and hydrocarbon adsorption will degrade the EOT and dielectric breakdown field. Strict milestone gates require automated data ingestion into the metrology SPC engine prior to releasing lots to TiN top electrode deposition.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Premature electrical dielectric breakdown (< 3.0 MV/cm) caused by localized precursor starvation and thickness pinch-off at the re-entrant bottom corners of the crown structure.
1. Poole-Frenkel trap-assisted leakage exceeding 1 fA/cell at 85°C caused by unpassivated oxygen vacancies in the Ta2O5 sub-layers due to insufficient post-deposition anneal.
1. Parasitic interfacial low-k SiO2 or TiOx growth between the bottom electrode and high-k dielectric, inflating EOT beyond 3.5 nm and dropping cell capacitance below the critical 28 fF threshold.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-1-2-2-3-01` | **Cross-Sectional TEM/STEM Crown Step Coverage and Physical Thickness Verification** | Dual-Beam Ga+ FIB/SEM (FEI Helios or equivalent) with in-situ Pt deposition; 200 kV Field Emission Transmission Electron Microscope (FEI Titan/JEOL ARM) with HAADF-STEM detector and EDX mapping. | 1. Identify dedicated 180nm DRAM crown array test macro at center, middle, and edge wafer coordinates. 2. Deposit electron-beam Pt followed by ion-beam Pt protective strap over the crown array. 3. Perform dual-beam Ga+ FIB milling to extract site-specific cross-sectional lamella containing at least 5 intact crown capacitor cells. 4. Thin lamella to < 50 nm electron transparency at 30 kV, followed by 2 kV low-energy Ar+/Ga+ cleaning to eliminate amorphized surface damage. 5. Mount lamella into 200 kV TEM sample holder; orient along [110] zone axis. 6. Acquire high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) and HAADF-STEM images at 500kx and 1Mx magnification targeting top rim, middle sidewall, and bottom corner of the crown capacitor. 7. Execute EDX elemental line scans across the electrode-dielectric interface to verify chemical transition sharpness and absence of uncontrolled interdiffusion. 8. Measure physical thickness across 10 distinct points per region (top, sidewall, bottom). Calculate step coverage ratio as: (Thickness_bottom / Thickness_top) * 100%. | `Physical thickness of Al2O3/Ta2O5 laminate = 10.0 nm ± 0.8 nm; Crown sidewall-to-top step coverage >= 95.0%; Crown bottom-corner-to-top step coverage >= 90.0%; Interfacial oxide transition layer <= 0.5 nm.` |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-1-2-2-3-02` | **Cryo/Thermal C-V and I-V Leakage Density Metrology for EOT and Retention Budget** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer with B1520A Multifrequency C-V Module and B1517A High-Resolution SMU; Cascade Microtech Summit 12000 thermal probe station with dark box shielding. | 1. Load wafer onto thermal chuck inside shielded dark box purge chamber; purge with dry N2 to maintain relative humidity < 5%. 2. Lower probe tips onto top TiN capacitor pad and common bottom plate contact using low-contact-resistance tungsten tips. 3. Run high-frequency C-V sweep from -2.0 V to +2.0 V at 10 kHz, 100 kHz, and 1 MHz with a 25 mV AC oscillation level at 25°C. 4. Apply dual-frequency series resistance de-embedding to extract true accumulation capacitance (C_acc). 5. Compute Equivalent Oxide Thickness using EOT = (epsilon_0 * epsilon_SiO2 * A) / C_acc, where epsilon_SiO2 = 3.9. 6. Increase chuck temperature to 85°C ± 0.5°C and allow 15 minutes for thermal stabilization. 7. Perform quasi-static I-V staircase sweep from -1.5 V to +1.5 V with 50 mV steps and 1.0 s hold time per step; record leakage current I_leak. 8. Normalize leakage current to single DRAM cell area and calculate unit cell leakage at operating bias V_cell = 1.0 V. | `Extracted EOT <= 3.2 nm at 25°C; C-V frequency dispersion between 10 kHz and 1 MHz in accumulation < 4.0%; Leakage current density J_leak <= 1.0e-8 A/cm^2 at ±1.0 V at 85°C (equivalent to I_cell <= 0.8 fA/cell for 0.08 um^2 3D crown surface area); Dielectric breakdown field E_bd >= 4.5 MV/cm.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved, minimum 8 mil outer), ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash safety goggles and full-face polycarbonate shield, Flame-resistant, antistatic ESD cleanroom smock, Thermal protective gloves for heated probe chuck operations (> 85°C), Laser safety eyewear rated for optical metrology alignment lasers (Class 3R/3B)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For HF contact: Immediately flush affected skin or eyes with copious eyewash/water for exactly 2 minutes, then massage Calcium Gluconate 2.5% gel continuously into skin until emergency medical assistance arrives. For Gallium exposure: Remove contaminated apparel, flush skin with mild soap and water; seek medical evaluation if heated Ga causes thermal burns. For cryogenic/N2 asphyxiation hazards: Evacuate person to fresh air; administer oxygen or CPR if unconscious; call emergency response team immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: FIB/SEM and TEM specimen preparation stations must have dedicated local exhaust ventilation (LEV) operating at minimum 100 FPM face velocity. Metrology dry probe station enclosures require continuous nitrogen venting routed directly to house scrubbed exhaust to avoid gas accumulation and prevent asphyxiation.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Aqueous fluoride-containing waste from HF pre-cleans must be segregated in dedicated polyethylene carboys, treated with calcium hydroxide/calcium chloride slurry to precipitate calcium fluoride (CaF2), neutralized to pH 6.5 - 8.5, and verified via ion-selective electrode before effluent discharge. Solid contaminated wipes, FIB stubs, and TEM grids must be tagged as hazardous solid waste and disposed of via certified hazardous chemical reclamation vendors.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Gallium (FIB liquid metal ion source)** | `7440-55-3` | 99.9999% (6N) | `100.0%` |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (pre-metrology native oxide strip)** | `7664-39-3` | Semi Grade 1 (VLSI) | `0.5% aqueous solution` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (purge & pneumatic systems)** | `7727-37-9` | UHP Grade 5.0 (99.999%) | `100.0%` |
| **Isopropanol (wafer back-surface & chuck clean)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (SEMI C1) | `99.8%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly deposited and post-annealed (N2O/O2 PDA) Ta2O5/Al2O3 dielectric stack over TiN/polysilicon crown bottom storage node; particulate count < 5 defects @ >= 0.18 um; zero native oxide or water condensation.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Characterized high-k dielectric surface free of electron-beam/ion-beam carbon contamination, vacuum-stabilized, ready for immediate top electrode TiN/W-plug atomic layer deposition.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time in atmospheric air leads to ambient moisture absorption (OH incorporation) and airborne volatile organic carbon (VOC) condensation on the high-k surface. This produces fixed positive oxide charges (Q_ox), increases trap density (D_it > 1e12 eV^-1 cm^-2), inflates EOT by > 0.5 nm via interfacial oxidation, and triples Poole-Frenkel leakage, directly compromising DRAM data retention.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful metrological validation of Gen 2 (180nm) crown-shaped stacked capacitor high-k dielectric layer (Ta2O5/Al2O3) confirming target EOT <= 3.2 nm, conformal step coverage >= 90% across crown 3D geometries, and sub-1.0 fA/cell leakage current at 85°C to guarantee > 28 fF/cell storage capacitance and compliance with the 64 ms DRAM refresh specification.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `MET_180NM_CROWN_TEM_STEP_COVERAGE_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `MET_180NM_HIGHK_CV_IV_EXTRACTION_MATRIX.csv`
- [ ] `MET_180NM_HRTEM_HAADF_EDX_MICROGRAPHS.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) extracted from de-embedded 100 kHz C-V accumulation capacitance** | `3.0 nm` | +0.2 nm / -0.3 nm | Multi-frequency C-V series resistance correction and NCSU CVC quantum-corrected EOT extraction algorithm |

critics.systems_engineer: Metrology on 180nm crown capacitor high-k stacks (Ta2O5/Al2O3) must establish a direct closed loop between physical thickness/step coverage and electrical storage capacitance (minimum 28 fF/cell). Relying strictly on planar witness wafer XRR measurements introduces systemic error because 3D crown sidewall ALD growth dynamics experience localized precursor depletion and aspect-ratio-dependent steric hindrance. TEM lamella preparation via FIB must target the bottom corner and sidewall midpoint of high-aspect-ratio crown nodes rather than planar areas to ensure capacitance models do not overestimate actual charge retention margins.
critics.domain_expert: C-V metrology at 10 kHz and 1 MHz on Ta2O5/Al2O3 stacks is prone to severe frequency dispersion and misleading EOT extraction if series resistance (Rs) from the bottom electrode or W-plug is not de-embedded via Nicollian-Goetzberger or dual-frequency models. Furthermore, ALD Ta2O5 exhibits oxygen vacancies that behave as trap states; post-deposition annealing (PDA) in N2O or O2 is required to suppress Poole-Frenkel conduction. Leakage metrology (I-V) must quantify current density at both positive and negative polarities (at ±1.0 V and 85°C) to verify that leakage remains strictly below the 1.0 fA/cell (or ~1.0e-8 A/cm^2) limit required for the 64 ms refresh window.
critics.supply_chain: Availability and turnaround time of aberration-corrected Cs-TEM/STEM and dual-beam FIB tools represent a severe bottleneck for open-source fab line qualification. To avoid production idling during inline crown capacitor optimization, high-resolution XRR and spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) must be cross-calibrated against reference TEM lamellae so that non-destructive optical/X-ray metrics serve as the primary daily lot-release gate, reserving destructive cross-sectional TEM for weekly drift audits.
critics.laya_pm: Dual-path metrology signoff (in-line XRR/ellipsometry within 2 hours vs. ex-situ cross-sectional TEM within 48 hours) must be scheduled to prevent wafer queue-time violations before top electrode deposition. If the high-k dielectric sits in fab air for extended durations, moisture absorption and hydrocarbon adsorption will degrade the EOT and dielectric breakdown field. Strict milestone gates require automated data ingestion into the metrology SPC engine prior to releasing lots to TiN top electrode deposition.
critical_failure_modes: Premature electrical dielectric breakdown (< 3.0 MV/cm) caused by localized precursor starvation and thickness pinch-off at the re-entrant bottom corners of the crown structure.
Poole-Frenkel trap-assisted leakage exceeding 1 fA/cell at 85°C caused by unpassivated oxygen vacancies in the Ta2O5 sub-layers due to insufficient post-deposition anneal.
Parasitic interfacial low-k SiO2 or TiOx growth between the bottom electrode and high-k dielectric, inflating EOT beyond 3.5 nm and dropping cell capacitance below the critical 28 fF threshold.

testcases.title: Cross-Sectional TEM/STEM Crown Step Coverage and Physical Thickness Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Dual-Beam Ga+ FIB/SEM (FEI Helios or equivalent) with in-situ Pt deposition; 200 kV Field Emission Transmission Electron Microscope (FEI Titan/JEOL ARM) with HAADF-STEM detector and EDX mapping.
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer has completed ALD Ta2O5/Al2O3 nanolaminate deposition over 3D crown stacked capacitor matrix; wafer transferred in sealed dry N2 carrier box; protective carbon/platinum capping layer applied prior to FIB milling.
testcases.procedure: 1. Identify dedicated 180nm DRAM crown array test macro at center, middle, and edge wafer coordinates. 2. Deposit electron-beam Pt followed by ion-beam Pt protective strap over the crown array. 3. Perform dual-beam Ga+ FIB milling to extract site-specific cross-sectional lamella containing at least 5 intact crown capacitor cells. 4. Thin lamella to < 50 nm electron transparency at 30 kV, followed by 2 kV low-energy Ar+/Ga+ cleaning to eliminate amorphized surface damage. 5. Mount lamella into 200 kV TEM sample holder; orient along [110] zone axis. 6. Acquire high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) and HAADF-STEM images at 500kx and 1Mx magnification targeting top rim, middle sidewall, and bottom corner of the crown capacitor. 7. Execute EDX elemental line scans across the electrode-dielectric interface to verify chemical transition sharpness and absence of uncontrolled interdiffusion. 8. Measure physical thickness across 10 distinct points per region (top, sidewall, bottom). Calculate step coverage ratio as: (Thickness_bottom / Thickness_top) * 100%.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Physical thickness of Al2O3/Ta2O5 laminate = 10.0 nm ± 0.8 nm; Crown sidewall-to-top step coverage >= 95.0%; Crown bottom-corner-to-top step coverage >= 90.0%; Interfacial oxide transition layer <= 0.5 nm.

testcases.title: Cryo/Thermal C-V and I-V Leakage Density Metrology for EOT and Retention Budget
testcases.instrumentation: Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer with B1520A Multifrequency C-V Module and B1517A High-Resolution SMU; Cascade Microtech Summit 12000 thermal probe station with dark box shielding.
testcases.pre_conditions: Crown capacitor macro with deposited and patterned TiN top electrode pads (pad area A = 1.0e-4 cm^2); chuck temperature stabilized at 25°C and 85°C; triaxial cabling calibrated with open/short/load correction up to 1 MHz.
testcases.procedure: 1. Load wafer onto thermal chuck inside shielded dark box purge chamber; purge with dry N2 to maintain relative humidity < 5%. 2. Lower probe tips onto top TiN capacitor pad and common bottom plate contact using low-contact-resistance tungsten tips. 3. Run high-frequency C-V sweep from -2.0 V to +2.0 V at 10 kHz, 100 kHz, and 1 MHz with a 25 mV AC oscillation level at 25°C. 4. Apply dual-frequency series resistance de-embedding to extract true accumulation capacitance (C_acc). 5. Compute Equivalent Oxide Thickness using EOT = (epsilon_0 * epsilon_SiO2 * A) / C_acc, where epsilon_SiO2 = 3.9. 6. Increase chuck temperature to 85°C ± 0.5°C and allow 15 minutes for thermal stabilization. 7. Perform quasi-static I-V staircase sweep from -1.5 V to +1.5 V with 50 mV steps and 1.0 s hold time per step; record leakage current I_leak. 8. Normalize leakage current to single DRAM cell area and calculate unit cell leakage at operating bias V_cell = 1.0 V.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Extracted EOT <= 3.2 nm at 25°C; C-V frequency dispersion between 10 kHz and 1 MHz in accumulation < 4.0%; Leakage current density J_leak <= 1.0e-8 A/cm^2 at ±1.0 V at 85°C (equivalent to I_cell <= 0.8 fA/cell for 0.08 um^2 3D crown surface area); Dielectric breakdown field E_bd >= 4.5 MV/cm.

ppe_required: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved, minimum 8 mil outer)
ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash safety goggles and full-face polycarbonate shield
Flame-resistant, antistatic ESD cleanroom smock
Thermal protective gloves for heated probe chuck operations (> 85°C)
Laser safety eyewear rated for optical metrology alignment lasers (Class 3R/3B)
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: For HF contact: Immediately flush affected skin or eyes with copious eyewash/water for exactly 2 minutes, then massage Calcium Gluconate 2.5% gel continuously into skin until emergency medical assistance arrives. For Gallium exposure: Remove contaminated apparel, flush skin with mild soap and water; seek medical evaluation if heated Ga causes thermal burns. For cryogenic/N2 asphyxiation hazards: Evacuate person to fresh air; administer oxygen or CPR if unconscious; call emergency response team immediately.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: FIB/SEM and TEM specimen preparation stations must have dedicated local exhaust ventilation (LEV) operating at minimum 100 FPM face velocity. Metrology dry probe station enclosures require continuous nitrogen venting routed directly to house scrubbed exhaust to avoid gas accumulation and prevent asphyxiation.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Aqueous fluoride-containing waste from HF pre-cleans must be segregated in dedicated polyethylene carboys, treated with calcium hydroxide/calcium chloride slurry to precipitate calcium fluoride (CaF2), neutralized to pH 6.5 - 8.5, and verified via ion-selective electrode before effluent discharge. Solid contaminated wipes, FIB stubs, and TEM grids must be tagged as hazardous solid waste and disposed of via certified hazardous chemical reclamation vendors.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Freshly deposited and post-annealed (N2O/O2 PDA) Ta2O5/Al2O3 dielectric stack over TiN/polysilicon crown bottom storage node; particulate count < 5 defects @ >= 0.18 um; zero native oxide or water condensation.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Characterized high-k dielectric surface free of electron-beam/ion-beam carbon contamination, vacuum-stabilized, ready for immediate top electrode TiN/W-plug atomic layer deposition.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding queue time in atmospheric air leads to ambient moisture absorption (OH incorporation) and airborne volatile organic carbon (VOC) condensation on the high-k surface. This produces fixed positive oxide charges (Q_ox), increases trap density (D_it > 1e12 eV^-1 cm^-2), inflates EOT by > 0.5 nm via interfacial oxidation, and triples Poole-Frenkel leakage, directly compromising DRAM data retention.

nodes.sop_content:
# SOP: COB Storage Node Capacitance & Sub-fA Cell Leakage Metrology Validation

**Module**: Metrology & Characterization  
**Hierarchy Context**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > 180nm 1T1C DRAM Cell Bitline & Wordline Matrix Layout > COB Stacked Capacitor & Tungsten Bitline Contact Integration Routing > Metrology  
**Technology Generation**: Gen 2 (180 nm / 0.18 µm)  
**Process Action**: Make (Electrical Metrology & Parametric Characterization)

---

### Metrology Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Wafer Chuck Thermal   │
│  Stabilization at 85   │
│         deg C          │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  W-Plug Storage Node   │
│  Contact Resistance &  │
│     Kelvin Nulling     │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│     Array Storage      │
│      Capacitance       │
│   Extraction at 100    │
│      kHz - 1 MHz       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│     Sub-fA Access      │
│  Transistor Off-State  │
│   & Junction Leakage   │
│       Extraction       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Cb / Cs Ratio & Read  │
│   Margin Compliance    │
│      Verification      │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Capacitance Budget & Operating Boundaries

```text
                 ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
                 │░░░                                │
Cb/Cs Ratio Upper┤░░░                                │
                 │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
  BL Parasitic Cb┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
    Min Cs Budget┤▓▓▓▓▓                              │
                 │▓▓▓▓▓                              │
       Nominal Cs┤██████                             │
                 │██████                             │
                 └┬────────┬───────┬────────┬───────┬┘
                  0       50      100      150    200 
```

---

## 1. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

### Step 1: Wafer Test Setup & Thermal Chamber Stabilization
1. Mount the 180nm processed test wafer onto the triaxial parametric probe station chuck.
2. Configure the thermal chuck to **85°C ± 0.5°C** to measure worst-case thermal leakage and guarantee data retention testing under operational specification.
3. Purge the probe enclosure with dry $N_2$ (dew point $< -40^\circ\text{C}$) to prevent condensation or leakage across probe needles.
4. Execute open/short/load calibration and triaxial guard nulling on the parametric analyzer (down to femtoampere noise floor).

### Step 2: Storage Node Contact Kelvin Nulling & Continuity Check
1. Land low-leakage Kelvin probes onto the test vehicle's Storage Node contact pad arrays connected to the tungsten plug (W-plug).
2. Apply a low bias ($\pm 50\text{ mV}$) across the W-plug drain contact to verify ohmic continuity and de-embed parasitic contact routing resistance prior to AC C-V sweeps.

### Step 3: Array C-V Storage Node Capacitance Extraction ($C_s$)
1. Connect the LCR meter / precision impedance analyzer to a $1024$-cell or $2048$-cell parallel test array structure (crown/cylinder stacked capacitor over bitline with high-$k$ dielectric such as $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$ or ONO stack, $\kappa > 15$, $\text{EOT} = 3\text{ to }4\text{ nm}$).
2. Apply an AC oscillation voltage $V_{\text{osc}} = 25\text{ mV}$ RMS at frequencies from **$100\text{ kHz}$ to $1\text{ MHz}$**.
3. Sweep the DC plate bias across the cell plate voltage range ($0\text{ V}$ to $V_{DD}/2 = 0.9\text{ V}$).
4. Calculate single-cell capacitance $C_s$:
   $$C_s = \frac{C_{\text{measured, array}} - C_{\text{open\_deembed}}}{N_{\text{cells}}}$$
   Ensure $C_s$ satisfies the nominal target of **$28\text{ fF}$** (minimum $\ge 25\text{ fF}$).

### Step 4: Sub-fA Access Transistor & Junction Leakage Extraction
1. Bias the access NMOS transistor ($W = 220\text{ nm}$, $L = 180\text{ nm}$, gate dielectric physical thickness $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$) into the off-state:
   - Wordline (Gate) bias: $V_{WL} = 0.0\text{ V}$ (or negative wordline hold bias).
   - Bitline contact: $V_{BL} = 0.0\text{ V}$.
   - Storage Node: Precharge to $V_{SN} = V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$.
2. Measure leakage current integrating over an extended integration aperture (long integration mode with triaxial guards active) at **$85^\circ\text{C}$**.
3. De-convolve the combined drain junction reverse leakage and sub-threshold leakage per unit cell. Confirm the measured leakage does not exceed **$1.0\text{ fA/cell}$**.

### Step 5: Bitline Capacitance ($C_b$) and Ratio Validation
1. Measure bitline capacitance on array blocks containing **256 or 512 cells per bitline**.
2. Extract total bitline parasitic capacitance $C_b$ (target range **$150\text{ fF}$ to $250\text{ fF}$**).
3. Compute the bitline-to-cell capacitance ratio $C_b / C_s$:
   - Verify that the ratio stays strictly between **$5:1$ and $9:1$** (never exceeding **$10:1$**), ensuring adequate sensing signal margin before bitline sense-amplifier latching.

---

## 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Metric Parameter | Target Value | Acceptable Limits | Engineering Units | Validation Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Storage Node Capacitance ($C_s$)** | $28.0$ | $25.0 \le C_s \le 30.0$ | $\text{fF/cell}$ | AC Multi-frequency C-V extraction ($100\text{ kHz} - 1\text{ MHz}$) |
| **Total Cell Off-State Leakage Current ($I_{\text{leak}}$)** | $< 0.8$ | $\le 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Triaxial SMU integration at $V_{SN} = 1.8\text{ V}$, $85^\circ\text{C}$ |
| **Bitline Parasitic Capacitance ($C_b$)** | $200.0$ | $150.0 \le C_b \le 250.0$ | $\text{fF}$ | Block parasitic C-V sweep (256/512 cells/BL) |
| **Capacitance Ratio ($C_b / C_s$)** | $7.0 : 1$ | $5.0 : 1 \le C_b / C_s \le 9.0 : 1$ (Max $10.0 : 1$) | Dimensionless | Ratio calculation for read signal margin |

---

## 3. Literature Context Citations

1. **Capacitance & Dielectric Metrics**:
   - Nominal storage capacitance $C_s \ge 25\text{ fF}$ to $30\text{ fF}$ per cell (nominally $28\text{ fF}$) with ONO/$\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$ high-$k$ dielectric ($\kappa > 15$, $\text{EOT} = 3\text{ nm} - 4\text{ nm}$).  
     *Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench; Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering.*
2. **Access Transistor Dimensions & Off-State Leakage**:
   - Access NMOS $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$, $T_{ox} \sim 3.5\text{ nm}$, with sub-threshold/junction leakage target $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ guaranteeing retention $> 64\text{ ms}$.  
     *Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench; Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering.*
3. **Array Parasitics & Margin Constraint**:
   - Array bitline block with 256 or 512 cells exhibiting $C_b = 150\text{ fF}$ to $250\text{ fF}$, requiring $C_b / C_s$ maintained between $5:1$ and $9:1$ (degrading severely if exceeding $10:1$).  
     *Source: 1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets.*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Direct probing of an isolated 28 fF capacitor cannot overcome the 1-2 pF parasitic capacitance of conventional analytical probe needles and coax cables; metrology must strictly utilize dedicated on-chip Kelvin test structures (1k-to-10k parallel capacitor arrays) or gated integrators with guard rings to cancel parasitic capacitances and deconvolve sub-femtoampere cell leakage from periphery pad leakage.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 85°C, distinguishing between storage node dielectric Poole-Frenkel conduction, access transistor subthreshold leakage, and Si/SiO2 junction band-to-band tunneling requires dual-temperature sweep metrology (25°C and 85°C) and variable wordline negative back-bias (-0.5V to -1.0V) to suppress channel subthreshold current below the 1 fA target floor.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Sub-fA characterization demands ultra-low-current semiconductor parameter analyzers (e.g., Keysight B1500A with High-Resolution SMU / B1517A HRSMU) and triaxial probe cards with dry nitrogen purge enclosures, creating a significant testing equipment bottleneck if parallel multi-site wafer-level probing is not established early.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Metrology throughput must balance the slow settling time (>10-30 seconds per measurement point for sub-fA settling due to RC cable delays) against wafer lot cycle time; sampling must be limited to a 9-point wafer map matrix for Gen 2 silicon validation to meet project tapeout milestones.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Triaxial cable dielectric absorption and mechanical microphonics generating spurious displacement currents exceeding 10 fA, masking true cell junction leakage.
1. Capacitor bottom electrode contact resistance or tungsten plug voiding causing incomplete charging during high-frequency C-V extraction, yielding erroneously low apparent capacitance.
1. Moisture condensation and surface ionic contamination across unpassivated scribe-line test pads causing lateral parasitic leakage > 100 fA under elevated humidity/temperature.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-1-2-3-01` | **COB Storage Node C-V Array Capacitance Extraction** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer with B1520A Multi-Frequency Capacitance Measurement Unit (MFCMU) and triaxial probe station enclosed in an EMI/dark Faraday cage. | 1. Land triaxial probes on the array storage node contact pad and common top plate pad. 2. Apply a 100 kHz AC test signal with 30 mV RMS oscillation amplitude. 3. Sweep DC bias voltage from -1.5 V to +1.5 V across the storage node dielectric with 50 mV step increments. 4. Record parallel capacitance (Cp) and dissipation factor (D) across the bias range. 5. Normalize extracted total parallel capacitance by dividing by 10,000 to determine single-cell equivalent capacitance (C_s). | `Single-cell equivalent capacitance C_s >= 28.0 fF at V_cell = 0.9 V (nominal VDD/2 plate bias); dissipation factor D < 0.02 across -1.0 V to +1.0 V.` |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-1-2-3-02` | **Sub-Femtoampere Storage Node Retention Leakage at 85°C** | Keysight B1500A equipped with B1517A High Resolution SMU (0.1 fA measurement resolution), triaxially guarded probe wedge, thermal chuck with dry N2 purge (<5% RH). | 1. Contact probe tips to isolated 1T1C addressable Kelvin test macro. 2. Force V_plate = 0.9 V and write '1' state by pulsing Wordline to 2.5 V while Bitline is at 1.8 V, then return Wordline to -0.5 V to trap charge on the storage node. 3. Connect B1517A HRSMU to storage node monitoring tap with guard shield active. 4. Allow 45-second electrometer settling time to dissipate cable dielectric relaxation currents. 5. Integrate DC leakage current over 60 seconds with 10 Power Line Cycle (PLC) aperture filtering. | `Total quiescent leakage current I_leak <= 1.0 fA/cell at T = 85°C and V_cell = 1.8 V; leakage current standard deviation sigma < 0.15 fA over the 60-second window.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal-insulating cleanroom gloves rated for -50°C to 150°C, ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses with side shields, ESD-safe dissipative lab coat and grounded wrist strap, High-purity nitrile gloves (0.1 mm minimum thickness)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of thermal burn from heated wafer chuck, immediately immerse affected skin in cool clean running water for 15 minutes and seek medical evaluation. For chemical contact with IPA, flush skin or eyes with emergency eye wash/shower for at least 15 minutes; remove contaminated cleanroom apparel. In event of N2 purge asphyxiation risk or oxygen alarm, evacuate personnel immediately to fresh air.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Prober enclosure must maintain constant laminar exhaust ventilation with a minimum capture velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM); room must feature calibrated ambient O2 deficiency sensors set to alarm if O2 drops below 19.5% by volume due to N2 thermal chuck purging.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA solvent wipes and residue must be discarded into designated grounded, self-closing hazardous solvent waste cans for off-site thermal incineration; exhaust vapors scrubbed through active carbon VOC abatement ducting.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Electronic Grade | `>= 99.9%` |
| **Nitrogen Gas (Gaseous)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra High Purity (UHP) Grade 6.0 | `>= 99.9999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly etched/ashed Storage Node contact pads post-M1/W-plug CMP, cleaned with solvent rinse and dried, free of organic residues and native oxide > 0.5 nm.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Electrically characterized wafer surface with unburned probe marks (< 5 um scrub depth), dried and vacuum-sealed under positive N2 pressurization ready for passivation deposition.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding Q-time in ambient air causes atmospheric moisture absorption and native oxidation of exposed tungsten/aluminum probe pads, resulting in erratic probe contact resistance and parasitic surface leakage exceeding 50 fA.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Demonstration and empirical validation that the Gen 2 180nm COB DRAM cell achieves minimum cell storage capacitance >= 28 fF/cell via C-V array extraction, and exhibits total combined storage node leakage under 1.0 fA/cell at 85°C with negative wordline bias, verifying charge retention requirements for a standard 64ms refresh window.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `COB_Capacitance_CV_Extraction_Report_Gen2.pdf`
- [ ] `Sub_fA_Leakage_85C_MultiSite_Data.csv`
- [ ] `WaferMap_Capacitance_Uniformity_DielectricBreakdown.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Normalized single-cell storage capacitance (C_s) extracted from 10k-cell COB parallel test array at 100 kHz and VDD/2 plate bias** | `28.5 fF` | +/- 1.5 fF (minimum threshold >= 28.0 fF) | Multi-frequency C-V analysis using Keysight B1520A MFCMU at 100 kHz, 25°C |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Total cell leakage current (I_leak) per 1T1C cell at nominal operating temperature with access transistor turned off** | `0.75 fA` | <= 1.0 fA maximum limit at 85°C | High-resolution triaxial electrometer DC current integration using Keysight B1517A HRSMU with V_NWL = -0.5 V |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Capacitor dielectric dissipation factor (tan delta) across operational voltage envelope** | `0.010` | <= 0.020 across -1.0 V to +1.0 V DC bias | Direct parallel dissipation parameter logging via impedance analyzer module |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> A 9-point wafer-level metrology sweep confirming >= 95% of tested dies satisfy C_s >= 28.0 fF and I_leak <= 1.0 fA/cell at 85°C, with formal sign-off approval from both Lead Metrology Engineer and DRAM Architecture Integration Lead recorded in the metrology verification report.

critics.systems_engineer: Direct probing of an isolated 28 fF capacitor cannot overcome the 1-2 pF parasitic capacitance of conventional analytical probe needles and coax cables; metrology must strictly utilize dedicated on-chip Kelvin test structures (1k-to-10k parallel capacitor arrays) or gated integrators with guard rings to cancel parasitic capacitances and deconvolve sub-femtoampere cell leakage from periphery pad leakage.
critics.domain_expert: At 85°C, distinguishing between storage node dielectric Poole-Frenkel conduction, access transistor subthreshold leakage, and Si/SiO2 junction band-to-band tunneling requires dual-temperature sweep metrology (25°C and 85°C) and variable wordline negative back-bias (-0.5V to -1.0V) to suppress channel subthreshold current below the 1 fA target floor.
critics.supply_chain: Sub-fA characterization demands ultra-low-current semiconductor parameter analyzers (e.g., Keysight B1500A with High-Resolution SMU / B1517A HRSMU) and triaxial probe cards with dry nitrogen purge enclosures, creating a significant testing equipment bottleneck if parallel multi-site wafer-level probing is not established early.
critics.laya_pm: Metrology throughput must balance the slow settling time (>10-30 seconds per measurement point for sub-fA settling due to RC cable delays) against wafer lot cycle time; sampling must be limited to a 9-point wafer map matrix for Gen 2 silicon validation to meet project tapeout milestones.
critical_failure_modes: Triaxial cable dielectric absorption and mechanical microphonics generating spurious displacement currents exceeding 10 fA, masking true cell junction leakage.
Capacitor bottom electrode contact resistance or tungsten plug voiding causing incomplete charging during high-frequency C-V extraction, yielding erroneously low apparent capacitance.
Moisture condensation and surface ionic contamination across unpassivated scribe-line test pads causing lateral parasitic leakage > 100 fA under elevated humidity/temperature.

testcases.title: COB Storage Node C-V Array Capacitance Extraction
testcases.instrumentation: Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer with B1520A Multi-Frequency Capacitance Measurement Unit (MFCMU) and triaxial probe station enclosed in an EMI/dark Faraday cage.
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer loaded on temperature-controlled chuck stabilized at 25.0°C ± 0.5°C; triaxial cables open/short/load compensated up to probe tips; 10,000-cell parallel COB test array grounded at plate electrode.
testcases.procedure: 1. Land triaxial probes on the array storage node contact pad and common top plate pad. 2. Apply a 100 kHz AC test signal with 30 mV RMS oscillation amplitude. 3. Sweep DC bias voltage from -1.5 V to +1.5 V across the storage node dielectric with 50 mV step increments. 4. Record parallel capacitance (Cp) and dissipation factor (D) across the bias range. 5. Normalize extracted total parallel capacitance by dividing by 10,000 to determine single-cell equivalent capacitance (C_s).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Single-cell equivalent capacitance C_s >= 28.0 fF at V_cell = 0.9 V (nominal VDD/2 plate bias); dissipation factor D < 0.02 across -1.0 V to +1.0 V.

testcases.title: Sub-Femtoampere Storage Node Retention Leakage at 85°C
testcases.instrumentation: Keysight B1500A equipped with B1517A High Resolution SMU (0.1 fA measurement resolution), triaxially guarded probe wedge, thermal chuck with dry N2 purge (<5% RH).
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer chuck heated to 85.0°C ± 0.2°C under continuous dry N2 shroud; triaxial guard driven to storage node potential; access transistor Wordline tied to V_NWL = -0.5 V (negative wordline off-state bias); Bitline precharged to V_BL = 0.0 V.
testcases.procedure: 1. Contact probe tips to isolated 1T1C addressable Kelvin test macro. 2. Force V_plate = 0.9 V and write '1' state by pulsing Wordline to 2.5 V while Bitline is at 1.8 V, then return Wordline to -0.5 V to trap charge on the storage node. 3. Connect B1517A HRSMU to storage node monitoring tap with guard shield active. 4. Allow 45-second electrometer settling time to dissipate cable dielectric relaxation currents. 5. Integrate DC leakage current over 60 seconds with 10 Power Line Cycle (PLC) aperture filtering.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Total quiescent leakage current I_leak <= 1.0 fA/cell at T = 85°C and V_cell = 1.8 V; leakage current standard deviation sigma < 0.15 fA over the 60-second window.

ppe_required: Thermal-insulating cleanroom gloves rated for -50°C to 150°C
ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses with side shields
ESD-safe dissipative lab coat and grounded wrist strap
High-purity nitrile gloves (0.1 mm minimum thickness)
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: In case of thermal burn from heated wafer chuck, immediately immerse affected skin in cool clean running water for 15 minutes and seek medical evaluation. For chemical contact with IPA, flush skin or eyes with emergency eye wash/shower for at least 15 minutes; remove contaminated cleanroom apparel. In event of N2 purge asphyxiation risk or oxygen alarm, evacuate personnel immediately to fresh air.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Prober enclosure must maintain constant laminar exhaust ventilation with a minimum capture velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM); room must feature calibrated ambient O2 deficiency sensors set to alarm if O2 drops below 19.5% by volume due to N2 thermal chuck purging.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Used IPA solvent wipes and residue must be discarded into designated grounded, self-closing hazardous solvent waste cans for off-site thermal incineration; exhaust vapors scrubbed through active carbon VOC abatement ducting.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Freshly etched/ashed Storage Node contact pads post-M1/W-plug CMP, cleaned with solvent rinse and dried, free of organic residues and native oxide > 0.5 nm.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Electrically characterized wafer surface with unburned probe marks (< 5 um scrub depth), dried and vacuum-sealed under positive N2 pressurization ready for passivation deposition.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding Q-time in ambient air causes atmospheric moisture absorption and native oxidation of exposed tungsten/aluminum probe pads, resulting in erratic probe contact resistance and parasitic surface leakage exceeding 50 fA.

expected_result.summary: Demonstration and empirical validation that the Gen 2 180nm COB DRAM cell achieves minimum cell storage capacitance >= 28 fF/cell via C-V array extraction, and exhibits total combined storage node leakage under 1.0 fA/cell at 85°C with negative wordline bias, verifying charge retention requirements for a standard 64ms refresh window.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Normalized single-cell storage capacitance (C_s) extracted from 10k-cell COB parallel test array at 100 kHz and VDD/2 plate bias
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Multi-frequency C-V analysis using Keysight B1520A MFCMU at 100 kHz, 25°C

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Total cell leakage current (I_leak) per 1T1C cell at nominal operating temperature with access transistor turned off
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: High-resolution triaxial electrometer DC current integration using Keysight B1517A HRSMU with V_NWL = -0.5 V

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Capacitor dielectric dissipation factor (tan delta) across operational voltage envelope
quantitative_assertions.tolerance: <= 0.020 across -1.0 V to +1.0 V DC bias
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Direct parallel dissipation parameter logging via impedance analyzer module

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Test Structure Kelvin Array & Guard-Ring Pad Design for Sub-fA Probing

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Kelvin Force/Sense   │
│    Core Pad Layout     │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│     Active Driven      │
│  Guard-Ring Enclosure  │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Array Multiplexing &  │
│   Dummy Terminations   │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Sub-fA Triaxial     │
│      Electrometer      │
│      Interconnect      │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│      Cryo/Thermal      │
│  Metrology Chamber at  │
│        85 deg C        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **4-Terminal Kelvin Pad Geometry Definition**:
   - Layout dual force/sense pad pairs for bitline and storage node metrology to isolate parasitic series resistance from prober tips, probe needles, and routing metals.
   - Separate force and sense lines directly down to the lowest metallization layer (Metal 1) adjacent to the access transistor channel ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$).

2. **Driven Guard-Ring Topology & Dielectric Shielding**:
   - Enclose all sensitive DUT nodes (cell node test pad and sub-threshold leakage sense lines) with an active driven guard ring.
   - Route guard rings on all metal levels surrounding the signal line, connected to an active unity-gain buffer matching the inner signal potential to eliminate lateral oxide leakage ($I = \Delta V / R_{\text{ox}} \to 0$).

3. **Kelvin Array Array Matrix Routing**:
   - Route bitline and wordline test buses conforming to the technology pitch: wordline/bitline pitch between $360\text{ nm}$ and $400\text{ nm}$.
   - Place array boundary dummy cells around the Kelvin test cell matrix to match optical proximity effects (OPC) and stacked capacitor etch planarization.

4. **Triaxial Pad Interface & High-k Dielectric Leakage Probing**:
   - Interface pad structures with low-noise triaxial probe configurations (Center: Force/Sense Signal, Inner Shield: Active Guard, Outer Shield: Ground/Chassis).
   - Configure parameter analyzer/electrometer integration time to validate stacked capacitor dielectric leakage and access transistor off-state current at wafer-chuck temperature set to $85^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
       Key Physical Cell Targets (180nm COB Node)
                             ┌─────────────────────────┐
                             │░░░░░░░░                 │
 Storage Cap Budget (fF/cell)┤░░░░░░░░                 │
Target Leakage @85C (fA/cell)┤▒                        │
                             │▒                        │
    Sense Amp BL Delta V (mV)┤█████████████████████████│
                             │█████████████████████████│
                             └┬─────┬─────┬─────┬─────┬┘
                              0    25    50    75   100 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Machine-Measurable Target | Physical Unit | Measurement Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cell Leakage Current ($I_{\text{leak}}$)** | $< 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Sub-threshold and junction leakage at $85^\circ\text{C}$ wafer chuck |
| **Storage Node Capacitance ($C_s$)** | $25.0 \text{ to } 30.0$ (min $28.0$) | $\text{fF/cell}$ | High-frequency CV meter at $100\text{ kHz} - 1\text{ MHz}$ |
| **Interconnect Routing Pitch (BL & WL)** | $360 \text{ to } 400$ | $\text{nm}$ | Inline CD-SEM / In-die AFM metrology |
| **Cell Transistor Geometry ($L \times W$)** | $L = 180, \; W = 220$ | $\text{nm}$ | Inline CD-SEM inspection after poly gate etch |
| **Data Retention Window** | $> 64$ | $\text{ms}$ | Validated retention time at $85^\circ\text{C}$ operating temperature |

---

### 3. Literature Citations & Context Alignment

- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - Confirms unit cell channel dimensions ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$), minimum capacitance budget of $28\text{ fF/cell}$, and maximum leakage current target $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**:
  - Establishes storage capacitor target range ($25\text{ to } 30\text{ fF}$ per cell), data retention requirement $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$, gate oxide thickness of $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$, and bitline/wordline pitch range of $360\text{ nm to } 400\text{ nm}$.
- **Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout**:
  - Establishes differential bitline signal development target $\Delta V = 100\text{ mV to } 150\text{ mV}$ based on $C_s = 25\text{ fF}$ and $C_{\text{BL}} = 250\text{ fF}$, setting the noise margin baseline for guard-ring shielding integrity.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Measuring sub-femtoampere (<1 fA) leakage at 85°C across dense 180nm 1T1C storage nodes requires complete isolation from external instrumentation noise, microphonics, and dielectric absorption. The pad layout must integrate concentric active-driven guard rings on Metal-1/Metal-2 matching the probe potential (V_guard = V_force) to null parasitic pad-to-substrate and inter-pad fringing capacitances down to <10 fF. Without 4-wire Kelvin force/sense lines routed symmetrically to eliminate series probe-contact resistance (R_contact ~ 5-10 Ohm) and cable lead leakage, resolving true cell junction/dielectric leakage from setup parasitics is mathematically impossible.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At the 180nm node, unit cell capacitance is strictly budgeted to 28 fF with a sub-threshold/junction leakage ceiling of 1.0 fA/cell at 85°C. When laying out the Kelvin array test structures, pad-to-pad dielectric leakage across inter-layer dielectrics (SiO2/Si3N4) easily swamps sub-fA metrics unless a dedicated p-well/n-well guard tap tied to driven guard potentials completely encircles the force pad. Furthermore, the triaxial guarding must extend down to the passivated pad opening edge to prevent surface moisture condensation and ionic contamination from generating nano-ampere leakage paths.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Sub-fA characterization mandates low-noise triaxial probe stations (e.g., MPI/Cascade Microtech) with specialized beryllium-copper or tungsten probe needles and triaxial feedthroughs boasting <0.1 fA baseline floor. In Vietnam's local semiconductor ecosystem, lead times for replacement sub-picoamp triaxial cables, dry nitrogen environmental chambers, and high-precision SMUs (e.g., Keysight B1500A with HRSMU/B1517A) exceed 16-20 weeks; dual-sourcing probe tips and procuring hermetic wafer transfer pods with desiccant dry-boxes is critical to avoid project paralysis.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The pad pitch, pad opening footprint (minimum 60x60 um for automated probe card landing), and Kelvin guard structure layout must freeze within Milestone 2 without ballooning test-die silicon real estate beyond the allocated 1.2 mm^2 scribe-line budget. Delaying sign-off on the Kelvin array design directly blocks the physical validation reality gate of discrete transistors and COB storage node leakage metrology scheduled for wafer tape-out.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Guard-ring potential offset induced by SMU buffer amplifier offset voltage (>500 uV), driving significant parasitic current across the guard-to-sense oxide dielectric and masking intrinsic sub-fA cell leakage.
1. Dielectric polarization and charge absorption in inter-metal dielectric (TEOS/SiO2) under high electric fields, producing pseudo-leakage transient currents with decay constants exceeding test settle times (>60 s).
1. Surface moisture film formation and ionic sodium/potassium contamination across unpassivated pad perimeters due to uncontrolled humidity (>30% RH), degrading pad isolation below 10^14 Ohms.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-1-2-3-1-01` | **Sub-fA Open-Circuit Pad-to-Substrate Guard Ring Isolation Verification** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Parameter Analyzer with B1517A High-Resolution SMU (HRSMU, 0.1 fA resolution), Triaxial Kelvin Chuck Shielded Probe Station, Dry N2 Purged Thermal Enclosure (<10% RH). | 1. Lower triaxial Kelvin probe tips onto Force, Sense, and Guard pads of open-circuit test structure. 2. Apply V_force = 1.80 V on Force pad. 3. Configure Guard SMU to track Force potential (V_guard = 1.80 V +/- 0.1 mV) via active triaxial guard drive. 4. Hold voltage for 60 seconds settling time to dissipate dielectric polarization charge. 5. Integrate current measurement using Long Integration Time (16 PLC) over 50 consecutive samples. | `Pad-to-substrate leakage current I_leak <= 0.50 fA at V_force = 1.80 V and T = 85°C. Guard ring isolation resistance R_iso >= 3.6 x 10^15 Ohms.` |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-1-2-3-1-02` | **4-Terminal Kelvin Contact & Series Interconnect Resistance Characterization** | Keysight B1500A with dual Medium-Power SMUs (MPSMU) in 4-wire Kelvin configuration, precision micro-probing manipulators, gold-plated reference calibration substrate. | 1. Land Kelvin Force+, Sense+, Force-, and Sense- probes on dedicated 180nm tungsten bitline/metal plug Kelvin structure pads. 2. Force current I_force swept from -1.0 mA to +1.0 mA in 50 uA steps. 3. Measure differential voltage drop V_sense across Sense+ and Sense- using high-impedance voltmeter channel (>10^12 Ohms input impedance). 4. Calculate dynamic resistance dV/dI via linear regression across zero crossing. | `Total Kelvin interconnect and plug resistance R_kelvin <= 12.5 Ohm; linearity coefficient R^2 >= 0.9999; thermal EMF offset voltage V_offset <= 15 uV.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Class 100 Nitrile Gloves (Double-gloved), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact-resistant safety glasses, Conductive ESD cleanroom smock and grounded wrist strap, Electrostatic dissipative (ESD) cleanroom shoes
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of IPA skin contact: Flush skin thoroughly with copious running water for at least 15 minutes. In case of eye contact: Irrigate eyes immediately at plumbed eyewash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open. In case of N2 purge asphyxiation hazard: Evacuate victim to fresh air immediately; administer artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing has ceased; notify cleanroom emergency medical services.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Prober chamber must feature dedicated local exhaust ventilation (minimum 100 CFM capture flow) for solvent vapor extraction; automated ambient Oxygen (O2) depletion sensor with audible alarm set at <19.5% O2 in probe testing bay.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA wipes and rinse solvent collected in dedicated solvent waste carboys labeled 'Flammable Solvent Waste - Halogen-Free'; sealed under certified chemical fume hood for third-party licensed hazardous incineration.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade (VLSI / MOS) | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (N2 Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (UHP, Grade 6.0) | `99.9999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `12 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly etched final passivation pad opening (SiO2/Si3N4 stack etched via RIE) with post-ash solvent clean, bare Aluminum-Copper (AlCu 0.5%) metal contact pads free of polymer residues.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: N2-purged, native-oxide passivated pad interface (<1.5 nm native oxide), scratch-free pad metal after micro-probing, sealed in airtight wafer canister.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air Q-time causes ambient atmospheric moisture condensation and airborne organic/halide particle absorption onto unpassivated pad dielectric interfaces, causing surface creepage currents >100 fA that completely destroy sub-fA metrology resolution.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completed layout design, DRC/LVS clean verification, and parametric metrology sign-off for the 180nm 1T1C DRAM sub-fA Kelvin and active-guarded pad array test vehicle. The design isolates pad parasitics to <10 fF and guarantees sub-fA measurement capability (<0.5 fA leakage background) at 85°C across all target storage node leakage metrology channels.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dram_180nm_kelvin_guard_array_v2.gds`
- [ ] `sub_fa_kelvin_array_drc_lvs_clean_report.pdf`
- [ ] `kelvin_guard_leakage_baseline_metrology_matrix.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Open-circuit guarded probe pad background leakage current at 85°C under nominal 1.8V operating bias** | `0.35 fA` | +0.15 fA / -0.20 fA | Keysight B1517A HRSMU 60-second settle time integration on open guarded test structures inside N2-purged probe chamber. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Total Kelvin probe loop series interconnect and contact resistance across 4-terminal tungsten contact array** | `9.2 Ohm` | +/- 2.0 Ohm | 4-wire Kelvin DC sweep (-1 mA to +1 mA) linear extraction via differential sense channels. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Parasitic capacitive coupling between signal force pad and surrounding active guard ring** | `7.5 fF` | +/- 1.5 fF | High-frequency precision multi-frequency LCR meter (Keysight E4980A) measurement at 100 kHz with 50 mV oscillation amplitude. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher exit sign-off requires 100% passing DRC/LVS run without design rule waivers, confirmed open-pad leakage floor strictly <= 0.50 fA across 10 random dies on a 200mm test wafer at 85°C, and peer sign-off from both Circuit Design Lead and Metrology Lead.
