nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Shadow Mask Alignment & Thermal Evaporation of Aluminum Dot Array

**Document ID:** `SOP-FAB-FE-0042`  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > High-K Gate Dielectric & Thin Film Thermal Oxidation Line > Spectroscopic Ellipsometry & MOS C-V Dielectric Metrology > MOS Test Capacitor Array Mask & Shadow Pad Deposition > Shadow Mask Alignment & Thermal Evaporation of Aluminum Dot Array  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Process Workflow Diagram

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Substrate & Shadow   │
│       Mask Prep       │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Fixture Alignment &  │
│       Clamping        │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Vacuum Pumpdown <   │
│       2e-6 Torr       │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Thermal Evaporation  │
│         of Al         │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Cooling & Venting   │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  MOS C-V Metrology &  │
│      Acceptance       │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Concise Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Substrate & Mask Preparation:**
   - Inspect the test wafer carrying the high-k / thermally grown thin oxide layer ($\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ physical thickness).
   - Clean the precision laser-cut molybdenum/beryllium-copper shadow mask in anhydrous isopropyl alcohol (IPA) and dry under filtered $\text{N}_2$.
   - Load high-purity (5N / 99.999%) Aluminum evaporation pellets or wire into the tungsten boat or basket source.

2. **Shadow Mask Alignment & Mechanical Clamping:**
   - Mount the test wafer on the substrate platen in the tooling stage.
   - Align the shadow mask aperture array over designated test capacitor test areas.
   - Secure the mask flush against the dielectric surface with magnetic backing or spring-loaded mechanical clamps to minimize edge penumbra and vapor bleed.

3. **Chamber Load & High-Vacuum Pumpdown:**
   - Transfer the clamped assembly into the thermal evaporator chamber and face downward to the source.
   - Seal the chamber and initiate roughing and high-vacuum turbomolecular/cryopump cycle until chamber base pressure pumps down below $2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$ to prevent oxygen incorporation into the depositing aluminum dots.

4. **Thermal Evaporation:**
   - Pre-condition the Al charge by ramping filament current with the source shutter closed to degas volatile surface species.
   - Open the shutter and adjust source current to deposit aluminum at a calibrated deposition rate of $50\text{ to }100\text{ nm/minute}$ monitored via quartz crystal microbalance (QCM).
   - Terminate deposition once target physical thickness is achieved ($350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$).

5. **Post-Deposition Cool-Down & Vent:**
   - Turn off filament current and allow the substrate and boat to cool down under high vacuum until temperature drops below $100^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Backfill chamber with dry $\text{N}_2$ to atmospheric pressure, unclamp mask, and transfer wafer to wafer cassette for metrology.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value & Tolerance | Physical Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Chamber Base Vacuum Pressure** | $< 2 \times 10^{-6}$ | $\text{Torr}$ | Calibrated Bayard-Alpert ion gauge / vacuum transducer |
| **Al Deposition Rate** | $50\text{ to }100$ | $\text{nm/min}$ | In-situ calibrated Quartz Crystal Microbalance (QCM) |
| **Film Thickness Target** | $350 \pm 5\%$ ($332.5\text{ to }367.5$) | $\text{nm}$ | Stylus profilometry / Spectroscopic ellipsometry |
| **Post-Anneal Sheet Resistance ($R_s$)** | $< 0.08$ | $\Omega/\square$ | Four-point probe (following $400^\circ\text{C}$, 30 min $\text{N}_2/\text{H}_2$ 95/5 anneal) |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **Source:** *Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects*
  - Vacuum chamber base pressure requirement: $< 2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$ to prevent oxygen incorporation.
  - Source purity: $99.999\%$ (5N) Aluminum.
  - Deposition rate: $50\text{ to }100\text{ nm/minute}$.
  - Target thickness: $350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$.
  - Sheet resistance metric: $R_s < 0.08\ \Omega/\square$ after post-metal anneal ($400^\circ\text{C}$ for $30\text{ minutes}$ in forming gas $\text{N}_2/\text{H}_2\ 95/5$).
- **Source:** *Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering*
  - MOS dielectric interface: Thermally grown silicon dioxide ($\text{SiO}_2$) with $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ physical thickness for capacitance metrology benchmarking.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermal evaporation utilizes a point or boat source that generates a divergence angle across large wafers, resulting in non-uniform deposition rates and penumbral shadow effects under stencil masks. Stencil aperture edge-tapering and standoff gap tolerances directly modulate dot edge blurring and effective MOS capacitor area, which cascades into capacitance measurement errors during C-V oxide profiling.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: High-purity 5N Aluminum evaporated from tungsten boats suffers from radiant thermal heat transfer to the wafer, risking micro-cracking or thermal stress in fragile ultra-thin high-k gate dielectrics (Al2O3/HfO2) and native interfacial oxides. Direct mechanical contact of the shadow mask can induce mechanical scratches, pinholes, or particle contamination across sensitive MOS capacitors.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Pre-patterned bimetal (Invar/Ni) or laser-cut molybdenum/silicon shadow masks have constrained availability and wear out through Al build-up over 10-15 runs. Sourcing 99.999% (5N) vacuum-grade aluminum pellets/wire and high-end tungsten evaporation coils requires dual-vendor qualification to avoid cleanroom downtime.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Shadow pad deposition is a critical test vehicle milestone for MOS gate oxide qualification. Cycle time must incorporate stencil alignment tooling, roughing to high-vacuum base pressure (< 2x10^-6 Torr), cool-down intervals, and solvent cleaning of masks without slipping Gen 2 line tape-out schedules.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Penumbral shadow blurring: Mask standoff gap causes diffuse dot perimeters, yielding unpredictable capacitor surface areas and distorted C-V extraction.
1. Mechanical scratch defects and dielectric puncturing: Direct contact friction between rigid shadow mask and high-k thin film generates electrical shorting paths.
1. Thermal radiation-induced gate oxide breakdown: Unshielded tungsten filament boat overheating substrate causes thermal stress fractures in sub-10nm dielectric.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-2-3-1-2-01` | **Aluminum Dot Electrode Thickness & Profilometry Uniformity** | Stylus Profilometer (Bruker Dektak XT or equivalent) and in-situ Quartz Crystal Microbalance (QCM) | 1. Zero QCM monitor and deposit Aluminum dot array targeting nominal 200 nm at a rate of 0.3-0.5 nm/s. 2. Vent chamber with dry N2 after 20-minute cool-down. 3. Unclamp wafer and measure step height across 9 distributed dots (center, inner ring, outer ring) using stylus profilometer across 500 um scan length. | `Nominal dot thickness between 190 nm and 210 nm (200 nm ± 5%); cross-wafer thickness standard deviation < 4.0%.` |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-2-3-1-2-02` | **MOS Dot Edge Definition & Area Fidelity Inspection** | Calibrated Optical Metrology Microscope with digital image analysis (100x-500x magnification) | 1. Position wafer under 200x optical objective. 2. Capture images of 5 representative circular dots (nominal diameter 200 um). 3. Measure maximum orthogonal diameters (D_x, D_y) and inspect penumbral halo transition width using edge-detection intensity profile. | `Effective diameter within 200 um ± 3 um; edge blur/penumbra width < 2.5 um; zero mechanical scratch tracks visible across dielectric perimeter.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloving), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Nomex heat-resistant gloves for hot filament/boat servicing, N95 particulate respirator during chamber vacuum wall flaking/pumping cleaning
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with hot fixtures: Immediately drench affected area with cold water for at least 15 minutes; seek medical attention for thermal burns. Inhalation of metal particulates during chamber maintenance: Move victim to fresh air; administer oxygen if breathing is difficult. Eye contact with solvent: Flush eyes at eyewash station for minimum 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: High-vacuum turbomolecular/roughing pump backing lines vented directly to dedicated acid/solvent building exhaust scrubber line; chamber maintenance performed under laminar flow bench with local extraction snorkel.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent tungsten boats and peeled aluminum flakes segregated into dry hazardous heavy metal disposal drums; spent solvent collected in labeled flammable solvent waste receptacles per RCRA regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Aluminum (elemental vacuum source pellets)** | `7429-90-5` | 5N (99.999% trace metals basis) | `100%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (mask cleaning / degreasing)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic / VLSI grade | `>99.8%` |
| **Nitrogen (venting and purge gas)** | `7727-37-9` | UHP Grade 5.0 | `>99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly deposited and post-deposition annealed high-k / SiO2 gate dielectric surface, chemically degreased, dry, and particle-free (< 5 particles > 0.3 um).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Patterned Al dot electrode array on dielectric substrate; back-side metallized or ready for forming gas anneal (FGA) in N2/H2.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture adsorption and airborne hydrocarbon condensation on bare high-k oxide causing interfacial dipoles, degraded fixed charge density (Q_f), and high leakage current / hysteresis on subsequent C-V metrology.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful shadow-mask-aligned thermal evaporation of a 200 nm pure Aluminum dot array for MOS capacitor test structures with sharp edge definition, minimal penumbral blur, and verified dielectric integrity.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `al_dot_array_profilometry_map.csv`
- [ ] `mos_shadow_mask_optical_inspection_report.pdf`
- [ ] `dot_electrode_sem_edge_profile.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Aluminum film thickness at center and outer wafer radius** | `200 nm` | ±10 nm (±5%) | Stylus Profilometer (Dektak XT) 9-point surface scan |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Electrode pad diameter fidelity against nominal shadow mask aperture** | `200.0 um` | ±3.0 um | Calibrated optical microscope digital edge threshold analysis |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Shadow mask penumbral edge blur width** | `< 1.5 um` | +1.0 um max threshold | Optical line scan optical density transition distance (10% to 90% opacity) |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 9 profilometer sites verify thickness within 190-210 nm, optical microscopy confirms penumbral halo < 2.5 um with zero perimeter scratch damage, and test wafer passes initial probe continuity check for subsequent C-V characterization.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Capacitor Area Profilometry & Post-Deposition Forming Gas Anneal

- **Document ID:** `SOP-FAB-FE-CAP-042`
- **Revision:** 2.0 (Gen 2 µm / 180nm Baseline)
- **Hierarchy:** High-K Gate Dielectric & Thin Film Thermal Oxidation Line > MOS Test Capacitor Array Mask & Shadow Pad Deposition > Metrology & Thermal Processing
- **Owner:** DRAM Foundation VN Multi-Agent Council (Domain Expert AI)

---

### 1. Process Overview & Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Clean Surface & Load  │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Stylus Profilometry   │
│      Step Height       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Area & Pad Dimension  │
│      Verification      │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Load into Quartz    │
│        Furnace         │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Forming Gas Anneal   │
│    400°C-450°C N2/H2   │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Cooldown & MOS C-V   │
│       Inspection       │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

#### Step 1: Substrate Preparation & Vacuum Stage Loading
1. Verify front-side MOS test capacitor array shadow pads (deposited over $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ / $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$ / ONO or thin dielectric stacks) are free of organic residue and particulate contamination.
2. Transfer wafer via vacuum wand onto the automated mechanical stylus profilometer vacuum chuck.

#### Step 2: Contact Stylus Profilometry & Area Metrology
1. Align the optical crosshair to the perimeter edge of the shadow-evaporated/sputtered metal top electrode pad.
2. Program a scan length across the boundary step height:
   - **Stylus Force:** $1.0\text{ to }3.0\text{ mg}$ to avoid soft-metal gouging.
   - **Scan Speed:** $5\text{ to }10\ \mu\text{m/s}$ across the transition boundary.
3. Extract physical electrode step thickness and pad diameter/edge dimensions across 5 die sites (Center, North, South, East, West).
4. Compute effective capacitor geometric area ($A_{\text{eff}}$) for subsequent area-normalized dielectric parameterization ($\text{fF}/\mu\text{m}^2$).

#### Step 3: Atmosphere Purge & Furnace Loading
1. Transfer profilometry-verified wafers into a horizontal atmospheric quartz diffusion/anneal tube furnace.
2. Initiate high-purity Nitrogen ($\text{N}_2$, $99.999\%$) pre-purge at $10\text{ to }15\text{ SLM}$ for 15 minutes to reduce ambient $\text{O}_2$ below $5\text{ ppm}$.

#### Step 4: Post-Deposition Forming Gas Anneal (FGA)
1. Switch gas flow to forming gas mixture ($90\text{–}95\%\ \text{N}_2\ /\ 5\text{–}10\%\ \text{H}_2$).
2. Ramp furnace temperature to the standard metallization contact passivation window of **$400^\circ\text{C}\text{ to }450^\circ\text{C}$** at $5^\circ\text{C/min}$.
3. Dwell at **$400^\circ\text{C}\text{ to }450^\circ\text{C}$** for **$30\text{ minutes}$** under forming gas ambient to passivate interface trap density ($D_{\text{it}}$) at the semiconductor/dielectric boundary and sinter contact interfaces.

#### Step 5: Post-Anneal Cooldown & Handoff to MOS C-V
1. Switch gas manifold back to pure $\text{N}_2$ flush; ramp down temperature below $150^\circ\text{C}$ prior to tube boat pull.
2. Unload wafer to dry nitrogen cooling cassette for handoff to MOS C-V and dielectric leakage metrology.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Operational Target Metric | Physical Units | Tolerance / Limits |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Profilometer Scan Repeatability** | $1\sigma \le 0.5$ | $\text{nm}$ | Step height reproducibility on 5 reference points |
| **Capacitor Pad Lateral Dimension** | Per target pad mask diameter | $\mu\text{m}$ | $\pm 1.0\ \mu\text{m}$ across $5$-point wafer map |
| **Forming Gas Anneal Temperature** | $400\text{ to }450$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | $\pm 2.0\ ^\circ\text{C}$ furnace flat-zone stability |
| **Equivalent Cell Capacitance Target** | $\ge 25\text{ to }30$ (scaled cell reference) | $\text{fF/cell}$ | Minimum $28\ \text{fF/cell}$ budget for retention $> 64\ \text{ms}$ |
| **Capacitor Dielectric Leakage** | $\le 1.0$ (cell-normalized @ $85^\circ\text{C}$) | $\text{fA/cell}$ | At nominal operating voltage condition |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Source Citations

- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - Minimum capacitance budget of $\ge 28\ \text{fF/cell}$ to maintain signal margin and noise immunity against bitline coupling.
  - Leakage current target $\le 1\ \text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
  - Storage dielectric options: $\text{ONO}$, $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$, and $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ high-k stacks ($\kappa > 15$).
- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**
  - Storage capacitor retention requirement: $25\text{ to }30\ \text{fF/cell}$ for retention time $> 64\ \text{ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
  - Equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) window: $3\text{ to }4\ \text{nm}$.
- **Source: Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks**
  - Refractive index standard $n = 2.00 \pm 0.02$ at $632.8\ \text{nm}$ for stoichiometric dielectric $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ layers.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Combining mechanical/optical stylus profilometry with high-temperature forming gas anneal (FGA) requires rigid sequencing and strict contamination isolation. Profilometer contact must avoid gouging soft aluminum/polysilicon test pads, which would generate metallic particulate excursions into the clean quartz diffusion tube. Furthermore, the quartz furnace PID loop must maintain ±0.5°C across the central 350 mm flat zone under a 2 to 5 SLPM laminar gas flow to ensure uniform interface state passivation across the entire 150mm/200mm wafer load.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Post-metal or post-dielectric forming gas anneal (typically 5% H2 in 95% N2 at 400°C–450°C) is critical to passivate Si/SiO2 or high-k interfacial dangling bonds (Pb centers), driving Dit below 1e10 eV^-1 cm^-2. However, executing stylus profilometry prior to anneal risks organic cross-contamination and micro-scratching. If profilometry is performed post-anneal, thermal-induced metal hillocks or reflow will alter step-height measurements, causing inaccurate effective capacitor area extraction during MOS C-V metrology.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: High-purity forming gas (5% H2 / 95% N2, 99.999% semiconductor grade) cylinders require certified CGA 350 connections, automated safety interlocks, and specialized orbital-welded 316L VIM/VAR delivery manifolds. Quartz process tubes and calibrated diamond-tip styli have 12-16 week replacement lead times, representing acute supply-chain risks for continuous fab operation.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scheduling profilometry and FGA requires clear stage-gate definitions. Running physical contact metrology on active die regions can degrade yield; non-destructive optical profilometry on peripheral scribe-line test pads should be enforced. Strict Q-time tracking must prevent Native Oxide and moisture regrowth prior to the FGA step, holding the overall cycle time per lot within a 4-hour window.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Profilometer diamond stylus penetration or shear tearing through thin metal/dielectric stacks causing micro-particulate shedding and contamination inside the furnace quartz tube.
1. Incomplete N2 purge or air back-diffusion during forming gas anneal leading to hydrogen oxidation, exothermic flash, or incomplete passivation of Si/SiO2 interface traps (Dit > 5e10 eV^-1 cm^-2).
1. Wafer boat insertion/withdrawal exceeding 50 mm/min mechanical speed limit, inducing thermal gradient shock and crystallographic slip dislocations across the silicon substrate.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-2-3-1-3-01` | **Capacitor Pad Step-Height & Area Profilometry Verification** | Calibrated Contact Stylus Profilometer (e.g., KLA Tencor Alpha-Step D-600) with 2 µm diamond stylus and Optical Confocal Interferometer | 1. Load wafer onto stage and align scribe-line MOS capacitor test arrays (100 µm x 100 µm and 200 µm x 200 µm pads). 2. Perform 500 µm line scans across 5 orthogonal sites (Center, North, South, East, West) across pad edges at 10 µm/s scan speed. 3. Extract step height (Z-profile) and calculate pad lateral dimensions (X, Y) via edge-detection threshold (50% height marker). 4. Compute effective capacitor electrode area A_eff and surface roughness Ra on top metal/dielectric layers. | `Pad lateral dimension deviation <= ±0.5% of nominal design mask area; Step height uniformity across wafer <= ±2.5 nm (3-sigma); Top electrode surface roughness Ra < 1.2 nm; No mechanical stylus gouging or dielectric breakthrough.` |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-2-3-1-3-02` | **Three-Zone Furnace Forming Gas Anneal (FGA) Interface Passivation** | Three-Zone Horizontal Quartz Diffusion Furnace with digital triple-loop PID controller, Type-R thermocouples, calibrated H2/N2 mass flow controller (MFC), and MOS C-V Prober (4192A / Keithley 4200-SCS) | 1. Transfer wafer boat into furnace at mechanical ramp rate of <= 35 mm/min under 3.0 SLPM laminar N2 flow. 2. Switch gas delivery to pre-mixed Forming Gas (5% H2 / 95% N2) at 4.0 SLPM laminar sweep; maintain isothermal 425°C soak for 30 minutes. 3. Transition gas delivery back to pure N2 sweep (5.0 SLPM) and initiate controlled cooling cycle. 4. Mechanically retract wafer boat at <= 35 mm/min to room temperature load station. 5. Transfer wafers to MOS C-V probe station and measure high-frequency/quasi-static C-V curves to calculate interface trap density Dit. | `Interface trap density Dit <= 1.0e10 eV^-1 cm^-2 near midgap; flatband voltage shift Delta-Vfb <= ±30 mV across 5 wafer sites; zero thermal slip line dislocations visible under Nomarski microscopy.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom chemical splash goggles / full face shield, Thermal heat-resistant Nomex/Kevlar furnace safety gloves (rated >= 500°C), ESD-safe cleanroom nitrile gloves under-layer, Flame-retardant cleanroom bunny suit and safety shoes
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Inhalation: Immediately remove victim from exposure area to fresh air; administer oxygen if breathing is labored; seek emergency medical evaluation. Thermal Burns: Flush affected skin immediately with copious cold deionized water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply oily ointments; cover with sterile dressing and transport to medical care.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous toxic/flammable gas monitoring with lower explosive limit (LEL) sensors calibrated for H2 (< 10% LEL trigger threshold); dedicated process exhaust plenum maintaining minimum negative static pressure of -0.5 in. w.g. with dedicated burn box or scrubber interlock.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Furnace exhaust effluent routed through an active thermal burn box / wet dynamic scrubber to oxidize trace hydrogen and cool exhaust gases prior to atmospheric discharge; spent cleaning wipes bagged in sealed hazardous waste drums.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrogen (in Forming Gas mix)** | `1333-74-0` | Semiconductor Grade (99.999% base pure) | `5% v/v balance N2` |
| **Nitrogen (Carrier / Purge Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (UHP 99.9999%) | `95% v/v in FGA mix, 100% in purge` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA - Stage Wipe)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly etched/lifted-off metal contact pads and clean dielectric surface free of organic residues and moisture, stored in desiccated container.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Passivated, hydrogen-terminated interface state (Dit < 1e10 eV^-1 cm^-2), annealed metal/dielectric stack, zero organic residue, dry wafer surface.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air Q-time causes uncontrolled moisture chemisorption, native oxide formation on metal pad interfaces, and airborne hydrocarbon contamination, inducing ohmic contact degradation, erratic C-V hysteresis, and thermal blister defects during subsequent FGA.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful dimensional qualification of DRAM test capacitor pads via micro-profilometry and passivation of interfacial defect states via 3-zone quartz tube forming gas annealing at 425°C.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `cap_pad_area_profilometry_report_lotA.csv`
- [ ] `furnace_fga_thermal_gasflow_log_run425.pdf`
- [ ] `mos_cv_interface_trap_density_dit_analysis.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Average capacitor electrode area matches nominal mask geometry with minimal edge taper deviation** | `40000.0` | ± 200.0 µm^2 | High-resolution stylus profilometry edge-detection boundary integration across 200µm x 200µm test structures |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Interface trap state density (Dit) at midgap after forming gas anneal** | `8.0e9` | <= 1.0e10 eV^-1 cm^-2 | High-frequency (1 MHz) and quasi-static MOS C-V extraction via Terman/Castagne method |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Furnace center flat-zone temperature uniformity during 425°C soak** | `425.0` | ± 0.5 °C | In-situ triple Type-R profiling thermocouples integrated into quartz tube PID controller |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Profilometry verification confirms MOS capacitor pad area within ±0.5% of design spec without stylus scratch damage; furnace FGA run achieves Dit <= 1.0e10 eV^-1 cm^-2 across all measured test sites with no slip dislocations and zero process interlock alarms.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Multi-Angle Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Film Thickness Calibration

**Task Title:** Multi-Angle Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Film Thickness Calibration  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > High-K Gate Dielectric & Thin Film Thermal Oxidation Line [Front-End Fabrication] > Spectroscopic Ellipsometry & MOS C-V Dielectric Metrology [Metrology] > Multi-Angle Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Film Thickness Calibration [Metrology]  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type:** Make  
**Role:** Domain Expert AI, DRAM Foundation VN Multi-Agent Council  

---

### Process Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Start: Wafer Loading  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Goniometer & Laser   │
│      Calibration       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Multi-Angle Spectral  │
│      Acquisition       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Cauchy/Sellmeier    │
│     Model Fitting      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│       Acceptance       │
│   Validation & Wafer   │
│        Mapping         │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Substrate Pre-Alignment & Stage Loading:**
   - Transfer the thermal gate oxide or capacitor dielectric wafer onto the vacuum chuck of the spectroscopic ellipsometer.
   - Engage vacuum hold and execute automatic notch/flat optical centering.

2. **Goniometer Initialization & Optical Beam Alignment:**
   - Calibrate the goniometer zero angle and reference detector alignment using the clean reference silicon substrate.
   - Configure the source beam through the polarizer-compensator optical train to verify beam intensity across the ultraviolet-visible-near infrared spectrum.

3. **Multi-Angle Spectral Acquisition ($\Psi, \Delta$):**
   - Direct the polarized beam onto the sample across designated incident angles (e.g., $65^\circ, 70^\circ, 75^\circ$ around the Brewster angle of silicon).
   - Record the polarization change angles $\Psi(\lambda)$ and $\Delta(\lambda)$ according to the fundamental ellipsometric ratio:
     $$\rho = \frac{r_p}{r_s} = \tan(\Psi) \cdot \exp(i\Delta)$$
     where $r_p$ and $r_s$ denote the complex Fresnel reflection coefficients.

4. **Dispersion Modeling & Layer Inversion:**
   - Apply a validated optical dispersion model:
     - Use a **Cauchy dispersion model** or **Sellmeier dispersion model** to parameterize refractive index $n(\lambda)$ and extinction coefficient $k(\lambda)$ for transparent thin dielectrics ($\text{SiO}_2$, $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$).
   - Fit layer physical thickness ($t$) and optical constants against acquired $(\Psi, \Delta)$ spectra via Levenberg-Marquardt regression minimization ($\text{MSE} \to \min$).

5. **Wafer Non-Uniformity Mapping:**
   - Execute an automated **9-point** or **49-point wafer map** across concentric radial coordinates to characterize radial film non-uniformity across spin coating or furnace dry oxidation runs.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Targets

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Physical Unit | Tolerance / Boundary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Dry Gate Oxide Physical Thickness ($t_{\text{ox}}$)** | `3.5` | `nm` | `±0.05 nm` (sub-Angstrom precision) |
| **Photoresist Layer Thickness ($t_{\text{PR}}$)** | `1.3` | `µm` | `±2 nm` |
| **Automated Wafer Mapping Grid Density** | `9` or `49` | `points/wafer` | Exact grid point match |
| **Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) for Stacked Cap Dielectric** | `3 to 4` | `nm` | Target window for 180nm cell retention |

---

### 3. Literature Citations & Traceability

1. **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology:**
   - *Physical Principle & Equation:* $\rho = r_p / r_s = \tan(\Psi) \cdot \exp(i\Delta)$ using Fresnel reflection coefficients.
   - *Modeling:* Cauchy and Sellmeier dispersion models for $n(\lambda)$ and $k(\lambda)$.
   - *Measurement Precision & Targets:* Dry gate oxide target of $3.5\text{ nm}$ with $\pm0.05\text{ nm}$ precision; photoresist layer at $1.3\text{ \mu m}$ with $\pm2\text{ nm}$ precision.
   - *Mapping:* Automated 9-point and 49-point wafer mapping protocols tracking radial furnace and spin coating non-uniformity.
2. **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering:**
   - *Dielectric Thickness Context:* Gate dielectric thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$ dry oxidation with $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ physical thickness; stacked capacitor high-$k$ dielectric equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) around $3\text{ to }4\text{ nm}$.
3. **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:**
   - *Stack Integration:* Stacked capacitor dielectric layer baseline (ONO / $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$ / $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ high-$k$ stack with effective dielectric constant $\kappa > 15$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automated Multi-Angle Spectroscopic Ellipsometry (VASE/MASE) integration into the 180nm DRAM gate line must reconcile spot-size footprint (typically 200 µm to 1 mm without micro-focus optics) against dedicated in-die scribe line test pads (minimum 80 µm x 80 µm). Furthermore, high-throughput wafer transfer requires automated SECS/GEM interface mapping to correlate 49-point thickness and refractive index variations directly with furnace thermal gradients and downstream dry-etch bias drift.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For ultra-thin gate oxides (~3.5 nm to 6.0 nm in 180nm peripheral/array transistors) and high-k capacitor stacks, multi-angle acquisition (65°, 70°, 75° near the Brewster angle of silicon ~75.6° at 632.8 nm) is essential to de-correlate optical thickness (t) from refractive index (n). Using a single Cauchy dispersion model on sub-4 nm films introduces parameter correlation instabilities; an explicit Si/SiO2 transition interfacial layer (0.3–0.5 nm sub-oxide) and fixed substrate optical constants (ex-situ calibrated Si substrate) must be parameterized to prevent 0.2 nm systematic thickness offsets.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procurement of a refurbished dual-source Xe/He-Ne multi-angle spectroscopic ellipsometer requires strict auditing of optical goniometer mechanical backlash (<0.005° angular accuracy), replacement availability of certified NIST-traceable 100 mm/150 mm SiO2/Si calibration reference standards, and long-term supply agreements for D2/Xenon arc lamps with guaranteed spectral stability down to 193 nm DUV.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Tool commissioning and recipe qualification must freeze within a 3-week window to avoid holding up the gate dielectric furnace runs. Scribe-line metrology target layouts must be locked prior to reticle tape-out, and daily automated tool matching across 3 standard wafer thicknesses (2 nm, 25 nm, 100 nm) must demonstrate gauge repeatability and reproducibility (GR&R) < 10% before greenlighting active lot measurement.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Parameter correlation failure in the regression solver between dielectric constant (n) and physical thickness (t) for films under 5 nm, yielding non-physical n values (>1.65 for SiO2) and skewed thickness outputs.
1. Goniometer stage angular miscalibration leading to systematic incidence angle offsets (>0.05°), causing severe distortion in Brewster angle Delta-inversion and high Mean Squared Error (MSE > 2.5).
1. Surface hydrocarbon and airborne moisture condensation due to broken Q-time post-oxidation, adding 0.3–0.8 nm of fictitious organic thickness to the gate dielectric model.

Fit measured Psi and Delta spectra using standard Levenberg-Marquardt regression against calibrated Si-SiO2 Cauchy model. 5. | `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-2-3-2-02` | **Automated 49-Point Dielectric Wafer Uniformity and Refractive Index Profiling** | Automated Multi-Angle Spectroscopic Ellipsometer with 150mm R-Theta vacuum stage, vacuum-coupled micro-spot optics (100 µm), NIST 100 nm thermal SiO2/Si control wafer | 1. ### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloving required), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV laser/arc-lamp safety glasses (OD > 4 at 193-400 nm), Cleanroom ESD-safe anti-static gown, hood, and conductive booties
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin/eye contact with cleaning IPA: Flush eyes or skin immediately with sterile cleanroom eyewash/water for at least 15 minutes; seek medical attention if irritation persists. For high-intensity UV exposure: Evacuate beam area immediately, cover eyes, and consult an ophthalmologist for potential photokeratitis evaluation. In case of inert N2 gas asphyxiation: Relocate victim immediately to fresh air, administer artificial oxygen if qualified, and summon emergency medical services.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous tool chassis negative-pressure exhaust ducting at >= 50 SCFM to evacuate ozone generated by broadband DUV Xenon/Deuterium sources; room-level continuous oxygen deficiency monitoring (alarm threshold < 19.5% O2) in metrology bay.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA wipes and lens tissue must be collected in closed, grounded, flame-retardant cleanroom solvent disposal bins and routed to the site organic solvent waste stream; spent Deuterium/Xenon arc lamps must be de-pressurized per hazardous metal/glass disposal protocols.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) for optics and stage wipe down** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Electronic Grade (>99.99%) | `100%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (N2 purge gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity Grade 6.0 (99.9999%) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly grown thermal oxide or high-k dielectric layer post-furnace/ALD, free of organic contamination, particulate count < 10 at 0.18 µm.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Optically characterized, non-destructively inspected dielectric surface with zero beam-induced carbon deposition, ready for immediate gate polysilicon deposition.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding Q-time induces adventitious airborne molecular contamination (AMC) and moisture adsorption, resulting in artificial 0.4–0.9 nm thickness overestimation and uncorrectable drift in downstream gate polysilicon dry-etch endpoint timing.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Multi-Angle Spectroscopic Ellipsometry tool fully calibrated and qualified for 180nm DRAM ultra-thin gate dielectric (<5 nm) and cell storage oxide/nitride/oxide stacks, achieving sub-Angstrom measurement precision, robust optical dispersion parameter extraction, and SECS/GEM wafer map correlation.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `MASE_GateOxide_Calibration_Report_Gen2.pdf`
- [ ] `Wafer_Uniformity_49Pt_Thickness_Map.csv`
- [ ] `NIST_Traceable_Dispersion_Model_Verification.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Static measurement 1-sigma repeatability on sub-5nm gate oxide reference** | `0.015` | +0.005 nm / -0.015 nm | 30 consecutive spectral acquisitions on stationary NIST 3.5 nm standard without unclamp |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Refractive index extraction accuracy on 100nm calibration standard at 632.8nm** | `1.4570` | ±0.0025 | Cauchy dispersion parameter extraction across 65°, 70°, and 75° angles fitted against NIST reference table |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Tool-to-tool optical dispersion model Goodness-of-Fit Mean Squared Error (MSE)** | `1.00` | <= 1.50 maximum | Levenberg-Marquardt non-linear regression analysis output calculated across 250 nm - 850 nm spectrum |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Successful 30-cycle repeatability demonstrating 1-sigma <= 0.03 nm, Mean Squared Error <= 1.20 on certified 3.5 nm oxide standards, zero unresolvable parameter correlation between n and t, and formal sign-off approval by Metrology Domain Expert and Quality Lead.

### Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
**Title:** High-Frequency Quasi-Static MOS C-V Profiling & EOT Extraction  
**Node:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN) — Front-End Metrology Line  
**Document Link:** [docs/sop_hf_qs_mos_cv_profiling_eot.md](docs/sop_hf_qs_mos_cv_profiling_eot.md)

---

#### 1. Workflow Architecture & Sequence

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Start: MOSCAP Wafer   │
│        Loading         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Backside Ohmic     │
│     Contact Check      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   HF 1 MHz C-V Sweep   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Quasi-Static C-V    │
│          Ramp          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Cox Saturation & EOT  │
│       Extraction       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Acceptance Gate     │
│        Decision        │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

#### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Test Vehicle Mounting & Backside Ohmic Verification**:
   - Secure the P-type (100) Si test wafer onto the probe station gold-plated vacuum chuck inside a dark, shielded Faraday box.
   - Verify low-resistance substrate grounding through the backside Gold (Au) or Aluminum (Al) contact layer.
   - Position micro-probes on clean Aluminum top gate dots ($200\ \mu\text{m}$, $500\ \mu\text{m}$, or $1000\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter) sputtered through shadow masks over the oxide layer ($3.5\text{ nm}$ to $25\text{ nm}$).

2. **High-Frequency (1 MHz) C-V Profiling**:
   - Apply a small AC probing signal: $f = 1\text{ MHz}$, $v_{ac} = 20\text{ mV RMS}$.
   - Sweep DC bias from inversion ($V_G > V_T$) into accumulation ($V_G < V_{fb}$ for P-type substrate, e.g., $+2.0\text{ V} \rightarrow -2.5\text{ V}$).
   - Record capacitance saturation in strong accumulation ($C_{max} = C_{ox} = \frac{\varepsilon_{ox}\varepsilon_0\text{Area}}{t_{ox}}$) and verify that HF capacitance does not recover in inversion due to minority carrier generation limitations.

3. **Quasi-Static (QS) Inversion & Interface Profiling**:
   - Transition instrumentation to quasi-static electrometer mode ($dV/dt = 20\text{ mV/s}$).
   - Ramp gate voltage across the same potential span in light-tight equilibrium conditions to measure displacement current:
     $$I_{QS}(V_G) = C_{QS}(V_G) \cdot \frac{dV_G}{dt}$$
   - Verify low-frequency recovery where $C_{QS}$ returns to $C_{ox}$ in strong inversion ($V_G > V_T$).

4. **Physical Thickness & EOT Extraction**:
   - Determine $C_{ox}$ from the plateau of the HF accumulation trace at strong negative bias.
   - Extract Equivalent Oxide Thickness using:
     $$\text{EOT} = \frac{\varepsilon_{SiO2} \cdot \varepsilon_0 \cdot \pi (d/2)^2}{C_{ox}}$$
     where $\varepsilon_{SiO2} = 3.9$, $\varepsilon_0 = 8.854 \times 10^{-14}\text{ F/cm}$, and $d \in \{200, 500, 1000\}\ \mu\text{m}$.

---

#### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                        Target Acceptance Limits        
                 ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
                 │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
Min Cap (fF/cell)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
  EOT High-k (nm)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒                               │
                 │▒▒▒▒▒▒                               │
 EOT Gate Ox (nm)┤██████                               │
                 │██████                               │
                 └┬────────┬────────┬────────┬────────┬┘
                  0        7       14       21       28 
```

1. **Gate Dielectric Physical/EOT Thickness**: $\mathbf{3.5 \pm 0.1\text{ nm}}$ (thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ measured via HF $1\text{ MHz}$ $C_{ox}$ saturation).
2. **High-k Stack Capacitor EOT**: $\mathbf{3.0\text{ to }4.0\text{ nm}}$ ($\kappa > 15$ with $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5 / \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ or $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$/ONO stacks).
3. **Storage Cell Capacitance Budget**: $\mathbf{\ge 28\text{ fF/cell}}$ (acceptable cell window $25\text{ to }30\text{ fF/cell}$ to preserve data retention $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).
4. **Leakage Current Ceiling**: $\mathbf{< 1\text{ fA/cell}}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ (sub-threshold and junction limit).

---

#### 4. Context Literature Citations
- **Source: Stage 2 Reality Gate: Planar MOS Capacitor C-V Profiling & Dit Extraction**:
  - Test structure geometry: circular Al gate dots ($200\ \mu\text{m}, 500\ \mu\text{m}, 1000\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter) on P-type (100) Si; Au or Al backside substrate ohmic contact; $1\text{ MHz}$ accumulation saturation $C_{ox} = (\varepsilon_{ox}\varepsilon_0\text{Area})/t_{ox}$ resolving $t_{ox}$ with $\pm 0.1\text{ nm}$ precision; QS inversion recovery vs HF minimum.
- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**:
  - Gate oxide dry thermal oxidation target of $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$; high-k dielectric stack EOT target of $3\text{ to }4\text{ nm}$; cell storage capacitance target range of $25\text{ to }30\text{ fF/cell}$ for $> 64\text{ ms}$ retention at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - Minimum capacitance floor of $28\text{ fF/cell}$; high-k dielectric effective constant $\kappa > 15$; sub-threshold and junction leakage target $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Dual-frequency C-V extraction must couple high-frequency (1 MHz) and quasi-static (or low-frequency 10 Hz - 1 kHz) sweeps on the same physical MOSCAP pad to ensure accurate EOT and interface trap density (Dit) mapping without parasitic series resistance (Rs) distortion. Cable inductances and coaxial probe parasitics at 1 MHz must be compensated using open/short/load calibration at the probe tip plane; otherwise, measured accumulation capacitance will artificially depress, skewing calculated EOT thinner than physical reality.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Accurate equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) extraction requires quantum-mechanical correction (Hauser C-V model or NCSU CVC simulator) rather than naive classical parallel-plate Cox = eps_ox * eps_0 * A / t_ox. In accumulation on P-type Si, quantum confinement pushes the peak hole density ~0.3-0.5 nm away from the Si/SiO2 interface, which adds an apparent inversion/accumulation capacitance in series and causes classical extraction to overestimate physical EOT by 0.3-0.4 nm for thin dielectric regimes.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Shadow mask fabrication for 200 um, 500 um, and 1000 um circular Al dots must utilize laser-cut beryllium-copper or stainless steel foils with tighter than +/- 2 um edge burr tolerance. Variations in dot diameter directly propagate into gate area error delta-A/A, which linearly corrupts extracted Cox, EOT, and substrate doping density calculations across wafer lots.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: MOSCAP metrology is the primary gatekeeper for the Stage 2 to Stage 3 reality transition. Cycle time per 6-inch wafer must not exceed 45 minutes for a 9-site die map (high-frequency + quasi-static sweeps). Delays in post-metallization forming gas anneal (FGA) queue time degrade Dit baseline consistency, creating false yield drop alarms in DRAM cell access transistor validation.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Series resistance (Rs) roll-off at 1 MHz causing accumulation capacitance attenuation and catastrophic EOT overestimation.
1. Backside substrate ohmic contact degradation (native oxide regrowth or incomplete Al/Au sintering) producing an artificial double-diode C-V distortion.
1. Excessive quasi-static leakage current (I_gate > 10 pA) causing baseline integrator drift and invalidation of the high-low frequency Dit extraction.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-2-3-3-01` | **High-Frequency (1 MHz) Multi-Area MOSCAP Accumulation Capacitance and EOT Extraction** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer with B1520A Multi-Frequency C-V Unit (MFCMU), Cascade Microtech Summit 12000 semi-automatic shielded probe station, dark box with triaxial guarding. | 1. - **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloving), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses, Static-dissipative ESD lab coat and ESD heel straps
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Flush with sterile eyewash station for 15 minutes. Inhalation: Move subject to fresh air immediately. Skin contact: Wash affected area with mild detergent and water, discard contaminated PPE. Electrical shock hazard: Ensure emergency master power kill switch on prober station is engaged prior to touching prober frame if anomalous high voltage occurs.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Probe station located under laminar flow hood (Class 100 / ISO 5) with exhaust velocity 0.45 m/s +/- 0.05 m/s. Dedicated chemical bench exhaust for solvent cleaning swabs with face velocity >= 100 FPM (0.51 m/s).

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-forming gas annealed Al gate dots with hydrophobic backside contact; free from particulate debris (> 0.3 um zero particle count on test sites).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Punctured/probed Al dot pads with witness scrub marks < 15 um; wafer stored in purged N2 FOUP/desiccator prior to discrete transistor test integration.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture and organic airborne molecular contamination (AMC) adsorption onto gate edges and bare unpassivated field regions creates surface conductance channels and alters Dit by > 5.0e10 eV^-1 cm^-2.

critics.systems_engineer: Dual-frequency C-V extraction must couple high-frequency (1 MHz) and quasi-static (or low-frequency 10 Hz - 1 kHz) sweeps on the same physical MOSCAP pad to ensure accurate EOT and interface trap density (Dit) mapping without parasitic series resistance (Rs) distortion. Cable inductances and coaxial probe parasitics at 1 MHz must be compensated using open/short/load calibration at the probe tip plane; otherwise, measured accumulation capacitance will artificially depress, skewing calculated EOT thinner than physical reality.
critics.domain_expert: Accurate equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) extraction requires quantum-mechanical correction (Hauser C-V model or NCSU CVC simulator) rather than naive classical parallel-plate Cox = eps_ox * eps_0 * A / t_ox. In accumulation on P-type Si, quantum confinement pushes the peak hole density ~0.3-0.5 nm away from the Si/SiO2 interface, which adds an apparent inversion/accumulation capacitance in series and causes classical extraction to overestimate physical EOT by 0.3-0.4 nm for thin dielectric regimes.
critics.supply_chain: Shadow mask fabrication for 200 um, 500 um, and 1000 um circular Al dots must utilize laser-cut beryllium-copper or stainless steel foils with tighter than +/- 2 um edge burr tolerance. Variations in dot diameter directly propagate into gate area error delta-A/A, which linearly corrupts extracted Cox, EOT, and substrate doping density calculations across wafer lots.
critics.laya_pm: MOSCAP metrology is the primary gatekeeper for the Stage 2 to Stage 3 reality transition. Cycle time per 6-inch wafer must not exceed 45 minutes for a 9-site die map (high-frequency + quasi-static sweeps). Delays in post-metallization forming gas anneal (FGA) queue time degrade Dit baseline consistency, creating false yield drop alarms in DRAM cell access transistor validation.
critical_failure_modes: Series resistance (Rs) roll-off at 1 MHz causing accumulation capacitance attenuation and catastrophic EOT overestimation.
Backside substrate ohmic contact degradation (native oxide regrowth or incomplete Al/Au sintering) producing an artificial double-diode C-V distortion.
Excessive quasi-static leakage current (I_gate > 10 pA) causing baseline integrator drift and invalidation of the high-low frequency Dit extraction.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

**Title:** MOS Dot-Capacitor Test Structure Back-Contact Preparation & Probe Station Setup  
**Module:** Metrology / High-Frequency Quasi-Static MOS C-V Profiling & EOT Extraction  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > High-K Gate Dielectric & Thin Film Thermal Oxidation Line > Spectroscopic Ellipsometry & MOS C-V Dielectric Metrology > High-Frequency Quasi-Static MOS C-V Profiling & EOT Extraction > MOS Dot-Capacitor Test Structure Back-Contact Preparation & Probe Station Setup  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type:** Make  

---

### Process Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Backside Native     │
│     Oxide Strip 1      │
│       percent HF       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Backside Ohmic     │
│  Metallization 200nm   │
│       Al or GaIn       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Chuck Vacuum Mount &  │
│   Shielded Probe Box   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Microchamber Purge   │
│   N2 & Triaxial Dark   │
│         Setup          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Substrate Ohmic     │
│  Grounding & Top Dot   │
│        Landing         │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Backside Native Oxide Removal & De-glaze:**
   - Protect the top wafer surface containing the MOS dot capacitors (with ~3.5 nm thermally grown SiO₂ gate dielectric or 3 to 4 nm EOT high-k Ta₂O₅/Al₂O₃ / ONO dielectric dots) using a frontside spin-coat layer of protective photoresist.
   - Dip/swab the wafer backside in dilute HF (1% to 2% aqueous solution) for 30 s to strip native oxide until the silicon surface becomes completely hydrophobic.
   - DI water rinse and blow dry with ultra-pure filtered $N_2$.

2. **Back-Contact Ohmic Formation:**
   - For rapid bench metrology: Apply a uniform scratch/rub coat of high-purity Gallium-Indium (Ga-In) eutectic paste directly onto the bare Si backside to establish a degenerate, low-resistance ohmic contact.
   - For standard fabrication lots: Deposit a 200 nm Aluminum (Al) back-contact metallization layer via physical vapor deposition (PVD sputtering or thermal evaporator), followed by rapid thermal annealing (RTA) in forming gas ($N_2/H_2$) at 400°C for 5 minutes.
   - Strip frontside protective photoresist using an acetone/IPA ultrasonic bath and dry under $N_2$.

3. **Probe Station Platen & Triaxial Chuck Setup:**
   - Secure the wafer onto the gold-plated vacuum chuck of a shielded microchamber probe station.
   - Verify continuous chuck vacuum hold ($\ge 70\text{ kPa}$ depression).
   - Ensure the probe station's dark box enclosure is sealed to completely eliminate ambient photon-assisted carrier generation during quasi-static and high-frequency C-V profiling.
   - Ground the substrate through the gold-plated chuck using guarded triaxial cabling connected to the LCR meter / SMU low terminal ($V_{low}$ / Force Low).

4. **Microchamber Nitrogen Purge & Dark Environment:**
   - Purge the dark enclosure with dry $N_2$ ($RH < 5\%$) to prevent moisture condensation and parasitic surface conduction paths during metrology sweeps.
   - Allow thermal stabilization at standard room temperature ($25.0^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$) or heated chuck stage ($85.0^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ for DRAM retention/leakage benchmark conditions).

5. **Top Dot Microchamber Probe Landing:**
   - Align tungsten or beryllium-copper microprobe tips (tip radius $\le 5\ \mu\text{m}$) over the frontside gate metal/polysilicon dot test pad under microscope optics.
   - Lower the manipulator with precise micro-stepper control until initial electrical contact is registered; apply an overdrive travel of 10 to 15 $\mu\text{m}$ to pierce surface passivating oxides without punching through thin dielectric layers (~3.5 nm physical thickness).
   - Route probe signal through a guarded triaxial probe arm to the high terminal ($V_{high}$ / Force High / Sense High).

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
Acceptance Threshold Limits (Upper Bound)
                      ┌────────────────────────────────┐
                      │░░░░░░░░░░                      │
  Probe Overdrive (um)┤░░░░░░░░░░                      │
                      │▒▒                              │
 Dark Box Leakage (fA)┤▒▒                              │
    Chuck Stray C (fF)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
                      │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
Back-Contact R_c (ohm)┤███████                         │
                      │███████                         │
                      └┬───────┬───────┬──────┬───────┬┘
                      0.0    12.5    25.0   37.5   50.0 
```

1. **Back-Contact Ohmic Series Resistance ($R_{series}$ / $R_c$):**  
   - **Target Metric:** $\le 10.0\ \Omega$ (measured across wafer back-contact to chuck ground before C-V sweep).
2. **Open-Circuit Background Stray Capacitance:**  
   - **Target Metric:** $\le 50.0\text{ fF}$ (residual probe-to-chuck parasitic capacitance post-open calibration, well below cell budget $C_s = 25\text{ to }30\text{ fF}$).
3. **Dark Box Baseline Parasitic Leakage Current:**  
   - **Target Metric:** $\le 1.0\text{ fA}$ at $V_{bias} = 1.0\text{ V}$ and $85.0^\circ\text{C}$ enclosure temperature (matching the sub-1 fA DRAM storage retention leakage threshold).
4. **Manipulator Probe Overdrive Travel Tolerance:**  
   - **Target Metric:** $12.5 \pm 2.5\ \mu\text{m}$ (travel range 10.0 to 15.0 $\mu\text{m}$ to safeguard the ~3.5 nm thin gate dielectric from mechanical punch-through).

---

### Literature Context Citations

- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**  
  - Target cell capacitance baseline of $25\text{ to }30\text{ fF}$ per cell (data retention $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).
  - Gate dielectric physical thickness $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ grown by dry oxidation ($850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$), requiring low overdrive landing.
  - High-k dielectric equivalent oxide thickness ($\text{EOT}$) around $3\text{ to }4\text{ nm}$ ($\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$/$\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$).
- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**  
  - Sub-threshold and junction leakage threshold limit $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
  - Minimum capacitance budget of $28\text{ fF/cell}$ validating triaxial guard calibration requirements.
- **Source: Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout**  
  - Baseline nominal storage cell capacitance $C_s = 25\text{ fF}$ compared against bitline parasitics $C_{BL} = 250\text{ fF}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Back-side ohmic contact impedance directly acts as a series parasitic resistance (R_series) in high-frequency (1 MHz) C-V metrology. If R_series exceeds 5-10 Ohms across the substrate chuck, the measured accumulation capacitance will artificially roll off according to C_meas = C_ox / [1 + (omega * C_ox * R_series)^2], yielding corrupted equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) and erroneous Dit calculations downstream in the 180nm dielectric line.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Direct physical contact between rough unpolished wafer backsides and brass/vacuum chucks causes Schottky barrier rectification on p-type Si (1-10 Ohm*cm). A standardized back-surface native oxide strip using buffered oxide etch (BOE) or dilute HF, followed immediately by 200-300 nm sputtered/evaporated Al (or In-Ga eutectic mechanical scrubbing for rapid test coupons) and a 400°C forming gas anneal (N2/H2 95:5), is mandatory to achieve an unrectified, true ohmic contact with contact resistivity below 1e-4 Ohm*cm2.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: In-Ga eutectic liquid metal paste presents severe gallium cross-contamination risks for downstream CMOS furnaces and vacuum chucks, while sputtering Au on wafer backsides introduces gold deep-level traps (E_v + 0.35 eV / E_c - 0.54 eV) that kill DRAM access transistor retention time. The baseline process must standardize on semiconductor-grade PVD Al target (99.999% purity) and dedicated quartz carrier boats to prevent fab-wide contamination.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Back-contact preparation adds chemical processing and annealing cycle time directly preceding probe station touchdown. Maintaining a rigid queue time between back-contact native oxide etch, metallization, and probe-station vacuum-chuck mounting is essential to eliminate rework loops and ensure reproducible MOSCAP gate-dot testing throughput across fab batches.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Series resistance artifact: Native oxide regrowth on backside prior to metallization introduces a non-ohmic Schottky barrier causing accumulation capacitance roll-off at 1 MHz.
1. Probe punch-through / dot scrub damage: Excessive micromanipulator probe contact force (>50 mN) rupturing the thin 3.5 nm gate dielectric under the 200/500 um Al gate dot.
1. Parasitic chuck leakage: High backside contact resistance causing phase angle distortion (phase angle < 85° in accumulation) rendering parallel conductance and Dit extraction invalid.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-2-3-3-1-01` | **Backside Ohmic Contact Linearity and Series Resistance Extraction** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Parameter Analyzer with B1505A / SMU modules, manual analytical probe station with gold-plated vacuum chuck | 1. Lower tungsten probe tip (radius 5 um) onto an unpassivated wafer substrate front-side test pad or adjacent substrate tap. 2. Sweep chuck-to-probe DC voltage from -2.0 V to +2.0 V in 50 mV steps. 3. Record I-V curve and extract slope dI/dV at zero bias and maximum bias (+/- 1.5 V). 4. Calculate contact linearity ratio [dI/dV(+1.5V)] / [dI/dV(-1.5V)] and total substrate bulk series resistance R_series. | `I-V response must be purely ohmic and symmetric: Contact linearity ratio must fall between 0.90 and 1.10, and extracted series resistance R_series must be < 5.0 Ohms across the 100 mm / 150 mm substrate area.` |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-2-3-3-1-02` | **High-Frequency Accumulation Phase Angle and C_ox Dispersion Verification** | Keysight E4980A Precision LCR Meter / B1520A Multifrequency C-V Unit connected via coaxial triaxial cables to shielded probe station | 1. Apply gate DC bias of -3.0 V (strong accumulation for p-type Si) with an AC oscillation signal of 25 mV RMS at 100 kHz, 500 kHz, and 1 MHz. 2. Measure parallel capacitance Cp, parallel conductance Gp, and impedance phase angle Theta. 3. Quantify high-frequency accumulation capacitance dispersion: Delta_C = |Cp(100kHz) - Cp(1MHz)| / Cp(100kHz) * 100%. | `Impedance phase angle Theta must be >= 86.0 degrees in strong accumulation (-3.0 V bias at 1 MHz), and high-frequency capacitance dispersion Delta_C between 100 kHz and 1 MHz must be <= 2.5%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Fluoropolymer / heavy neoprene gloves over nitrile inner gloves, Chemical splash apron and full-face polycarbonate shield, Safety goggles meeting ANSI Z87.1 standard, Cleanroom acid-resistant smock and closed-toe chemical-resistant boots
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For HF exposure: Immediately rinse affected area with copious laminar water for 2 minutes, then vigorously massage 2.5% calcium gluconate gel continuously into skin until medical help arrives; obtain emergency medical treatment immediately. In case of inhalation, administer oxygen and calcium gluconate aerosol if trained.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated polypropylene wet-bench exhaust hood maintaining face velocity of 0.5 +/- 0.1 m/s (100 FPM) equipped with continuous acid-scrubber ducting; forming gas tube furnace connected to combustible gas exhaust with continuous H2 leak sensor interlocking automatic safety shut-off valve.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Segregate all HF rinses and acid waste into dedicated fluoropolymer drain tanks; neutralize with calcium hydroxide [Ca(OH)2] slurry to precipitate non-hazardous calcium fluoride (CaF2) cake; verify supernatant pH between 6.5 and 8.5 before controlled discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| **Hydrofluoric Acid (Dilute 10:1 or 2%)** | `7664-39-3` | SEMI Grade 4 / VLSI Purified | `2.0% - 5.0% w/w` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: As-grown MOS capacitor wafer with front-side Al gate dots patterned via shadow mask sputtering, backside unpolished/passivated with native oxide and thermal oxide stray growth.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Backside stripped of native/thermal oxide, metallized with 300 nm continuous annealed Al ohmic layer (RMS roughness < 10 nm, contact resistivity < 1e-4 Ohm*cm2), loaded into probe station vacuum chuck.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time in air prior to backside metallization or between anneal and probe mounting induces native oxide growth (>1.2 nm SiO2) on bare silicon or galvanic oxidation on backside Al, creating parasitic contact series resistance and phase distortion that invalidates 1 MHz C-V extraction.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Standardized back-contact preparation protocol and high-precision probe station configuration established for MOS dot-capacitors, delivering repeatable ohmic substrate contact (<5 Ohms), minimal high-frequency dispersion (<2.5%), and verified 1 MHz C-V accumulation profiles for accurate physical oxide thickness and Dit characterization on 180nm DRAM test structures.

| `ASSERT-02` | **1 MHz Accumulation Impedance Phase Angle Theta at VG = -3.0V** | `88.0` | +/- 2.0 degrees (Minimum 86.0 degrees) | Direct measurement via Keysight E4980A LCR meter calibrated at probe needle tip |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher exit signoff is achieved when 5 distinct 500 um diameter MOS gate dots across the wafer demonstrate symmetrical ohmic I-V behavior (R_series < 5.0 Ohms), 1 MHz accumulation phase angle >= 86.0 degrees, and capacitance dispersion between 100 kHz and 1 MHz <= 2.5%, confirmed by archived .csv data logs and signed calibration checklists.

critics.systems_engineer: Back-side ohmic contact impedance directly acts as a series parasitic resistance (R_series) in high-frequency (1 MHz) C-V metrology. If R_series exceeds 5-10 Ohms across the substrate chuck, the measured accumulation capacitance will artificially roll off according to C_meas = C_ox / [1 + (omega * C_ox * R_series)^2], yielding corrupted equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) and erroneous Dit calculations downstream in the 180nm dielectric line.
critics.domain_expert: Direct physical contact between rough unpolished wafer backsides and brass/vacuum chucks causes Schottky barrier rectification on p-type Si (1-10 Ohm*cm). A standardized back-surface native oxide strip using buffered oxide etch (BOE) or dilute HF, followed immediately by 200-300 nm sputtered/evaporated Al (or In-Ga eutectic mechanical scrubbing for rapid test coupons) and a 400°C forming gas anneal (N2/H2 95:5), is mandatory to achieve an unrectified, true ohmic contact with contact resistivity below 1e-4 Ohm*cm2.
critics.supply_chain: In-Ga eutectic liquid metal paste presents severe gallium cross-contamination risks for downstream CMOS furnaces and vacuum chucks, while sputtering Au on wafer backsides introduces gold deep-level traps (E_v + 0.35 eV / E_c - 0.54 eV) that kill DRAM access transistor retention time. The baseline process must standardize on semiconductor-grade PVD Al target (99.999% purity) and dedicated quartz carrier boats to prevent fab-wide contamination.
critics.laya_pm: Back-contact preparation adds chemical processing and annealing cycle time directly preceding probe station touchdown. Maintaining a rigid queue time between back-contact native oxide etch, metallization, and probe-station vacuum-chuck mounting is essential to eliminate rework loops and ensure reproducible MOSCAP gate-dot testing throughput across fab batches.
critical_failure_modes: Series resistance artifact: Native oxide regrowth on backside prior to metallization introduces a non-ohmic Schottky barrier causing accumulation capacitance roll-off at 1 MHz.
Probe punch-through / dot scrub damage: Excessive micromanipulator probe contact force (>50 mN) rupturing the thin 3.5 nm gate dielectric under the 200/500 um Al gate dot.
Parasitic chuck leakage: High backside contact resistance causing phase angle distortion (phase angle < 85° in accumulation) rendering parallel conductance and Dit extraction invalid.
