# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Details
- **Title**: High-Frequency (100kHz–1MHz) & Quasi-Static C-V Dual-Sweep Acquisition
- **Module**: Metrology / MOS C-V Dielectric Metrology & EOT Extraction
- **Process Line**: Front-End Fabrication / High-K Gate Dielectric & Thin Film Thermal Oxidation Line
- **Technology Node**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM (Gen 2 µm)

---

## 1. Process Workflow & Methodology

```text
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│     Wafer Load &     │
│     Light-Tight      │
│      Shielding       │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│  Probe Calibration:  │
│   Open/Short/Load    │
│      Correction      │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│  High-Frequency C-V  │
│  Sweep: 100 kHz - 1  │
│         MHz          │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│   Quasi-Static C-V   │
│   Sweep: Ramp Rate   │
│        dV/dt         │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│     Simultaneous     │
│  Extraction: C_ox,   │
│      EOT, D_it       │
│                      │
└──────────────────────┘
```

---

## 2. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **Test Structure Selection & Wafer Setup**:
   - Transfer the 180nm test wafer onto the triaxial thermal chuck inside the light-tight, electrically shielded probe station.
   - Establish substrate backside contact (ground reference) and align microprobes to the MOS capacitor test pads corresponding to access transistor dummy gates and capacitor dielectric test structures.

2. **LCR & Electrometer Calibration**:
   - Perform open-circuit and short-circuit compensation on the LCR meter / impedance analyzer up to the probe tip plane across the $100\text{ kHz}$ to $1\text{ MHz}$ band.
   - Verify cabling parasitic capacitance nulling and zero-offset current verification on the quasi-static electrometer.

3. **High-Frequency (HF) C-V Acquisition**:
   - Set AC oscillation voltage level to $V_{ac} = 25\text{ mV}_\text{rms}$ at frequencies of $100\text{ kHz}$ and $1\text{ MHz}$.
   - Apply a continuous DC bias sweep ranging from accumulation to deep inversion (and reverse sweep to detect hysteresis / mobile ions), ensuring that the minority carrier response is suppressed at high frequency.
   - Record accumulation capacitance ($C_{ox}$) in strong accumulation.

4. **Quasi-Static (QS) C-V Acquisition**:
   - Apply a slow linear voltage ramp ($dV/dt$) using the quasi-static electrometer or ramp-rate unit to allow thermal equilibrium of inversion layer minority carriers.
   - Measure displacement current $I_{meas}$ to calculate low-frequency capacitance:
     $$C_{QS} = \frac{I_{meas}}{dV/dt}$$
   - Validate leakage suppression to ensure gate leakage does not distort the quasi-static curve.

5. **Interface Trap Density ($D_{it}$) & EOT Parameter Extraction**:
   - Superimpose the high-frequency ($100\text{ kHz} - 1\text{ MHz}$) and quasi-static ($C_{QS}$) curves.
   - Compute interface trap density ($D_{it}$) using the High-Low frequency method:
     $$D_{it} = \frac{C_{ox}}{q} \left( \frac{C_{QS}}{C_{ox} - C_{QS}} - \frac{C_{HF}}{C_{ox} - C_{HF}} \right)$$
   - Calculate Equivalent Oxide Thickness ($\text{EOT}$) from strong accumulation capacitance per unit area:
     $$\text{EOT} = \frac{\varepsilon_{SiO2} \cdot \varepsilon_0 \cdot A}{C_{ox}}$$

---

## 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
                    Dielectric Thickness Bounds (nm)    
                 ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
                 │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒    │
Physical Tox SiO2┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒    │
   EOT High-k max┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
                 │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
   EOT High-k min┤████████████████████████████         │
                 │████████████████████████████         │
                 └┬────────┬────────┬────────┬────────┬┘
                  0        1        2        3        4 
```

1. **Gate Dielectric Physical Thickness**:
   - **Target**: Physical $T_{ox} \sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ for thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ processed at $850^\circ\text{C} - 900^\circ\text{C}$ dry oxidation.
2. **Capacitor Dielectric Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT)**:
   - **Target**: $\text{EOT} = 3.0\text{ nm}$ to $4.0\text{ nm}$ for high-k ($\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ / $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$) stacked capacitor structures.
3. **Stacked Cell Capacitance ($C_s$) Budget**:
   - **Target**: Minimum $25\text{ fF}$ to $30\text{ fF}$ per cell (baseline $\ge 28\text{ fF/cell}$) at operating conditions.
4. **Thermal Leakage Current Threshold**:
   - **Target**: Sub-threshold and junction leakage $\le 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ to maintain retention time $> 64\text{ ms}$.

---

## 4. Literature & Source Citations
- **[Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering]**: 
  - Validates gate dielectric physical thickness of $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ ($\text{SiO}_2$ dry oxidation at $850^\circ\text{C} - 900^\circ\text{C}$), high-k stacked capacitor $\text{EOT}$ range between $3\text{ nm}$ and $4\text{ nm}$, and cell storage capacitance target of $25\text{ fF} - 30\text{ fF}$ ensuring retention $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **[Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]**:
  - Validates capacitance budget of minimum $28\text{ fF/cell}$ for soft-error immunity and the leakage current target of $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Dual-sweep high-frequency (100 kHz to 1 MHz) combined with quasi-static C-V requires rigorous synchronization between the LCR meter (Keysight E4980A / HP 4284A) and the high-resolution electrometer/SMU (Keithley 6517B or 4200-SCS). Parasitic cable capacitance and probe chuck stray impedance must be calibrated out down to < 50 fF via open/short/load de-embedding at the probe tips. In an open-source 180nm DRAM fab environment, ambient 50/60 Hz EMI and chuck thermal drift can introduce spurious displacement currents in quasi-static ramp measurements (dQ/dt = C*dV/dt + V*dC/dt), completely corrupting interface trap density (Dit) extraction across the bandgap.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For a 180nm gate dielectric stack (target physical tox ~3.5 nm to 6.0 nm SiO2/SiON equivalent, or initial high-k gate test structures), quantum mechanical confinement effects and poly-depletion must be accounted for when extracting EOT. In quasi-static acquisition, leakage current through thin dielectrics (> 10^-3 A/cm^2) masks the true displacement current, leading to false Dit peaks or unphysical capacitance rollover. The ramp rate must be tightly controlled (e.g., 10 mV/s to 100 mV/s) to ensure thermal equilibrium in inversion without triggering high leakage integration errors.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Triaxial low-noise cables (Keithley 7078-TRX), Kelvin tungsten probe needles (< 5 µm radius), and guarded probe station chucks with gold plating are single-source import constraints. If high-end SMUs or semiconductor parameter analyzers (4200A-SCS) are restricted or delayed, secondary-market refurbished HP 4284A LCR meters and Keithley 617/6514 electrometers must be maintained with verified calibration standards (NIST traceable standard mica/air capacitors).
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: MOS C-V characterization acts as the gatekeeper milestone for gate oxide reliability and thickness signoff prior to source/drain implantation and DRAM access transistor metallization. The metrology loop must deliver reproducible EOT, Vfb, and Dit within a 4-hour cycle time per lot to prevent wafer stagnation in dry nitrogen desiccators and avoid queue-time expiration prior to subsequent vacuum metallization.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Quasi-static leakage current breakthrough: Gate leakage current exceeds capacitive displacement current (I_leak > I_disp = C_ox * dV/dt), resulting in negative or unbounded interface trap density (Dit) calculation.
1. Parasitic stray capacitance decoupling failure: Uncompensated probe tip and triax cable capacitance (> 1 pF) obscures small-area (e.g., 100 µm x 100 µm) MOS capacitor accumulation plateau, producing artificially inflated EOT readings.
1. Slow trap hysteresis and mobile ion drift: Moisture or sodium surface contamination on unpassivated test pads causes sweep hysteresis (> 150 mV shift between forward and reverse bias), invalidating flatband voltage (Vfb) determination.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-2-3-3-2-01` | **High-Frequency (100kHz & 1MHz) Dual-Sweep Hysteresis and Flatband Extraction** | Precision LCR Meter (Keysight E4980A or HP 4284A), Shielded Triaxial Probe Station with Dark Box and Faraday Shield, Tungsten Probes (5 µm tip radius), Vacuum Chuck with back-contact bias. | 1. Position high-force tungsten probe on gate contact pad; confirm back-surface ohmic contact resistance < 10 ohms to chuck. 2. Set AC signal amplitude to 25 mV RMS at 100 kHz. 3. Bias sweep from deep accumulation (-2.5 V) to strong inversion (+2.5 V) and sweep back to -2.5 V at a step of 25 mV and 100 ms hold time. 4. Repeat acquisition at 1 MHz test frequency. 5. Record C-V and G-V (conductance) curves, extract accumulation capacitance (C_max) at -2.5 V and flatband voltage (V_fb). | `Dual-sweep hysteresis delta-V_fb <= 30 mV between forward and reverse sweeps at 100 kHz; accumulation capacitance reproducibility between 100 kHz and 1 MHz within ±3.0% after series resistance correction (R_s < 20 ohms).` |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-2-3-3-2-02` | **Quasi-Static Displacement Current C-V Sweep and Interface Trap Density (Dit) Extraction** | High-Resolution Sub-Femtoamp Electrometer/SMU (Keithley 6517B or 4200-SCS with 4200-PA preamp), Triax Guarded Probe Chuck, Temperature-Controlled Probe Station, Faraday Enclosure. | 1. Land electrometer sense needle on the gate electrode of the 100 µm x 100 µm MOS capacitor; land low-side ground sense on substrate contact pad. 2. Apply linear voltage ramp from -2.5 V to +2.0 V at a constant dV/dt = 50 mV/s. 3. Measure quasi-static displacement current I_qs(V) at 10 mV intervals (I_qs = C_qs * dV/dt). 4. Align with 100 kHz HF C-V curve from TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-2-3-3-2-01. 5. Compute Dit across the bandgap using High-Low (Castagné-Vapaille) method: Dit = (C_ox / q) * ((C_qs / (C_ox - C_qs)) - (C_hf / (C_ox - C_hf))). | `Peak midgap interface trap density Dit <= 5.0e10 cm^-2 eV^-1; quasi-static inversion capacitance recovers to within ±5.0% of accumulation oxide capacitance (C_ox) at +2.0 V; gate leakage current I_leak <= 50 fA at V_gate = -1.0 V.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (anti-static, powder-free, double-gloved), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV and impact-resistant safety glasses, Anti-static ESD lab coat / cleanroom bunny suit with grounded wrist strap, Conductive cleanroom ESD footwear
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with IPA: Flush skin with copious amounts of water for at least 15 minutes; remove contaminated garments. Eye contact: Irrigate eye immediately at emergency eyewash station for 15 minutes with eyelids held open. Inhalation of inert nitrogen (asphyxiant risk in enclosed dark box): Move personnel to fresh air immediately; provide artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing has ceased. High-voltage shock (> 50 V bias compliance during dielectric breakdown sweeps): De-energize tool immediately; assess breathing and pulse; call site emergency response and initiate CPR if necessary.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Probe station local exhaust snorkel ventilation operating at >= 100 CFM to extract IPA solvent vapors during needle tip scrubbing; room positive-pressure laminar airflow ceiling HEPA fan-filter units maintaining Class 100/ISO 5 air quality.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA wipes and swabs collected in dedicated grounded, self-closing hazardous flammable waste container; spent probe tips disposed of in designated puncture-proof sharps disposal bin.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) for probe needle cleaning** | `67-63-0` | VLSI / Semiconductor Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (purge gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra High Purity (UHP) Grade 5.0 | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly patterned gate metal pads (sputtered Al/1%Si or poly-Si/TiN) over gate dielectric, post-forming gas anneal (400°C 10% H2/92% N2), free of photoresist residues, particulate count < 5 defects @ 0.2 µm across active test dies.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Electrically characterized MOS pads with minimal probe scrub marks (< 3 µm scrub depth, zero pad peel-off), vacuum-dried, purged with UHP N2, ready for inter-layer dielectric (ILD) PECVD deposition.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive exposure to ambient cleanroom humidity causes moisture adsorption and native oxidation/hydroxylation of unpassivated aluminum pad surfaces, leading to erratic probe contact resistance (Rc > 100 ohms), mobile sodium ion drift (delta-Vfb > 200 mV), and false high-Dit extraction.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful dual-sweep high-frequency (100 kHz/1 MHz) and quasi-static C-V profiling on 180nm DRAM gate dielectric structures, delivering de-embedded C-V/G-V curves, validated flatband voltage, equivalent oxide thickness (EOT), and interface trap density distribution across the silicon bandgap without leakage artifacts.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `MOS_CV_DUAL_SWEEP_RAW_DATA_LOT_GEN2.csv`
- [ ] `EOT_VFB_DIT_EXTRACTION_REPORT_GEN2.pdf`
- [ ] `PROBE_SCRUB_PAD_INTEGRITY_INSPECTION.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) extracted from accumulation capacitance at 100 kHz with quantum confinement correction** | `4.20 nm` | ±0.15 nm | NCSU CVC (C-V Classic) modeling fit against corrected 100 kHz high-frequency accumulation capacitance on 100 µm x 100 µm test MOS capacitors. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Midgap interface trap density (Dit) extracted via High-Low (Castagné-Vapaille) method** | `3.5e10 cm^-2 eV^-1` | ±1.5e10 cm^-2 eV^-1 | Comparison between 100 kHz HF curve and 50 mV/s quasi-static C-V curve at midgap potential (E - Ev = 0.56 eV). |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Flatband voltage hysteresis shift under bidirectional -2.5V to +2.5V dual sweep** | `15.0 mV` | ±10.0 mV | Second-derivative inflection analysis of forward vs. reverse high-frequency C-V curves. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher exit approval requires verified acquisition of >= 5 distinct dies per wafer across 3 wafers per lot, showing C-V hysteresis delta-Vfb <= 25 mV, extracted EOT within 4.05 nm - 4.35 nm, midgap Dit <= 5.0e10 cm^-2 eV^-1, and complete probe mark inspection confirming pad contact integrity without gate oxide dielectric puncture.

Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering (IEEE / Legacy Foundry Technical Reports)

critics.systems_engineer: Dual-sweep high-frequency (100 kHz to 1 MHz) combined with quasi-static C-V requires rigorous synchronization between the LCR meter (Keysight E4980A / HP 4284A) and the high-resolution electrometer/SMU (Keithley 6517B or 4200-SCS). Parasitic cable capacitance and probe chuck stray impedance must be calibrated out down to < 50 fF via open/short/load de-embedding at the probe tips. In an open-source 180nm DRAM fab environment, ambient 50/60 Hz EMI and chuck thermal drift can introduce spurious displacement currents in quasi-static ramp measurements (dQ/dt = C*dV/dt + V*dC/dt), completely corrupting interface trap density (Dit) extraction across the bandgap.
critics.domain_expert: For a 180nm gate dielectric stack (target physical tox ~3.5 nm to 6.0 nm SiO2/SiON equivalent, or initial high-k gate test structures), quantum mechanical confinement effects and poly-depletion must be accounted for when extracting EOT. In quasi-static acquisition, leakage current through thin dielectrics (> 10^-3 A/cm^2) masks the true displacement current, leading to false Dit peaks or unphysical capacitance rollover. The ramp rate must be tightly controlled (e.g., 10 mV/s to 100 mV/s) to ensure thermal equilibrium in inversion without triggering high leakage integration errors.
critics.supply_chain: Triaxial low-noise cables (Keithley 7078-TRX), Kelvin tungsten probe needles (< 5 µm radius), and guarded probe station chucks with gold plating are single-source import constraints. If high-end SMUs or semiconductor parameter analyzers (4200A-SCS) are restricted or delayed, secondary-market refurbished HP 4284A LCR meters and Keithley 617/6514 electrometers must be maintained with verified calibration standards (NIST traceable standard mica/air capacitors).
critics.laya_pm: MOS C-V characterization acts as the gatekeeper milestone for gate oxide reliability and thickness signoff prior to source/drain implantation and DRAM access transistor metallization. The metrology loop must deliver reproducible EOT, Vfb, and Dit within a 4-hour cycle time per lot to prevent wafer stagnation in dry nitrogen desiccators and avoid queue-time expiration prior to subsequent vacuum metallization.
critical_failure_modes: Quasi-static leakage current breakthrough: Gate leakage current exceeds capacitive displacement current (I_leak > I_disp = C_ox * dV/dt), resulting in negative or unbounded interface trap density (Dit) calculation.

Parasitic stray capacitance decoupling failure: Uncompensated probe tip and triax cable capacitance (> 1 pF) obscures small-area (e.g., 100 µm x 100 µm) MOS capacitor accumulation plateau, producing artificially inflated EOT readings.

Slow trap hysteresis and mobile ion drift: Moisture or sodium surface contamination on unpassivated test pads causes sweep hysteresis (> 150 mV shift between forward and reverse bias), invalidating flatband voltage (Vfb) determination.

testcases.title: High-Frequency (100kHz & 1MHz) Dual-Sweep Hysteresis and Flatband Extraction
testcases.instrumentation: Precision LCR Meter (Keysight E4980A or HP 4284A), Shielded Triaxial Probe Station with Dark Box and Faraday Shield, Tungsten Probes (5 µm tip radius), Vacuum Chuck with back-contact bias.

Room temperature stabilized at 23.0°C ± 1.0°C, RH < 40%. MOS capacitor pad size: 100 µm x 100 µm aluminum gate on p-type Si substrate.
testcases.procedure: 1. Position high-force tungsten probe on gate contact pad; confirm back-surface ohmic contact resistance < 10 ohms to chuck. 2. Set AC signal amplitude to 25 mV RMS at 100 kHz. 3. Bias sweep from deep accumulation (-2.5 V) to strong inversion (+2.5 V) and sweep back to -2.5 V at a step of 25 mV and 100 ms hold time. 4. Repeat acquisition at 1 MHz test frequency. 5. Record C-V and G-V (conductance) curves, extract accumulation capacitance (C_max) at -2.5 V and flatband voltage (V_fb).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Dual-sweep hysteresis delta-V_fb <= 30 mV between forward and reverse sweeps at 100 kHz; accumulation capacitance reproducibility between 100 kHz and 1 MHz within ±3.0% after series resistance correction (R_s < 20 ohms).

testcases.title: Quasi-Static Displacement Current C-V Sweep and Interface Trap Density (Dit) Extraction
testcases.instrumentation: High-Resolution Sub-Femtoamp Electrometer/SMU (Keithley 6517B or 4200-SCS with 4200-PA preamp), Triax Guarded Probe Chuck, Temperature-Controlled Probe Station, Faraday Enclosure.
testcases.pre_conditions: Dark box closed with zero ambient light (< 0.01 lux). Baseline system leakage current on open probe <= 10 fA from -2.5 V to +2.5 V. Wafer pre-conditioned under dark dry N2 flow for 30 minutes.
testcases.procedure: 1. Land electrometer sense needle on the gate electrode of the 100 µm x 100 µm MOS capacitor; land low-side ground sense on substrate contact pad. 2. Apply linear voltage ramp from -2.5 V to +2.0 V at a constant dV/dt = 50 mV/s. 3. Measure quasi-static displacement current I_qs(V) at 10 mV intervals (I_qs = C_qs * dV/dt). 4. Align with 100 kHz HF C-V curve from TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-2-3-3-2-01. 5. Compute Dit across the bandgap using High-Low (Castagné-Vapaille) method: Dit = (C_ox / q) * ((C_qs / (C_ox - C_qs)) - (C_hf / (C_ox - C_hf))).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Peak midgap interface trap density Dit <= 5.0e10 cm^-2 eV^-1; quasi-static inversion capacitance recovers to within ±5.0% of accumulation oxide capacitance (C_ox) at +2.0 V; gate leakage current I_leak <= 50 fA at V_gate = -1.0 V.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Quantum-Corrected C-V Modeling, EOT & Interface State Density ($D_{it}$) Extraction

**Document ID:** `SOP-FAB-MET-180-QCV-001`  
**Process Line:** High-K Gate Dielectric & Thin Film Thermal Oxidation Line [Front-End Fabrication]  
**Technology Node:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (Gen 2 µm Architecture)  
**Action Type:** Make / Metrology Execution  

---

### 1. Metrology Process Architecture

│                        │
│   MOS Dot Structure    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │

│                        │    │                        │
└───────────┬────────────┘    └────────────┬───────────┘
            │                              │
            │ ╭────────────────────────────╯
            ▼ ▼

│       Correction       │
│                        │

             │

┌────────────────────────┐    ┌────────────────────────┐

│           nm           │    │                        │

│          Pass          │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

#### Step 1: Wafer Loading & Probe Setup
1. Mount the 180nm monitor wafer with designated MOS capacitor test dots and access transistor test structures ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$) on a temperature-controlled chuck stabilized at $25.0^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ (with secondary qualification at $85.0^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$).
2. Secure Kelvin micro-probes on the gate top contact and substrate/well back-contact inside a light-tight, electrically shielded Faraday cage to eliminate stray displacement currents.

#### Step 2: High-Frequency (HF) Capacitance-Voltage (C-V) Acquisition
1. Connect the LCR impedance analyzer in parallel-equivalent mode ($C_p - G_p$).
2. Apply a small AC oscillation signal of $15\text{ mV}_{\text{rms}}$ at $100\text{ kHz}$ and $1.0\text{ MHz}$.
3. Sweep the DC gate bias $V_G$ from accumulation ($-2.5\text{ V}$) through depletion to strong inversion ($+2.5\text{ V}$) at a step resolution $\le 20\text{ mV}$.
4. Perform Series Resistance ($R_s$) correction on the measured raw capacitance $C_{ma}$ and conductance $G_{ma}$:
   $$C_{hf} = \frac{(G_{ma}^2 + \omega^2 C_{ma}^2) C_{ma}}{[\omega C_{ma} - (G_{ma}^2 + \omega^2 C_{ma}^2) R_s \omega]^2 + G_{ma}^2}$$

#### Step 3: Quasi-Static (QS) Low-Frequency C-V Acquisition
1. Switch to the electrometer quasi-static C-V test head.
2. Initialize zero-bias equilibrium and sweep $V_G$ from accumulation to inversion at a linear ramp rate of $0.10\text{ V/s}$ ($dV/dt$), recording displacement current $I_{qs}$:
   $$C_{qs}(V_G) = \frac{I_{qs}(V_G)}{dV/dt}$$
3. Confirm absence of transient displacement charging anomalies or leakage distortions before modeling.

#### Step 4: Quantum-Mechanical (QM) Schrodinger-Poisson Fitting & EOT Extraction
1. Import corrected HF C-V curves into the 1D self-consistent Schrödinger-Poisson numerical solver.
2. Incorporate quantum carrier confinement in the silicon substrate (inversion/accumulation layer quantum capacitance offset $\Delta z \approx 0.3 - 0.5\text{ nm}$) and polysilicon gate depletion effects ($C_{\text{poly}}$).
3. Match the simulated quantum capacitance curve against measured accumulation capacitance ($C_{acc}$):
   $$\frac{1}{C_{tot}} = \frac{1}{C_{ox}} + \frac{1}{C_{qm}} + \frac{1}{C_{poly}}$$
4. Extract the physical Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT):
   $$\text{EOT} = \frac{\varepsilon_0 \cdot \varepsilon_{\text{SiO}_2} \cdot A_{\text{dot}}}{C_{ox}}$$
   where $\varepsilon_{\text{SiO}_2} = 3.9$ and $A_{\text{dot}}$ is the calibrated lithographic capacitor area.

#### Step 5: High-Low Frequency Interface State Density ($D_{it}$) Extraction
1. Align the surface potential $\psi_s(V_G)$ extracted from the integration of the quasi-static curve (Berglund integral):
   $$\psi_s(V_G) = \int_{V_{FB}}^{V_G} \left(1 - \frac{C_{qs}}{C_{ox}}\right) dV$$
2. Calculate the interface trap capacitance $C_{it}(\psi_s)$ using the combined High-Low method:
   $$C_{it} = \left(\frac{1}{C_{qs}} - \frac{1}{C_{ox}}\right)^{-1} - \left(\frac{1}{C_{hf}} - \frac{1}{C_{ox}}\right)^{-1}$$
3. Extract interface trap density across the silicon bandgap:
   $$D_{it} = \frac{C_{it}}{q \cdot A_{\text{dot}}}$$
4. Quantify mid-gap $D_{it}$ ($E - E_v \approx 0.56\text{ eV}$) and flag any excessive border or fast interface traps.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

     Dit (Mid-gap)┤▒▒▒▒                                │
                  │▒▒▒▒                                │
EOT (Quantum-Corr)┤█████                               │
                  │█████                               │
                  └┬────────┬────────┬───────┬────────┬┘
                   0        7       14      21       28 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value & Range | Tolerance / Physical Limit | Measurement Unit | Inspection Tool / Verification Mechanism |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Capacitor Dielectric EOT** | **$3.0\text{ nm}$ to $4.0\text{ nm}$** | $\pm 0.15\text{ nm}$ | $\text{nm}$ | 1D Schrödinger-Poisson Fit / High-Frequency MOS C-V Profiler |
| **Gate Oxide Physical Thickness ($T_{ox}$)** | **$\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$** (Dry $\text{SiO}_2$ grown at $850^\circ\text{C}-900^\circ\text{C}$) | $\pm 0.10\text{ nm}$ | $\text{nm}$ | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / Quantum C-V Accumulation Extraction |
| **Interface State Density ($D_{it}$)** | **$\le 2.0 \times 10^{10}$** at mid-gap | Upper ceiling: $5.0 \times 10^{10}$ | $\text{cm}^{-2}\cdot\text{eV}^{-1}$ | High-Low ($C_{qs} - C_{hf}$) Differential Metrology |
| **Cell Capacitance Yield Floor ($C_s$)** | **$\ge 28\text{ fF/cell}$** ($25\text{ to }30\text{ fF}$ nominal) | Leakage $< 1.0\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ | $\text{fF/cell}$ | Stacked Crown/Cylinder Array Metrology at $85^\circ\text{C}$ |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Source Citations

1. **[Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering](docs/context.yaml)**:
   - Dictates equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) window: *"stacked capacitors (Crown or Cylinder type) utilize silicon nitride (Si3N4) or tantalum pentoxide (Ta2O5) high-k dielectrics with equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) around 3 to 4 nm."*
   - Defines gate dielectric baseline: *"Gate dielectric is thermally grown silicon dioxide (SiO2) at 850°C-900°C dry oxidation with ~3.5 nm physical thickness."*
   - Validates cell charge storage envelope: *"The storage capacitor must maintain a minimum capacitance of 25 to 30 fF per cell to ensure data retention time > 64 ms at 85°C."*

2. **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench](docs/context.yaml)**:
   - Prescribes unit geometry and capacitance targets: *"Unit Cell Geometry: Access transistor channel length L = 180 nm, width W = 220 nm."*
   - Sets physical soft-error noise barrier: *"Capacitance Budget: Minimum 28 fF per cell ensures noise immunity against alpha-particle soft errors and bitline coupling capacitance."*
   - Enforces thermal leakage bound: *"Leakage Current Target: Sub-threshold and junction leakage must be kept below 1 fA/cell at 85°C to achieve refresh interval."*

3. **[Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout](docs/context.yaml)**:
   - Verifies operational readout boundary conditions: *"Differential Voltage Delta V = (C_s / (C_BL + C_s)) * (V_cell - V_DD/2). For typical cell capacitance C_s = 25 fF and bitline capacitance C_BL = 250 fF, signal delta V is approximately 100 mV to 150 mV."*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Failure to account for quantum mechanical carrier confinement and polysilicon gate depletion in Gen 2 (180nm node, tox ~ 3.5 nm) MOS capacitors overestimates physical oxide thickness (EOT) by 0.3 to 0.5 nm and shifts extracted flatband voltage (Vfb) by over 100 mV. The quantum-corrected C-V solver must self-consistently solve 1D Poisson-Schrodinger equations across accumulation and inversion regimes to ensure consistent SPICE parameter decks across digital access transistors and analog sensing circuits.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Direct extraction of interface trap density (Dit) across the silicon bandgap using the combined high-frequency (100 kHz - 1 MHz) and quasi-static (QSCV, ramp rate <= 50 mV/s) Castagne-Vapaille method suffers extreme vulnerability to dielectric leakage currents when Tox < 4.0 nm. Conductance profiling (G-V vs frequency 1 kHz - 10 MHz) and the Hauser NCSU C-V simulator must be used in conjunction to decouple series substrate resistance (Rs), parasitic cable inductance, and genuine interface trap conductance to maintain extracted Dit below 2.0e10 eV^-1 cm^-2.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Metrology throughput is bottlenecked by the dual-probe quasi-static electrometer integration and cryogenic/temperature-controlled chuck availability for deep-level trap extraction. Automated wafer-level probe cards require non-magnetic beryllium-copper or tungsten tips with contact force calibrated under 3.5 gf to avoid puncturing ultra-thin 3.5 nm gate dielectric test pads during 49-point wafer mapping.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: MOS C-V characterization sits on the critical path immediately following post-metal anneal (forming gas anneal, FGA). Excessive queue times or delays in the metrology feedback loop directly delay thermal budget adjustments in the thermal oxidation line, risking wafer lot hold status across multiple front-end runs.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Parasitic Series Resistance & Cable Inductance Skew: High substrate back-contact contact resistance (> 5 Ohm) causing artificial rollover and distortion in high-frequency accumulation capacitance, invalidating quantum EOT extraction.
1. Dielectric Tunneling Leakage Corrupting Quasi-Static Displacement Current: Direct gate tunneling current dominating displacement current dQ/dt during QSCV ramp, yielding non-physical negative interface trap densities or divergence at band edges.
1. Moisture Absorption and Charge Drift: Ambient humidity causing surface charge migration and mobile ion (Na+/K+) redistribution during unpassivated metrology delay, creating hysteresis and false Dit extraction peaks.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-2-3-3-3-01` | **Quantum-Corrected EOT Extraction via Dual-Frequency C-V and Poisson-Schrodinger Solver** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Parameter Analyzer with B1520A Multifrequency C-V Module (MFCMU), Cascade Microtech Summit 12000 Shielded Semi-Automated Probe Station with triaxial cabling and Faraday dark box. | 1. Perform open and short cable compensation at 100 kHz and 1 MHz on reference calibration substrate. 2. Establish low-resistance ohmic back-contact using gold-plated vacuum chuck with vacuum holding > 80 kPa. 3. Contact MOS gate pad with low-force (2.5 gf) W-probe. 4. Measure C-V characteristics from strong accumulation (-2.5 V) to deep inversion (+1.5 V) with AC signal amplitude Vac = 25 mV RMS at 100 kHz and 1 MHz. 5. Perform series resistance correction: C_cor = (G_m^2 + omega^2 * C_m^2) * C_m / (omega^2 * C_m^2 + (G_m - Rs * (G_m^2 + omega^2 * C_m^2))^2). 6. Execute self-consistent 1D Poisson-Schrodinger quantum solver fit against accumulation C-V curve to extract physical EOT, flatband voltage Vfb, and poly-depletion dopant density Npoly. | `Extracted quantum-corrected EOT must be within 3.50 nm ± 0.15 nm; poly-depletion active concentration Npoly >= 5.0e19 cm^-3; substrate doping Nsub = 1.0e17 to 3.0e17 cm^-3; standard deviation across 49 wafer sites <= 2.5%.` |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-2-3-3-3-02` | **Midgap Interface State Density (Dit) Extraction via High-Frequency / Quasi-Static C-V & Conductance Method** | Keysight B1500A Parameter Analyzer with B1500A-HR (High Resolution SMU) and B1520A MFCMU, thermally stabilized probe station at 25.0°C ± 0.1°C inside an RF/light-tight Faraday cage. | 1. Set electrometer in linear voltage ramp mode with dV/dt = 20 mV/s from inversion (+1.0 V) to accumulation (-2.0 V) to record quasi-static capacitance C_qs = I_leak_subtracted / (dV/dt). 2. Measure high-frequency (100 kHz) C_hf curve over the identical voltage range. 3. Align C_qs and C_hf at deep accumulation to verify absence of residual series resistance artifacts. 4. Compute interface trap density Dit(V) = (1 / q) * ( (C_qs * Cox / (Cox - C_qs)) - (C_hf * Cox / (Cox - C_hf)) ) / Area. 5. Cross-validate with conductance method Gp/omega versus frequency (1 kHz to 1 MHz) at midgap bias to verify peak extraction. | `Extracted midgap interface state density Dit_midgap <= 2.0e10 eV^-1 cm^-2; no anomalous Dit peak > 5.0e10 eV^-1 cm^-2 between (Ei - 0.3 eV) and (Ei + 0.3 eV); gate leakage compliance maintained < 10 pA across entire measurement window.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Class 100 Nitrile gloves (double-gloved, powder-free), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV and chemical splash safety goggles, Full electrostatic dissipative (ESD) cleanroom gowning including hood and booties, Thermal safety gloves for hot-chuck operations (up to 200°C)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of thermal burn from heated chuck, immediately immerse affected area in cool running water for at least 15 minutes. For forming gas release, evacuate area immediately; if inhaled, move victim to fresh air and supply supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored. For IPA eye contact, flush eyes thoroughly at eyewash station for 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous laminar airflow hood (Class 100 / ISO 5) with dedicated local point-of-use exhaust for solvent vapors (minimum capture velocity 100 fpm) and hydrogen monitoring sensors (LEL detector interlocked to gas shutoff at 10% LEL) in anneal-metrology interface.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA wipes and contaminated solvents collected in dedicated sealed, labeled flammables disposal containers; depleted forming gas vented via dedicated scrubbed exterior exhaust manifold.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| **Compressed Nitrogen (N2 purge)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity 6.0 (99.9999%) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly completed post-metal forming gas anneal (400°C H2/N2) with fully passivated Si/SiO2 dangling bonds and clean Al/TiN or poly top electrode pads free of fluorinated etch residue or native oxide growth.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Characterized MOS capacitor wafer with unpunctured pads, nitrogen-desiccated and vacuum-sealed in ESD cassette, ready for downstream inter-metal dielectric (IMD) deposition or final wafer sort.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air queue time causes ambient moisture adsorption and passivation de-hydrogenation, leading to artificial interface trap generation (+0.8e10 eV^-1 cm^-2 shift in Dit), flatband voltage drift due to airborne organic/alkali contamination, and false-positive lot rejection.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Complete metrology dataset containing quantum-corrected MOS C-V curves, validated 1D Poisson-Schrodinger EOT extraction models, and midgap/bandgap-resolved interface trap density (Dit) profiles across 49 wafer sites confirming thin-film dielectric reliability for 180nm open-source DRAM.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:

- [ ] `eot_dit_uniformity_contour_map.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

critics.systems_engineer: Failure to account for quantum mechanical carrier confinement and polysilicon gate depletion in Gen 2 (180nm node, tox ~ 3.5 nm) MOS capacitors overestimates physical oxide thickness (EOT) by 0.3 to 0.5 nm and shifts extracted flatband voltage (Vfb) by over 100 mV. The quantum-corrected C-V solver must self-consistently solve 1D Poisson-Schrodinger equations across accumulation and inversion regimes to ensure consistent SPICE parameter decks across digital access transistors and analog sensing circuits.
critics.domain_expert: Direct extraction of interface trap density (Dit) across the silicon bandgap using the combined high-frequency (100 kHz - 1 MHz) and quasi-static (QSCV, ramp rate <= 50 mV/s) Castagne-Vapaille method suffers extreme vulnerability to dielectric leakage currents when Tox < 4.0 nm. Conductance profiling (G-V vs frequency 1 kHz - 10 MHz) and the Hauser NCSU C-V simulator must be used in conjunction to decouple series substrate resistance (Rs), parasitic cable inductance, and genuine interface trap conductance to maintain extracted Dit below 2.0e10 eV^-1 cm^-2.
critics.supply_chain: Metrology throughput is bottlenecked by the dual-probe quasi-static electrometer integration and cryogenic/temperature-controlled chuck availability for deep-level trap extraction. Automated wafer-level probe cards require non-magnetic beryllium-copper or tungsten tips with contact force calibrated under 3.5 gf to avoid puncturing ultra-thin 3.5 nm gate dielectric test pads during 49-point wafer mapping.
critics.laya_pm: MOS C-V characterization sits on the critical path immediately following post-metal anneal (forming gas anneal, FGA). Excessive queue times or delays in the metrology feedback loop directly delay thermal budget adjustments in the thermal oxidation line, risking wafer lot hold status across multiple front-end runs.
critical_failure_modes: Parasitic Series Resistance & Cable Inductance Skew: High substrate back-contact contact resistance (> 5 Ohm) causing artificial rollover and distortion in high-frequency accumulation capacitance, invalidating quantum EOT extraction.

Dielectric Tunneling Leakage Corrupting Quasi-Static Displacement Current: Direct gate tunneling current dominating displacement current dQ/dt during QSCV ramp, yielding non-physical negative interface trap densities or divergence at band edges.

Moisture Absorption and Charge Drift: Ambient humidity causing surface charge migration and mobile ion (Na+/K+) redistribution during unpassivated metrology delay, creating hysteresis and false Dit extraction peaks.

testcases.title: Quantum-Corrected EOT Extraction via Dual-Frequency C-V and Poisson-Schrodinger Solver
testcases.instrumentation: Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Parameter Analyzer with B1520A Multifrequency C-V Module (MFCMU), Cascade Microtech Summit 12000 Shielded Semi-Automated Probe Station with triaxial cabling and Faraday dark box.
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer has completed forming gas anneal (400°C, 30 min, 10% H2/90% N2). MOS capacitor test structures (area A = 10,000 µm^2, square pad 100 µm x 100 µm, p-type Si substrate, N+ poly gate) cleaned and loaded under dry nitrogen curtain.
testcases.procedure: 1. Perform open and short cable compensation at 100 kHz and 1 MHz on reference calibration substrate. 2. Establish low-resistance ohmic back-contact using gold-plated vacuum chuck with vacuum holding > 80 kPa. 3. Contact MOS gate pad with low-force (2.5 gf) W-probe. 4. Measure C-V characteristics from strong accumulation (-2.5 V) to deep inversion (+1.5 V) with AC signal amplitude Vac = 25 mV RMS at 100 kHz and 1 MHz. 5. Perform series resistance correction: C_cor = (G_m^2 + omega^2 * C_m^2) * C_m / (omega^2 * C_m^2 + (G_m - Rs * (G_m^2 + omega^2 * C_m^2))^2). 6. Execute self-consistent 1D Poisson-Schrodinger quantum solver fit against accumulation C-V curve to extract physical EOT, flatband voltage Vfb, and poly-depletion dopant density Npoly.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Extracted quantum-corrected EOT must be within 3.50 nm ± 0.15 nm; poly-depletion active concentration Npoly >= 5.0e19 cm^-3; substrate doping Nsub = 1.0e17 to 3.0e17 cm^-3; standard deviation across 49 wafer sites <= 2.5%.

testcases.title: Midgap Interface State Density (Dit) Extraction via High-Frequency / Quasi-Static C-V & Conductance Method
testcases.instrumentation: Keysight B1500A Parameter Analyzer with B1500A-HR (High Resolution SMU) and B1520A MFCMU, thermally stabilized probe station at 25.0°C ± 0.1°C inside an RF/light-tight Faraday cage.
testcases.pre_conditions: TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-2-3-3-3-01 passed successfully. MOS capacitor structures (A = 25,000 µm^2) grounded and verified for gate leakage Ig < 1.0 pA at Vg = -0.5 V.
testcases.procedure: 1. Set electrometer in linear voltage ramp mode with dV/dt = 20 mV/s from inversion (+1.0 V) to accumulation (-2.0 V) to record quasi-static capacitance C_qs = I_leak_subtracted / (dV/dt). 2. Measure high-frequency (100 kHz) C_hf curve over the identical voltage range. 3. Align C_qs and C_hf at deep accumulation to verify absence of residual series resistance artifacts. 4. Compute interface trap density Dit(V) = (1 / q) * ( (C_qs * Cox / (Cox - C_qs)) - (C_hf * Cox / (Cox - C_hf)) ) / Area. 5. Cross-validate with conductance method Gp/omega versus frequency (1 kHz to 1 MHz) at midgap bias to verify peak extraction.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Extracted midgap interface state density Dit_midgap <= 2.0e10 eV^-1 cm^-2; no anomalous Dit peak > 5.0e10 eV^-1 cm^-2 between (Ei - 0.3 eV) and (Ei + 0.3 eV); gate leakage compliance maintained < 10 pA across entire measurement window.

ppe_required: Cleanroom Class 100 Nitrile gloves (double-gloved, powder-free)
ANSI Z87.1 certified UV and chemical splash safety goggles
Full electrostatic dissipative (ESD) cleanroom gowning including hood and booties
Thermal safety gloves for hot-chuck operations (up to 200°C)

Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) for chuck & wafer cleaning

ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: In case of thermal burn from heated chuck, immediately immerse affected area in cool running water for at least 15 minutes. For forming gas release, evacuate area immediately; if inhaled, move victim to fresh air and supply supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored. For IPA eye contact, flush eyes thoroughly at eyewash station for 15 minutes.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Continuous laminar airflow hood (Class 100 / ISO 5) with dedicated local point-of-use exhaust for solvent vapors (minimum capture velocity 100 fpm) and hydrogen monitoring sensors (LEL detector interlocked to gas shutoff at 10% LEL) in anneal-metrology interface.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Used IPA wipes and contaminated solvents collected in dedicated sealed, labeled flammables disposal containers; depleted forming gas vented via dedicated scrubbed exterior exhaust manifold.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Freshly completed post-metal forming gas anneal (400°C H2/N2) with fully passivated Si/SiO2 dangling bonds and clean Al/TiN or poly top electrode pads free of fluorinated etch residue or native oxide growth.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Characterized MOS capacitor wafer with unpunctured pads, nitrogen-desiccated and vacuum-sealed in ESD cassette, ready for downstream inter-metal dielectric (IMD) deposition or final wafer sort.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding air queue time causes ambient moisture adsorption and passivation de-hydrogenation, leading to artificial interface trap generation (+0.8e10 eV^-1 cm^-2 shift in Dit), flatband voltage drift due to airborne organic/alkali contamination, and false-positive lot rejection.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Interconnect Sputtering & Die Packaging Probe Station (Gen 2: 180nm DRAM)

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Wafer Cleaning &    │
│         Degas          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Ti/Cu Barrier & Seed  │
│        Sputter         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Al-Cu Interconnect   │
│     Metallization      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Passivation & Pad    │
│          Open          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Die Packaging Probe   │
│   Station Parametric   │
│          Test          │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Pre-Sputter Degas & In-Situ RF Etch**:
   - Transfer wafer into the ultra-high vacuum (UHV) multi-chamber sputtering cluster tool.
   - Perform degas bake and low-power in-situ Ar+ soft sputter etch to remove native oxide on exposed contact plugs (W-plugs) without degrading dielectric interfaces.
2. **Barrier & Seed Layer Magnetron Sputtering**:
   - Sputter a conformal barrier/liner layer (Ti / TiN) followed by metallization seed to prevent electromigration and contact interdiffusion over bitline and wordline contact interfaces.
3. **Interconnect Metallization & Patterning**:
   - Deposit top-level interconnect metal (Al-Cu / Cu alloy) targeted to accommodate tight bitline/wordline line pitches.
   - Execute lithography, metal reactive ion etching (RIE), or CMP planarization followed by final passivation layer deposition (SiO2/Si3N4) and bond pad opening etch.
4. **Die Packaging Probe Station Setup & Alignment**:
   - Mount processed wafer onto the thermal vacuum chuck of the packaging probe station.
   - Set chuck temperature to **85°C** to simulate worst-case retention and leakage conditions.
   - Align multi-contact wedge probe card to peripheral I/O bond pads and test structure pads (TEG) with micro-positioning accuracy.
5. **Electrical Parametric & Yield Characterization**:
   - Apply precharge potential $V_{\text{DD}} / 2$ to complementary bitlines ($BL$ and $\overline{BL}$).
   - Assert wordlines to actuate access transistors and measure differential read signal voltage ($\Delta V$).
   - Run sub-threshold/junction leakage parameter sweep on the cell array and record capacitor retention parameters.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Targets

```text
                  Electrical Acceptance Metrics Target Values
                     ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
                     │░                                │
     Max Leakage (fA)┤░                                │
                     │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                │
    Read Delta V (mV)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                │
Bitline Cap C_BL (fF)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
                     │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
     Cell Cap Cs (fF)┤█████                            │
                     │█████                            │
                     └┬───────┬───────┬───────┬───────┬┘
                     0.0    62.5    125.0   187.5 250.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Range | Physical Unit | Measurement Method / Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Storage Cell Capacitance ($C_s$)** | $\ge 28$ | $25 \text{ to } 30$ | $\text{fF/cell}$ | Automated LCR / CV parametric probe |
| **Cell Retention Leakage Current** | $< 1$ | Max $\le 1.0$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Sub-femtoamp Source Measure Unit (SMU) |
| **Bitline Parasitic Capacitance ($C_{\text{BL}}$)** | $250$ | Nominal $\pm 10\%$ | $\text{fF}$ | High-frequency test structure capacitance bridge |
| **Readout Differential Signal ($\Delta V$)** | $100 \text{ to } 150$ | Range $[100, 150]$ | $\text{mV}$ | Folded-bitline Sense Amplifier probe readout |

---

### 3. Context Citations

- **Storage Cell Capacitance ($\ge 28\text{ fF}$, budget $25\text{--}30\text{ fF}$)**:
  - *Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench*: *"Capacitance Budget: Minimum 28 fF per cell ensures noise immunity against alpha-particle soft errors and bitline coupling capacitance."*
  - *Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering*: *"The storage capacitor must maintain a minimum capacitance of 25 to 30 fF (femtofarads) per cell to ensure data retention time > 64 ms at 85°C."*
- **Leakage Current Budget ($< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$)**:
  - *Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench*: *"Leakage Current Target: Sub-threshold and junction leakage must be kept below 1 fA/cell at 85°C to achieve refresh interval..."*
- **Bitline Capacitance ($C_{\text{BL}} = 250\text{ fF}$) and Signal Window ($\Delta V = 100\text{--}150\text{ mV}$)**:
  - *Source: Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout*: *"Differential Voltage Delta V = (C_s / (C_BL + C_s)) * (V_cell - V_DD/2). For typical cell capacitance C_s = 25 fF and bitline capacitance C_BL = 250 fF, signal delta V is approximately 100 mV to 150 mV."*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Integrating DC/RF die probing with interconnect sputtering and ultrasonic packaging creates severe risk of cross-contamination and mechanical pad wear. Scrub marks from tungsten probe needles during pre-packaging parametric verification can disrupt native oxide uniformity on 100 um x 100 um aluminum bond pads, degrading ultrasonic coupling during 25 um wire bonding.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Room-temperature ultrasonic Al-1%Si wedge bonding on sputtered Al-Cu interconnects requires pristine surface metallurgy. Incomplete in-situ Ar sputter-etch pre-clean before metallization leads to elevated contact resistance (Rc > 0.5 ohm/via), while excessive ultrasonic transducer power (>100 mW at 60 kHz) causes silicon cratering beneath the DRAM pad dielectric stack.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Single-sourcing 25 um 99.99% Au wire and ceramic DIP-28/40 packages with open-cavity lids introduces multi-week lead time vulnerability in Southeast Asia. Qualifying domestic Al-1% Si wedge bonding with Ablebond 84-1LMIS silver-filled conductive epoxy is essential to avoid export-control and customs bottlenecks.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Back-end assembly and probing milestones require strict segregation between metallization sputtering vacuum cycles and post-dicing die-attach curing (150°C for 60 min). Misalignment between probe card pinouts and leadframe bond-out maps risks full wafer scrap during packaging qualification.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Die shear failure and thermal thermal runaway due to >5% epoxy voiding or under-curing of Ablebond 84-1LMIS under the DRAM substrate
1. Bond pad cratering and intermetallic microcracking induced by excessive ultrasonic power (>100 mW) penetrating through the inter-layer dielectric (ILD)
1. Native aluminum oxide regrowth (Al2O3 > 4 nm) between sputtering and wire bonding due to queue time expiry, preventing ultrasonic friction welding

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-01` | **Ultrasonic Wire Bond Pull Force and Failure Mode Verification** | Dage 4000 Wire Pull & Die Shear Tester equipped with 25 um wire hook and calibrated load cell (0-100 gf) | 1. Clamp packaged DRAM unit securely onto the Dage 4000 heated workholder at 25°C. 2. Calibrate pull hook zero-point and position hook under the center span of each wire loop at mid-distance between die pad and package lead. 3. Execute vertical pull test at a hook ascent rate of 100 um/s until wire rupture occurs. 4. Record peak force in grams-force (gf) and classify failure code (mid-span break, heel break, pad lift, lead lift) across 30 consecutive wire bonds. | `All tested wires must exhibit destructive pull strength >= 4.0 gf per Mil-Std-883 Method 2011; zero occurrences of bond pad peel/lift; 100% of ruptures must occur within the wire span or neck region.` |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-02` | **Die Attach Epoxy Acoustic Void Area and Thermal Resistance Analysis** | Sonix Scanning Acoustic Microscope (C-SAM) with 100 MHz transducer and Mentor Graphics T3Ster Thermal Transient Tester | 1. Submerge ceramic package in deionized acoustic coupling bath. 2. Gate C-SAM ultrasound reflection to the die-to-substrate epoxy interface and acquire high-resolution C-scan image (5 um pixel resolution). 3. Calculate total void area percentage using automated image thresholding. 4. Mount package on temperature-controlled heat sink (25°C), wire bond VDD/VSS pins, apply 1.0 W stepped heating pulse via T3Ster, and extract thermal resistance (R_th). | `Total void area under die footprint must be < 5.0% with no single void exceeding 1.0% of total die area; junction-to-case thermal resistance R_th must be <= 5.0 °C/W.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level 3 Cleanroom Tyvek coverall with ESD grounding boots, Chemical-resistant nitrile outer gloves (8 mil) over Class 100 nitrile inner gloves, ANSI Z87.1 certified impact safety glasses with side shields, Vapor respirator (half-mask with organic vapor/P100 particulate cartridge) during epoxy dispensing
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin contact with conductive epoxy, immediately wipe off with cleanroom wipe and wash skin thoroughly with soap and copious running water for >= 15 minutes; do not use organic solvents. For eye exposure, flush eyes at emergency eyewash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open. For argon asphyxiation risk, immediately move victim to fresh air, administer supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored, and obtain prompt emergency medical assistance.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dispensing station and curing ovens must be ducted to dedicated VOC exhaust with minimum face capture velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM); sputtering chamber roughing pump exhaust must route to toxic/pyrophoric abatement system with active N2 ballast; continuous oxygen depletion monitoring sensors (alarm threshold at 19.5% O2) installed near Ar gas cylinders and sputter load locks.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Uncured conductive epoxy waste, contaminated tips, and wipes must be segregated into sealed, labeled hazardous solid waste drums and incinerated via certified environmental disposal; exhausted solvent waste collected in grounded flammable safety cans; spent sputter targets recycled via precious metal recovery stream.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Silver Flake (Conductive Epoxy Filler)** | `7440-22-4` | Electronic Grade 99.99% | `70-85% wt` |
| **Bisphenol-A Diglycidyl Ether Epoxy Resin** | `25068-38-6` | Semiconductor Grade | `10-20% wt` |
| **Argon Gas (Sputter Sourcing & Purge)** | `7440-37-1` | Ultra-High Purity 5N5 (99.9995%) | `100% vol` |
| **Isopropanol (Solvent Cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Grade | `>99.8% wt` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly diced and solvent-cleaned 180nm DRAM dies with sputtered Al-1%Si/0.5%Cu bonding pads free of organic residue, dicing slurry particulates, and ionic chlorine contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Fully attached, wire-bonded DRAM dies inside ceramic DIP cavity with hermetically sealed or temporary tape-sealed lid, passed pull test without pad delamination.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Native Al2O3 layer exceeds 3.5 nm on bonding pads, causing high-impedance cold joints, bond lift failures during ultrasonic wedging, and premature corrosion of interconnections under ambient humidity.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical and parametric qualification of DRAM die attach, 25 um ultrasonic wire bonding, and probe station packaging verification meeting Mil-Std-883 standards with zero bond lift failures and verified thermal dissipation.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `DRAM_Gen2_WireBond_PullTest_MilStd883.csv`
- [ ] `DieAttach_CSAM_Acoustic_Void_Inspection.tiff`
- [ ] `Thermal_Resistance_Rth_Packaging_Report.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Destructive wire pull force for all bonded 25 um Al-1%Si interconnect wires** | `>= 4.0 gf` | +5.0/-0.0 gf | Dage 4000 micro-tester vertical pull test per Mil-Std-883 Method 2011 |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Acoustic void percentage in Ablebond 84-1LMIS die attach layer under 180nm DRAM die** | `< 5.0%` | +0.0%/-5.0% | Sonix C-SAM acoustic reflection image processing with automated threshold area calculation |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Single-pad interconnect contact resistance between wire bond wedge and DRAM Al pad** | `<= 0.15 ohm` | +/- 0.03 ohm | Four-point Kelvin probe parametric measurement using Keithley 2450 SMU |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 30 consecutive wire bonds successfully tested with mean pull strength >= 6.5 gf and zero individual readings below 4.0 gf; acoustic void inspection confirms < 5% total interface voiding; package junction-to-case thermal resistance R_th <= 5.0 °C/W; formal engineering signoff by Back-End Packaging Lead and Quality Assurance Council.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Title: M1/M2 Metallization Sputtering & Ti/TiN Barrier Deposition Recipe Execution
- **Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > Interconnect Sputtering & Die Packaging Probe Station [Back-End Packaging] > M1/M2 Metallization Sputtering & Ti/TiN Barrier Deposition Recipe Execution [Interconnect & Thin Film Deposition]
- **Generation:** Gen 2 (µm) / 180nm
- **Action Type:** Make

---

### 1. Process Overview & Chamber Preparation
```text
[ Load Wafer & Pump Down ] ──> [ Ar Working Gas Strike ] ──> [ DC Magnetron Sputter ] ──> [ Forming Gas Anneal ]
   Base P < 2x10^-6 Torr         Ar: 3 - 5 mTorr              Power: 1.5 - 3.0 kW          400°C, 30 min (N2/H2)
```

1. **Chamber Evacuation & Base Vacuum:**
   - Transfer wafer into the PVD load lock and pump down main vacuum chamber using turbomolecular or cryopump until base pressure reaches **$< 2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$** to suppress oxygen incorporation.
2. **Process Gas Introduction:**
   - Introduce ultra-high-purity Argon gas (**$\text{Ar } 99.999\%$ / 5N**) into the sputtering chamber.
   - Throttle gate valve / mass flow control to stabilize working process pressure between **$3\text{ to } 5\text{ mTorr}$**.
3. **Substrate Stage & Target Alignment:**
   - Engage substrate stage heating to promote film step coverage over high-aspect contacts (bitline and wordline straps).
   - Verify cathode target: **$99.999\%$ (5N) Aluminum target** (or Al-0.5% Cu alloy).
4. **DC Magnetron Sputtering Deposition:**
   - Ignite plasma and ramp planar DC magnetron power supply to **$1.5\text{ to } 3.0\text{ kW}$**.
   - Maintain controlled deposition rate calibrated at **$50\text{ to } 100\text{ nm/min}$**.
   - Deposition timer set to reach nominal Metal-1 (M1) physical thickness target of **$350\text{ nm}$** ($\pm 5\%$).
5. **Post-Metal Anneal (Forming Gas Treatment):**
   - Transfer metallized wafer to furnace/RTA chamber.
   - Run post-metal anneal under forming gas mixture (**$95\%\text{ N}_2 / 5\%\text{ H}_2$**) at **$400^\circ\text{C}$** for **$30\text{ minutes}$**.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Limit | Measurement Tool / Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Chamber Base Vacuum** | $< 2 \times 10^{-6}$ | Max $2 \times 10^{-6}$ | High-vacuum Penning/Ion Gauge ($\text{Torr}$) |
| **Process Working Pressure** | $3 \text{ to } 5$ | $\pm 0.2$ | Capacitance Manometer ($\text{mTorr}$) |
| **M1 Film Thickness** | $350$ | $\pm 5\%$ ($332.5 - 367.5$) | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / Profilometer ($\text{nm}$) |
| **Post-Anneal Sheet Resistance ($R_s$)** | $< 0.08$ | Upper bound $0.08$ | Four-Point Probe ($\Omega/\Box$) |

---

### 3. Verified Literature Citations

- **Source:** *Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects*
  - Vacuum pump-down target $< 2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$ via turbomolecular/cryopump.
  - Sputtering gas Ar $99.999\%$ at $3 - 5\text{ mTorr}$ working pressure.
  - $99.999\%$ (5N) Al target driven by planar DC magnetron at $1.5 - 3.0\text{ kW}$.
  - Deposition rate $50 - 100\text{ nm/min}$, target M1 thickness $350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$.
  - Post-metal anneal: $400^\circ\text{C}$ for $30\text{ min}$ in forming gas ($\text{N}_2/\text{H}_2\text{ } 95/5$), achieving $R_s < 0.08\text{ }\Omega/\Box$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Pumping down to <2x10^-6 Torr with cryo or turbomolecular pumping is mandatory to prevent oxygen and water vapor background partial pressures from forming resistive native Al2O3 inclusions within the M1 bulk. The DC magnetron sputtering sequence must enforce an in-situ RF soft-etch or degas before Ti deposition, otherwise contact resistance to active n+/p+ silicon and poly-Si wordlines will experience severe dispersion.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Direct Al deposition onto contact vias without a conformal Ti/TiN diffusion barrier induces catastrophic silicon spiking during the 400°C forming gas post-metal anneal (PMA). The Ti layer (20-30 nm) provides contact silicidation (TiSi2) for low-ohmic contact, while the reactive-sputtered TiN (40-60 nm in Ar/N2 ambient) serves as the atomic diffusion barrier against Al-Si interdiffusion and electromigration.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring 5N (99.999%) purity planar targets for both Al-0.5%Cu and Ti targets with verified low-uranium/thorium background alpha-emission is critical to prevent soft errors in DRAM cell arrays. Domestic sourcing lead-times for ultra-high purity (UHP) Ar (5N5) and N2 gases must include inline moisture/oxygen point-of-use (POU) purifiers to guarantee <1 ppb O2/H2O levels.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Target erosion profiles and deposition rate drifts directly modulate M1 sheet resistance and line thickness, impacting downstream lithography depth of focus (DOF) and metal dry etch endpoints. The recipe execution must integrate quartz crystal microbalance (QCM) monitoring and scheduled 4-point probe sheet resistance verification per 25-wafer lot.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Al-Si spiking through the shallow source/drain junctions during 400°C forming gas anneal caused by TiN barrier pinholes or stoichiometric sub-nitridation.
1. High via contact resistance and unrepeatable bitline RC delays due to vacuum break/ambient native oxide growth between pre-clean and Ti/TiN barrier sputtering.
1. Stress-induced voiding or delamination of Al/TiN bi-layers caused by substrate stage thermal mismatch or uncontrolled compressive/tensile plasma stress.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-1-01` | **M1 Post-Anneal Sheet Resistance & Film Uniformity Verification** | Four-Point Probe (FPP) Resistivity Mapping System (e.g., CDE ResMap 178) and Cross-Sectional FE-SEM | 1. Load wafer onto the automated four-point probe vacuum chuck. 2. Measure sheet resistance at 49 points with a 5mm edge exclusion using dual-configuration probe method. 3. Calculate mean sheet resistance (R_s) and wafer non-uniformity (1-sigma percentage). 4. Perform cross-sectional FE-SEM cleavage at wafer center to verify total metal stack thickness. | `Pass if mean sheet resistance R_s < 0.080 Ohm/sq, 1-sigma non-uniformity <= 3.5%, and total Al-0.5%Cu physical thickness measures 350 nm ± 17.5 nm (±5%).` |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-1-02` | **Ti/TiN Barrier Contact Silicidation & Junction Leakage Current Test** | Semiconductor Parameter Analyzer (e.g., Keysight B1500A) coupled with Cascade Microtech semi-automated probe station | 1. Place wafer on shielded thermal chuck at 25°C. 2. Establish Kelvin four-terminal contact with probe needles on force/sense pads of 1,000-via chain. 3. Sweep DC voltage from -1.0V to +1.0V with 10mV step; record I-V curve to compute specific contact resistance. 4. Apply reverse bias of 2.5V across n+/p-well diode structures and record reverse leakage current. | `Pass if contact resistance per contact via is <= 15 Ohm/via with linear Ohmic behavior (R^2 > 0.999), and junction reverse leakage current density at 2.5V reverse bias is < 1.0 nA/cm^2 (indicating zero Al-Si spiking).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom rated nitrile double-gloves with chemical splash-resistant outer gloves during target cleaning, ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-filtering safety glasses/face shield, Conductive ESD cleanroom smock, ESD boots, and grounded wrist strap, Half-mask elastomeric particulate respirator (P100) during chamber mechanical bead-blasting and shield cleanout
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of asphyxiation from inert gas (Ar/N2) release, immediately remove victim to fresh air and administer supplemental oxygen or CPR if breathing has stopped. In case of high-voltage DC arc shock from magnetron cathode power supply (up to 1 kV DC), isolate power main immediately before touching victim, assess for cardiac arrhythmias, initiate CPR/AED, and contact emergency medical services immediately. For thermal burns from hot substrate stage (300°C), cool with running clean water for 20 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous dedicated scrubbed process exhaust providing minimum 50 Pa negative draft on vacuum pump foreline exhausts. Continuous room-level optical oxygen depletion monitoring (low alarm at 19.5% O2, high alarm evacuation at 18.0% O2) linked to automatic Ar/N2 cylinder pneumatic shutoff valves. Interlocked toxic/combustible gas monitoring for forming gas (H2 < 1% lower explosive limit interlock).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent sputtering targets and contaminated copper backing plates must be treated as solid heavy-metal/reclaimable metal electronic waste and dispatched to certified metallurgical recycling facilities. Particulate aluminum/titanium dust recovered from deposition chamber shield cleaning must be vacuumed using HEPA/explosion-proof vacuums and wetted with mineral oil to mitigate combustible pyrophoric metal dust explosion risks.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Argon (Sputtering Process Gas)** | `7440-37-1` | Research Grade 5N5 (99.9995%) | `100% Compressed Gas` |
| **Nitrogen (Reactive Sputter & Purge Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity 6N (99.9999%) | `100% Compressed Gas` |
| **Hydrogen (Forming Gas Component)** | `1333-74-0` | Electronic Grade 5N (99.999%) | `5.0% in Nitrogen Balance` |
| **Titanium (Sputtering Target)** | `7440-32-6` | Electronic Grade 4N8 (99.998%) | `100% Solid Target` |
| **Aluminum-Copper (Sputtering Target)** | `7429-90-5` | 5N (99.999% trace metals basis) | `99.5% Al / 0.5% Cu by weight` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-metal contacts wet-etched in 100:1 Dilute HF (DHF), rinsed with 18.2 MOhm-cm DI water, dried with hot N2, with native oxide thickness verified < 0.5 nm.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Continuous Ti(25nm)/TiN(50nm)/Al-0.5%Cu(350nm) metallization stack without ambient pitting, moisture condensation, or surface particulate density > 0.05/cm^2.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding Q-time before Ti barrier deposition causes native silicon dioxide (SiO2) re-growth in open contact vias exceeding 1.2 nm, leading to contact non-ohmic rectification, threshold shift, and multi-kiloohm contact resistance failures.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical vapor deposition and post-anneal validation of the M1/M2 Ti/TiN/Al-0.5%Cu metallization stack on 180nm DRAM test wafers demonstrating sheet resistance R_s < 0.08 Ohm/sq, complete barrier integrity against Al-Si spiking, and uniform 350 nm bulk film deposition.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `M1_Metallization_FourPointProbe_Rs_Map.csv`
- [ ] `TiN_Barrier_CrossSection_FESEM_Analysis.pdf`
- [ ] `ViaChain_JunctionLeakage_KelvinContact_Data.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **M1 Post-Metal Anneal Mean Sheet Resistance** | `0.072 Ohm/sq` | < 0.080 Ohm/sq | Automated 49-point 4-point probe mapping across 100mm/150mm monitor wafer |
| `ASSERT-02` | **M1 Al-0.5%Cu Deposited Film Physical Thickness** | `350 nm` | ± 17.5 nm (±5%) | Cross-sectional cleavage Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FE-SEM) |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Specific Contact Resistance per 0.25um Contact Via** | `11.5 Ohm/via` | <= 15.0 Ohm/via | Kelvin 4-wire DC resistance measurement on 1,000 contact via chain test structure |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 49 wafer mapping points yield R_s < 0.080 Ohm/sq with 1-sigma non-uniformity <= 3.5%, cross-sectional FE-SEM reveals zero TiN micro-cracking or Al-Si spiking interfaces, and the 1,000-via test chain exhibits 100% continuity with contact resistance <= 15 Ohm/via after 400°C forming gas anneal.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Ti/TiN Adhesion & Diffusion Barrier Sputter Deposition

- **Node Title**: Ti/TiN Adhesion & Diffusion Barrier Sputter Deposition
- **Context**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > Interconnect Sputtering & Die Packaging Probe Station > M1/M2 Metallization Sputtering & Ti/TiN Barrier Deposition Recipe Execution
- **Generation**: Gen 2 (µm)
- **Action Type**: Make
- **Knowledge Base Persistence**: Captured in [`docs/knowledge/sop-ti-tin-barrier-sputter.md`](docs/knowledge/sop-ti-tin-barrier-sputter.md) per local repository protocol.

---

### 1. Process Flow Diagram
