---

### 3. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Chamber Evacuation & Base Vacuum Verification**:
   - Transfer wafer batch into the high-vacuum PVD load lock and shuttle to the process chamber.
   - Initiate high-vacuum pump-down using the turbomolecular/cryopump system until base pressure reaches **$< 2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$** to suppress residual oxygen and water vapor incorporation.
2. **Substrate Heating & Stage Stabilization**:
   - Ramp substrate stage heater to thermal stabilization temperature to ensure uniform step coverage across dense bitline/wordline contact arrays (pitch $360\text{ nm to }400\text{ nm}$).
3. **Plasma Ignition & Gas Mass Flow Control**:
   - Introduce ultra-high-purity Argon gas (**99.999% / 5N purity**) through mass flow controllers (MFC).
   - Throttle gate valve to regulate working chamber pressure within **$3\text{ to }5\text{ mTorr}$**.
4. **DC Magnetron Sputter Deposition (Ti Adhesion Layer)**:
   - Strike DC magnetron plasma onto high-purity target using the DC magnetron power supply operating at **$1.5\text{ to }3.0\text{ kW}$**.
   - Maintain calibrated deposition rate within **$50\text{ to }100\text{ nm/min}$** to deposit the initial conformal titanium (Ti) contact/adhesion layer directly over the drain contact and W-plug interface.
5. **Reactive Sputter Deposition (TiN Diffusion Barrier Layer)**:
   - Introduce high-purity reactive Nitrogen gas into the Ar stream while maintaining the working pressure at **$3\text{ to }5\text{ mTorr}$** and DC magnetron power at **$1.5\text{ to }3.0\text{ kW}$**.
   - Execute reactive deposition to form the stoichiometric TiN barrier layer above the Ti underlayer to prevent contact junction spiking and migration.
6. **Post-Deposition Cool Down & Unload**:
   - Extinguish plasma, shut off process gas flow, and idle substrate under high vacuum until temperature drops below oxidation threshold.
   - Transfer wafer back to load lock and pump/purge before progressing to Al-0.5% Cu metallization deposition (target $350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$).

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Physical Unit | Inspection / Measurement Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Base Vacuum Pressure** | $< 2 \times 10^{-6}$ | $\text{Torr}$ | In-situ Ion Gauge / Penning Gauge |
| **Process Working Pressure** | $3\text{ to }5$ | $\text{mTorr}$ | Capacitance Manometer |
| **DC Magnetron Power** | $1.5\text{ to }3.0$ | $\text{kW}$ | Power Supply Telemetry / RF-DC Controller |
| **Deposition Rate** | $50\text{ to }100$ | $\text{nm/min}$ | Quartz Crystal Microbalance (QCM) / Ellipsometry |
| **Post-Anneal Sheet Resistance ($R_s$)** | $< 0.08$ | $\Omega/\Box$ | Four-Point Probe (after $400^\circ\text{C}$, $30\text{ min}$ forming gas anneal) |

---

### 5. Context Citations

- **[Source: Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects]**: Base vacuum pump down below $2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$ via turbomolecular/cryopump; Ar 99.999% (5N) at $3\text{ to }5\text{ mTorr}$ working pressure; DC magnetron power at $1.5\text{ to }3.0\text{ kW}$; deposition rate at $50\text{ to }100\text{ nm/min}$; metal-1 stack target thickness $350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$; post-metal anneal in forming gas ($95/5\ \text{N}_2/\text{H}_2$ at $400^\circ\text{C}$ for $30\text{ min}$) yielding sheet resistance $R_s < 0.08\ \Omega/\Box$.
- **[Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]**: 180nm technology node layout topology ($8F^2/6F^2$ folded bitline), access transistor channel dimensions ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$), and tungsten plug (W-plug) contact integration.
- **[Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering]**: 180nm interconnect pitches ($360\text{ nm to }400\text{ nm}$) requiring high step coverage and stable diffusion barrier integration.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Integration with downstream Al-0.5% Cu interconnect metallization requires precise control over the Ti/TiN bi-layer stack stress and contact plug resistance. If the base vacuum fails to achieve < 2e-6 Torr, interstitial oxygen incorporation into the underlying 15 nm Ti adhesion layer will degrade ohmic contact to n+/p+ silicon and silicided contacts, while excessive compressive stress in the reactive TiN diffusion barrier (target 35 nm) will induce micro-delamination and dielectric cracking at contact via sidewalls.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: DC magnetron sputtering of the Ti adhesion layer must be executed with ultra-pure Ar (99.999%), followed immediately in-situ by reactive DC magnetron sputtering in an Ar/N2 ambient for stoichiometric TiN without vacuum break. Nitridation poisoning of the Ti target must be stabilized using closed-loop mass flow or plasma emission monitoring to guarantee the golden (111)-preferred orientation TiN phase, which acts as a dense diffusion barrier preventing Al spiking into shallow junction contacts during the 400°C post-metal anneal.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: High-purity 5N (99.999%) Titanium planar sputtering targets with certified low-oxygen (< 250 ppm) and low-iron (< 5 ppm) metallurgy must be secured alongside dual-source semiconductor-grade Ar (6N) and N2 (6N) gases. Single-source dependency on specialized backing plate bonding assemblies and long lead times for replacement cryopump regenerators represent primary schedule vulnerability points for pilot line execution.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Target qualification requires establishing reproducible target sputter erosion profiling and deposition rate calibrations within 12 shifts. Any unmitigated chamber flaking or particle shedding exceeding 30 particles at > 0.2 µm per 150mm wafer will shut down the front-end metallization track, impacting downstream M1 lithography and electrical parametric probe milestones.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Target poisoning-induced non-stoichiometric TiNx leading to Al junction spiking and junction leakage failure during 400°C post-metal anneal
1. Interfacial native oxide regrowth or oxygen contamination in Ti layer causing unacceptably high specific contact resistance (Rc > 50 Ohm/via)
1. High intrinsic film stress causing edge peeling and delamination of the Ti/TiN/AlCu composite stack at via edges

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-1-1-01` | **In-Line Sheet Resistance and Thickness Verification of Ti/TiN Bi-Layer** | Four-Point Probe (FPP) Resistivity Mapping Tool (e.g. KLA-Tencor ResMap) and Spectroscopic Ellipsometer / X-ray Reflectivity (XRR) | 1. Load monitor wafer into PVD degas chamber and preheat at 200°C for 60 seconds under vacuum. 2. Transfer under ultra-high vacuum (< 1e-7 Torr transfer) to PVD module. 3. Strike DC magnetron plasma on 99.999% Ti target at 2.0 kW, Ar flow 35 sccm, working pressure 3.5 mTorr; deposit 15 nm Ti adhesion layer. 4. Introduce reactive N2 at calibrated 25 sccm with Ar at 25 sccm (total 50 sccm, 4.0 mTorr) at 2.5 kW; deposit 35 nm TiN diffusion barrier in-situ without vacuum break. 5. Cool substrate under high vacuum and transfer wafer to load-lock. 6. Execute 49-point four-point probe sheet resistance mapping. 7. Measure thickness of individual layers using Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / XRR at center and 4 radial points. | `Total bi-layer thickness = 50.0 nm ± 2.5 nm (Ti: 15.0 nm ± 1.5 nm, TiN: 35.0 nm ± 2.0 nm); Sheet resistance Rs within 35.0 to 45.0 Ohm/sq; Sheet resistance uniformity (1-sigma) < 2.5% across 49 measurement sites.` |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-1-1-02` | **Thermal Barrier Integrity and Al-Spike Prevention Verification** | Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry (SIMS) / Focused Ion Beam Scanning Electron Microscopy (FIB-SEM) and Automated Defect Inspection Station | 1. Subject annealed sample to selective chemical wet strip of Al-Cu overlayer using phosphoric/acetic/nitric (PAN) etch solution at 45°C. 2. Inspect underlying TiN surface across 20 high-density contact via arrays using high-resolution SEM for barrier rupture, pitting, or micro-voids. 3. Prepare cross-sectional lamella across via bottom using FIB and examine under SEM/TEM for Si/Al interdiffusion. 4. Perform SIMS depth profile tracking Al, Ti, N, and Si atomic distribution across the junction interface. | `Zero visible Al-Si spike pits or barrier rupture defects across 100 inspected contact plugs; SIMS profile confirms Al diffusion into underlying Si substrate is below the detection threshold (< 1e16 atoms/cm3) at a depth 10 nm beneath the original silicide/Si interface.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloving required during chamber maintenance), ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash safety goggles and full-face shield, Flame-resistant cleanroom suit (Nomex/ESD blend), P100 HEPA air-purifying half-mask respirator during target handling and chamber shield cleans
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For cryogenic burns or pressurized gas exposure: Flush affected area immediately with tepid water (105-115°F/40-46°C); do not rub affected tissue. For inhalation of pyrophoric/toxic chamber byproduct particulates (finely divided Ti dust): Evacuate personnel to fresh air immediately, administer oxygen if breathing is labored, and obtain medical evaluation. For high-voltage DC magnetron shock: Shut off main emergency power off (EPO), verify victim is clear of energized parts, initiate CPR/AED if unresponsive, and summon emergency medical personnel.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous mechanical scrubbed exhaust on PVD roughing dry pumps and cryopump purge lines maintaining negative static pressure of >= 1.5 in. w.g.; chamber clean room ambient certified Class 100 with >= 60 air changes per hour; ambient real-time O2 deficiency monitoring with audible and strobe alarms set at 19.5% O2 threshold.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent Titanium targets and contaminated aluminum/stainless chamber shields must be vacuumed using explosion-proof HEPA vacuums rated for combustible metal dusts; metal scrap and Ti flake debris must be immersed in inert mineral oil or passivated under controlled water quenching before disposal as hazardous reactive solid waste per local semiconductor regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Titanium (solid target)** | `7440-32-6` | 5N (99.999% trace metals basis) | `100%` |
| **Argon (compressed gas)** | `7440-37-1` | Ultra-High Purity Grade 6.0 (99.9999%) | `100%` |
| **Nitrogen (compressed gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity Grade 6.0 (99.9999%) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-metal clean (DHF 100:1 etch or in-situ Ar soft sputter-clean) completed; contact via bottom exposed with native SiO2 thickness <= 0.4 nm and zero moisture condensation.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Stoichiometric, golden-phase TiN barrier layer deposited under vacuum; ready for immediate load-lock transfer to M1 Al-0.5% Cu sputter module without exposure to atmospheric oxygen.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Native oxide reformation (SiO2 > 1.2 nm) and atmospheric moisture absorption at via bottoms causing high contact resistance and adhesion failure; ambient oxidation of freshly sputtered TiN resulting in TiO2 surface dielectric skin that degrades Al/TiN interface conductivity and electromigration resistance.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful DC magnetron sputter deposition of an ultra-clean 15 nm Ti adhesion layer followed in-situ by a reactive 35 nm TiN diffusion barrier on 150mm DRAM wafers, meeting tight thickness uniformity, stoichiometric composition, low sheet resistance, and complete barrier integrity against Al diffusion.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `ti_tin_fpp_sheet_resistance_map.csv`
- [ ] `pvd_chamber_recipe_log_telemetry.pdf`
- [ ] `contact_via_tem_eds_cross_section.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Total Ti/TiN Bi-Layer Physical Thickness** | `50.0 nm` | ± 2.5 nm | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / Cross-Sectional TEM at wafer center and 4 edge points (10mm edge exclusion) |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Bi-Layer Post-Deposition Sheet Resistance (Rs)** | `39.5 Ohm/sq` | ± 4.5 Ohm/sq | Automated 49-point Four-Point Probe resistivity measurement system |
| `ASSERT-03` | **TiN Barrier Microdefect and Flake Particle Density** | `0 particles/cm2 (size >= 0.2 µm)` | + 0.05 particles/cm2 | Darkfield Laser Surface Particle Scanner (e.g. KLA Surfscan) |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Engineering sign-off requires: 1) Three consecutive qualification wafers achieving sheet resistance between 35.0 and 44.0 Ohm/sq with 1-sigma radial uniformity < 2.5%; 2) Cross-sectional TEM confirming Ti thickness at 15 ± 1.5 nm and TiN thickness at 35 ± 2.0 nm with conformal sidewall step coverage >= 30% in 180nm contact vias; 3) Zero Al-spiking observed following 400°C 30-minute forming gas anneal.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Ti/TiN Sputter Target Conditioning & Vacuum Base Pressure Qualification
**Scope / Process Node:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (Interconnect & Thin Film Deposition — Gen 2 / Back-End Metallization)  
**Action Type:** Make / Equipment Qualification  

---

### 1. Process Overview & Objectives
This SOP outlines the protocol for verifying ultra-high vacuum (UHV) base pressure integrity and executing pre-sputter target conditioning for Titanium (Ti) and Titanium Nitride (TiN) adhesion/diffusion barrier deposition. Pre-conditioning removes native oxides, atmospheric adsorbates, and nitrided target poisons, ensuring reproducible work function, low contact resistance, and prevention of oxygen incorporation prior to primary metallization (M1/M2).

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

```
  [1. Cryo / Turbo High-Vacuum Pumpdown]
                   │
                   ▼
  [2. Base Vacuum Qualification & Leak-Up Rate Test]
                   │
                   ▼
  [3. High-Purity Ar Gas Flow Stabilization]
                   │
                   ▼
  [4. Shutter-Closed Target Pre-Sputter Conditioning]
                   │
                   ▼
  [5. Plasma Stability & DC Power Verification]
```

#### Step 1: Chamber Roughing & High-Vacuum Pumpdown
1. Verify chamber seals, loadlock gate valve isolation, and cryopump/turbomolecular pump operational status.
2. Initiate roughing pumpdown to crossover pressure (~50–100 mTorr), then actuate the high-vacuum gate valve to engage the turbomolecular pump or cryopump.
3. Pump down the deposition chamber continuously until the high-vacuum ionization gauge confirms the base pressure threshold.

#### Step 2: Vacuum Base Pressure Qualification & Outgassing Verification
1. Measure chamber ultimate base pressure via calibrated ionization gauge. Verify base pressure achieves `< 2.0 × 10⁻⁶ Torr`.
2. *(Optional/Recommended)* Close chamber high-vacuum isolation valve for 180 seconds to perform a rate-of-rise (leak-up) check to distinguish real atmospheric vacuum leaks from chamber wall outgassing.

#### Step 3: Process Gas Delivery & Working Pressure Stabilization
1. Introduce 99.999% (5N) high-purity Argon (Ar) process gas through the calibrated mass flow controller (MFC).
2. Throttle the downstream gate valve / APC (Automatic Pressure Controller) to establish and stabilize the sputtering working pressure between `3.0 mTorr and 5.0 mTorr`.

#### Step 4: Shutter-Closed Pre-Sputter Target Conditioning (Burn-in)
1. Ensure the substrate shield / target shutter is fully closed over the substrate stage to isolate production wafers/platens from cross-contamination.
2. Ignite the DC magnetron plasma on the target.
3. Ramp DC magnetron power supply through a stepped conditioning sequence:
   - 0.5 kW for 60 seconds (plasma strike and stabilization)
   - 1.0 kW for 60 seconds (desorption of surface moisture/adsorbates)
   - 1.5 kW to 3.0 kW for 120 seconds (complete target surface clean-up and oxide strip)

#### Step 5: DC Electrical Characteristics & Plasma Extinction
1. Verify reflected power, target cathode voltage, and current stability at setpoint power.
2. Extinguish DC plasma or transition directly into reactive gas flow ($N_2$) for TiN barrier deposition recipe execution.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value & Tolerance | Unit | Measurement Method / Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Chamber Base Vacuum Pressure** | $< 2.0 \times 10^{-6}$ | $\text{Torr}$ | Calibrated Hot/Cold Cathode Ionization Gauge |
| **Sputter Working Gas Pressure** | $3.0 \text{ to } 5.0$ | $\text{mTorr}$ | Capacitance Manometer |
| **Argon (Ar) Gas Purity** | $\ge 99.999$ (5N) | $\%$ | Certified Gas Delivery Supply / RGA |
| **Target Conditioning DC Power Range** | $1.5 \text{ to } 3.0$ | $\text{kW}$ | DC Magnetron Power Supply Controller |

---

### 4. Literature Source Citations
- **Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects:**
  - *Chamber Base Pressure:* Vacuum chamber must pump down below $2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$ using turbomolecular or cryopump to prevent oxygen incorporation.
  - *Process Gas:* Sputtering process gas is high-purity Argon (Ar 99.999%) maintained at $3\text{ to }5\text{ mTorr}$ working pressure.
  - *Power Supply Specification:* DC magnetron power supply operating at $1.5\text{ to }3.0\text{ kW}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: PVD chamber high-vacuum base pressure must reliably reach < 2.0x10^-6 Torr via turbomolecular/cryopump prior to plasma ignition. Any chamber outgassing, virtual leaks from shield blind screw holes, or water desorption will degrade titanium target burn-in, resulting in excessive target poisoning and inconsistent DC discharge impedance.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Titanium (Ti) is an aggressive getter material. Pre-sputtering against a closed shutter (or dummy wafer) is essential to strip native surface oxides (TiO2/TiOx) from the target face. Without adequate target burn-in under pure Ar (3-5 mTorr at 1.5-2.5 kW), initial film deposition will inject oxygen contaminants into the barrier layer, driving specific contact resistance (Rc) and sheet resistance out of 180nm DRAM specifications.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: High-purity 99.999% (5N) circular planar Ti targets and ultra-high purity 6N Argon gas represent critical single-source lead-time bottlenecks. Improper burn-in recipes risk target micro-arcing and premature race-track erosion, significantly lowering target utilization efficiency and increasing production tool downtime.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Target conditioning and base pressure qualification must complete within an allocated 90-minute maintenance window per campaign to preserve downstream line pacing for M1/M2 metallization without creating front-end queue stalls.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Incomplete target burn-in leading to oxygen/nitrogen contamination spikes in the initial Ti barrier seed layer
1. Vacuum leak or cryopump saturation resulting in base pressure stalling above 2.0x10^-6 Torr and elevated H2O partial pressure
1. DC magnetron arc events caused by dielectric oxide breakdown on unconditioned target edges, inducing particle contamination

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-1-1-1-01` | **Cryo/Turbo High-Vacuum Chamber Base Pressure & Outgassing Rate Qualification** | Calibrated Bayard-Alpert Ionization Gauge and In-Situ Residual Gas Analyzer (RGA, 1-100 amu) | 1. Monitor chamber pressure pump-down trajectory until stabilized. 2. Record ultimate base pressure reading from the Bayard-Alpert ion gauge. 3. Execute RGA scan (m/z 1-50) to evaluate H2O (m/z 18), O2 (m/z 32), and N2 (m/z 28) partial pressures. 4. Perform rate-of-rise (RoR) test by closing the high-vacuum gate valve for 120 seconds and measuring delta P / delta t. | `Ultimate base pressure <= 2.0x10^-6 Torr; RGA water partial pressure (m/z 18) <= 5.0x10^-7 Torr; rate-of-rise <= 1.5x10^-5 Torr/min.` |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-1-1-1-02` | **Ti Sputter Target DC Magnetron Conditioning & Discharge Impedance Stability** | Oscilloscope-monitored DC Magnetron Power Supply (kW/V/I telemetry), Ar MFC (0-100 sccm), Optical Emission Spectrometer (OES) | 1. Initiate ramped DC pre-sputtering step-wise: 500W for 3 min, 1000W for 3 min, 2000W for 10 min. 2. Log arc count and discharge voltage stability at 2000W over the final 5 minutes. 3. Track Ti-I (365.3 nm) and O-I (777.4 nm) optical emission peak intensities to verify complete native oxide stripping. | `Discharge voltage variation <= +/- 3.0 V at 2000W; arc rate < 2 arcs/minute during final 5 minutes; OES intensity ratio I(O 777nm) / I(Ti 365nm) <= 0.01.` |

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Ti Adhesion & Reactive TiN Diffusion Barrier Sputter Deposition Recipe Execution

**Document ID:** `SOP-PVD-180NM-TI-TIN-001`  
**Classification:** Interconnect & Thin Film Deposition  
**Technology Node:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (Gen 2 µm)  
**Process Action:** Make  

---

### 1. Process Overview & Objective
This procedure details the sequential DC planar magnetron sputter deposition of a titanium (Ti) adhesion layer followed by reactive sputter deposition of a titanium nitride (TiN) diffusion barrier on contact vias and metal-1 (M1) interconnect trenches prior to Al/Al-Cu metallization. The Ti underlayer provides ohmic contact and adhesion to underlying dielectric/silicon, while stoichiometric TiN prevents aluminum spiking and interdiffusion into silicon junctions or contact plugs.

---

### 2. Equipment, Consumables & Target Specifications
- **PVD Platform:** Multi-chamber cluster tool or sequential load-lock DC magnetron sputtering system equipped with turbomolecular/cryopump vacuum units.
- **Sputter Targets:** High-purity 99.999% (5N) Titanium (Ti) target.
- **Process Gases:** 
  - Ultra-high-purity Argon ($\text{Ar}$, $99.999\%$)
  - Ultra-high-purity Nitrogen ($\text{N}_2$, $99.999\%$)
- **Forming Gas (Pre/Post-metal support):** $\text{N}_2/\text{H}_2\ (95/5)$.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

#### Step 1: Pre-Deposition Chamber Pump-Down & Base Pressure Verification
1. Load 180nm patterned wafers (post-contact etch / clean) into the load-lock cassette.
2. Evacuate the main deposition chamber using the turbomolecular/cryopumping system.
3. Verify baseline chamber pressure drops below **$2 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{Torr}$** before opening process isolation gate valves to prevent oxygen and moisture incorporation.

#### Step 2: In-Situ Substrate Degas & Pre-Sputter Target Conditioning
1. Transfer wafer to the degas / substrate heating stage.
2. Ignite the Ti planar DC magnetron target behind a closed shutter with pure Argon at working pressure ($3\text{ to }5\ \text{mTorr}$) at $1.5\ \text{kW}$ for 60 seconds to strip native oxide/contaminants from the target surface.

#### Step 3: Pure Ti Adhesion Layer Sputter Deposition
1. Set chamber process gas to pure $\text{Ar}$ ($99.999\%$) and stabilize working pressure between **$3\ \text{mTorr}$ and $5\ \text{mTorr}$**.
2. Ramp DC magnetron power supply on the Ti target to **$1.5\ \text{kW}\text{ to }3.0\ \text{kW}$**.
3. Open target shutter to deposit the Ti adhesion liner onto the contact floors and sidewalls (calibrated deposition rate: $50\text{ to }100\ \text{nm/min}$).

#### Step 4: Reactive TiN Diffusion Barrier Sputter Deposition
1. Maintain DC magnetron power ($1.5\ \text{kW}\text{ to }3.0\ \text{kW}$) on the Ti target.
2. Introduce controlled reactive $\text{N}_2$ flow alongside $\text{Ar}$ carrier gas into the plasma discharge, maintaining overall sputtering working pressure at **$3\text{ to }5\ \text{mTorr}$**.
3. Deposit stoichiometric TiN barrier layer over the Ti adhesion film.
4. Extinguish DC plasma, ramp down magnetron power, and pump purge chamber with $\text{Ar}$.

#### Step 5: Post-Deposition Transfer & Metrology Cue
1. Transfer wafer to the cooling station in vacuum or proceed directly to cluster M1 metallization (Al-0.5% Cu deposition targeting $350\ \text{nm} \pm 5\%$).
2. Run post-metal anneal verification cycle using forming gas ($\text{N}_2/\text{H}_2\ 95/5$ at $400^\circ\text{C}$ for 30 minutes) when evaluating full stack contact and sheet resistance.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Specification | Physical Units | Verification Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Chamber Base Vacuum Pressure** | $< 2 \times 10^{-6}$ | $\text{Torr}$ | In-situ Cold Cathode / Ion Gauge |
| **Sputtering Process Working Pressure** | $3 \text{ to } 5$ | $\text{mTorr}$ | Capacitance Manometer |
| **DC Magnetron Power Delivery** | $1.5 \text{ to } 3.0$ | $\text{kW}$ | DC Power Supply Controller Log |
| **Sub-threshold & Junction Leakage Limit** | $< 1$ | $\text{fA/cell (at } 85^\circ\text{C)}$ | Electrical Parametric Tester / Probe Station |

---

### 5. Context Citations
- **Vacuum Base Pressure ($< 2 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{Torr}$), Working Pressure ($3\text{ to }5\ \text{mTorr}$), DC Power ($1.5\text{ to }3.0\ \text{kW}$), Target Purity ($99.999\%$), Deposition Rate ($50\text{ to }100\ \text{nm/min}$), and Post-Metal Anneal ($400^\circ\text{C}$, 30 min, $\text{N}_2/\text{H}_2\ 95/5$):**  
  *Source: Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects*
- **Bitline Contact Integration, Shared Memory Cell Geometry, & Junction Leakage Threshold ($< 1\ \text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$):**  
  *Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: In-situ sequential deposition of Ti (adhesion) and reactive TiN (diffusion barrier) within an integrated multi-station PVD cluster tool is critical. Exposing the 20-30 nm Ti underlayer to ambient atmosphere prior to TiN reactive sputtering will instantly grow native TiO2 (rutile/anatase), which dramatically spikes contact resistance (Rc) into silicon/silicide active regions and degrades ohmic interface integrity.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Target poisoning hysteresis during reactive DC magnetron sputtering of Ti in Ar/N2 ambient requires closed-loop optical emission spectroscopy (OES) or fast plasma voltage feedback control. Operating in the transition mode between metallic and nitrided target states is essential to achieve stoichiometric TiN with (200) preferred crystallographic orientation, low residual compressive stress (< 1.5 GPa), and robust barrier efficiency against aluminum spike diffusion during 400°C post-metal anneal.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Requires 99.999% (5N) high-purity Titanium planar targets with controlled grain size (< 50 µm) and ultra-high purity process gases (Ar 99.9999% 6N and N2 99.9999% 6N). Point-of-use getter purifiers must be validated for nitrogen gas feed to prevent uncontrolled TiOxNy formation, which degrades the diffusion barrier against Al-Cu interdiffusion.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: PVD cluster chamber preventive maintenance and shield replacement schedules must be tied directly to cumulative sputtered kilowatt-hours (kWh). Flaking of accumulated TiN film from chamber shields generates killer particle defects directly landing on 180nm contact vias, directly impacting die yield across 150mm/200mm pilot line wafers.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Target poisoning runaway during reactive TiN deposition causing micro-arcing, target nodule ejection, and high particle density on contact vias.
1. Aluminum junction spiking due to non-stoichiometric, pinhole-rich, or under-thick TiN barrier failing during the 400°C forming gas post-metal anneal.
1. High contact resistance or contact open failure caused by uncontrolled interface oxidation of the Ti film prior to TiN cap deposition.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-1-1-2-01` | **Ti and Reactive TiN Film Thickness and Sheet Resistance Uniformity Verification** | Four-point probe (4PP) resistivity mapping tool (49-point map, 3mm edge exclusion) and spectroscopic ellipsometer / X-ray reflectometry (XRR) | 1. Load bare Si monitor wafer into loadlock and pump down to transfer pressure (< 5.0x10^-6 Torr). 2. Transfer to PVD chamber and strike Ar plasma on Ti target (DC power 2.0 kW, 3.5 mTorr Ar, 200°C chuck) to deposit 25 nm Ti. 3. Immediately initiate N2 reactive gas flow (calibrated Ar:N2 ratio 3:1) in transition mode to deposit 50 nm TiN. 4. Unload wafer and measure 49-point sheet resistance (Rs) via 4PP. 5. Measure absolute film thickness and density across wafer diameter using XRR. | `Total stack thickness (Ti + TiN) must be 75.0 nm ± 3.5 nm (within ±5%). 49-point sheet resistance uniformity (1-sigma standard deviation / mean) must be <= 2.5%. Combined sheet resistance Rs must be 28.0 to 36.0 Ohm/sq.` |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-1-1-2-02` | **Al-Si Junction Spike Barrier Integrity and Leakage Current Evaluation** | Automated DC Semiconductor Parameter Analyzer connected to semi-automatic wafer probe station, hot chuck set to 25°C | 1. Mount annealed contact test wafer on vacuum chuck of probe station. 2. Probe 20 randomly distributed 1000-contact n+/p diode chain structures across the wafer. 3. Sweep reverse bias voltage from 0.0 V to -5.0 V DC. 4. Measure leakage current density at -3.3 V reverse bias. 5. Perform cross-sectional transmission electron microscopy (TEM) / EDX line-scan on 2 fail/pass sites to inspect for Al diffusion spikes. | `Reverse leakage current density must be < 1.0 nA/cm^2 at -3.3 V for >= 95% of tested dies. Zero Al-Si spike penetration through the TiN/Ti barrier layer into the silicon substrate observable under STEM cross-section.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloving), ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical/impact safety glasses and full face shield during target handling, Flame-retardant cleanroom bunny suit and ESD-safe safety footwear, P100 particulate half-mask respirator during chamber shield cleaning or target maintenance
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Inhalation of inert gas (Argon/Nitrogen) causes rapid asphyxiation: Move victim immediately to fresh air; administer supplemental oxygen if breathing is difficult; perform artificial respiration if breathing has ceased. In case of mechanical eye/skin contact with pyrophoric or sharp Ti/TiN flakes during PM, flush eyes with sterile isotonic saline for >= 15 minutes and wash skin thoroughly with neutral soap and water. Seek immediate medical attention.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Chamber roughing pumps and turbomolecular pump backing lines must be connected to dedicated house toxic/inert gas scrubbed exhaust. Gas cabinets for Argon and Nitrogen must feature automatic excess-flow shutoff valves and continuous ambient O2 deficiency monitoring sensors set to alarm at < 19.5% O2.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent Titanium targets and contaminated stainless steel chamber shields must be sealed in heavy-duty polyethylene bags and sent to licensed metallurgical recycling facilities. Pyrophoric titanium particulate accumulation from vacuum traps must be pacified under mineral oil or water immersion prior to hazardous solid waste disposal.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Titanium (solid sputtering target)** | `7440-32-6` | 5N (99.999%) | `100%` |
| **Argon (compressed process gas)** | `7440-37-1` | Ultra-High Purity 6N (99.9999%) | `100%` |
| **Nitrogen (compressed process gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity 6N (99.9999%) | `100%` |
| **Titanium Nitride (deposited film/particulate dust)** | `25583-20-4` | Stoichiometric Thin Film | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-metal contact vias opened, cleaned with dilute HF (100:1) to strip native oxide, water rinsed, Marangoni dried, and hydrogen-passivated (Si-H terminated).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Stoichiometric (200)-oriented TiN passivated barrier surface (50 nm) over Ti adhesion layer (25 nm), sealed under high vacuum or inert N2 purge ready for Al-Cu metallization.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air Q-time causes uncontrolled native oxide (SiO2) re-growth in contact vias leading to contact opens; exceeding N2 Q-time prior to Al deposition results in ambient moisture/oxygen chemisorption on TiN surface, degrading subsequent Al interconnect wetting and adhesion.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful recipe qualification of in-situ Ti (25 nm) adhesion and reactive TiN (50 nm) diffusion barrier deposition via planar DC magnetron sputtering on 180nm DRAM test structures, achieving stoichiometric dense films, uniform sheet resistance, and zero aluminum spiking post-anneal.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `RECIPE_PVD_TI_TIN_180NM_QUAL_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `RESISTIVITY_4PP_49PT_UNIFORMITY_MAP.csv`
- [ ] `STEM_EDX_DIFFUSION_BARRIER_CROSS_SECTION.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Total deposited Ti/TiN bilayer film thickness** | `75.0 nm` | ±3.5 nm | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / X-Ray Reflectometry (XRR) |
| `ASSERT-02` | **As-deposited Ti/TiN sheet resistance across 49-point wafer map** | `32.0 Ohm/sq` | ±4.0 Ohm/sq | Automated 4-Point Probe Resistivity Mapping |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Post-400C forming gas anneal junction leakage current density at -3.3V bias** | `0.15 nA/cm^2` | < 1.0 nA/cm^2 | Automated Semiconductor Parameter Analyzer Diode Array Sweep |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Passage of TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-1-1-2-01 and TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-1-1-2-02 with all quantitative assertions verified across 3 consecutive qualification wafers, confirmed zero STEM-visible Al spikes post 400°C anneal, and formal joint sign-off by Lead Thin Film Process Engineer and Packaging Integration Manager.

Sweep reverse bias voltage from 0.0 V to -5.0 V DC. 4. Measure leakage current density at -3.3 V reverse bias. 5. Perform cross-sectional transmission electron microscopy (TEM) / EDX line-scan on 2 fail/pass sites to inspect for Al diffusion spikes.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Reverse leakage current density must be < 1.0 nA/cm^2 at -3.3 V for >= 95% of tested dies. Zero Al-Si spike penetration through the TiN/Ti barrier layer into the silicon substrate observable under STEM cross-section.

ppe_required: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloving)
ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical/impact safety glasses and full face shield during target handling
Flame-retardant cleanroom bunny suit and ESD-safe safety footwear
P100 particulate half-mask respirator during chamber shield cleaning or target maintenance
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: Inhalation of inert gas (Argon/Nitrogen) causes rapid asphyxiation: Move victim immediately to fresh air; administer supplemental oxygen if breathing is difficult; perform artificial respiration if breathing has ceased. In case of mechanical eye/skin contact with pyrophoric or sharp Ti/TiN flakes during PM, flush eyes with sterile isotonic saline for >= 15 minutes and wash skin thoroughly with neutral soap and water. Seek immediate medical attention.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Chamber roughing pumps and turbomolecular pump backing lines must be connected to dedicated house toxic/inert gas scrubbed exhaust. Gas cabinets for Argon and Nitrogen must feature automatic excess-flow shutoff valves and continuous ambient O2 deficiency monitoring sensors set to alarm at < 19.5% O2.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Spent Titanium targets and contaminated stainless steel chamber shields must be sealed in heavy-duty polyethylene bags and sent to licensed metallurgical recycling facilities. Pyrophoric titanium particulate accumulation from vacuum traps must be pacified under mineral oil or water immersion prior to hazardous solid waste disposal.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Pre-metal contact vias opened, cleaned with dilute HF (100:1) to strip native oxide, water rinsed, Marangoni dried, and hydrogen-passivated (Si-H terminated).
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Stoichiometric (200)-oriented TiN passivated barrier surface (50 nm) over Ti adhesion layer (25 nm), sealed under high vacuum or inert N2 purge ready for Al-Cu metallization.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding air Q-time causes uncontrolled native oxide (SiO2) re-growth in contact vias leading to contact opens; exceeding N2 Q-time prior to Al deposition results in ambient moisture/oxygen chemisorption on TiN surface, degrading subsequent Al interconnect wetting and adhesion.

expected_result.summary: Successful recipe qualification of in-situ Ti (25 nm) adhesion and reactive TiN (50 nm) diffusion barrier deposition via planar DC magnetron sputtering on 180nm DRAM test structures, achieving stoichiometric dense films, uniform sheet resistance, and zero aluminum spiking post-anneal.

quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / X-Ray Reflectometry (XRR)

quantitative_assertions.assertion: As-deposited Ti/TiN sheet resistance across 49-point wafer map
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Automated 4-Point Probe Resistivity Mapping

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Post-400C forming gas anneal junction leakage current density at -3.3V bias
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Automated Semiconductor Parameter Analyzer Diode Array Sweep

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Ti/TiN Bilayer Thickness, Sheet Resistance & Step Coverage Metrology

**Level & Module:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN) > Interconnect Sputtering & Die Packaging Probe Station > M1/M2 Metallization Sputtering & Ti/TiN Barrier Deposition Recipe Execution > Ti/TiN Adhesion & Diffusion Barrier Sputter Deposition > Metrology  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm / 180nm)  
**Action Type:** Buy / Quality Metrology Protocol  

---

### 1. Metrology Process Flow

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    Inspect & Prep     │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Four-Point Probe Rs  │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│     Spectroscopic     │
│  Ellipsometry / XRF   │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Cross-Sectional SEM  │
│     Step Coverage     │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   SPC Verification    │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Substrate Alignment & Pre-Inspection**:
   - Transfer wafer from PVD barrier cluster load-lock onto the automated inspection stage under cleanroom Class 1/10 conditions.
   - Align notch/flat to 0° reference position; confirm absence of micro-blistering, delamination, or particulate contamination on wafer test coupons and active array scribe lines.

2. **Sheet Resistance ($R_s$) Mapping via Four-Point Probe (FPP)**:
   - Perform a calibrated 49-point or 121-point dual-configuration four-point probe scan across the wafer surface.
   - Measure sheet resistance ($R_s$) across test areas to detect resistivity shifts and film thickness uniformity profiles across the wafer radius.

3. **Bilayer Thickness Determination (Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / XRF)**:
   - Measure unpatterned monitor dies and dedicated metrology test pads using spectroscopic ellipsometry (multi-wavelength $\lambda = 190\text{–}850\text{ nm}$) and calibrated X-ray Fluorescence (XRF) for Ti/TiN dual-layer deconvolution.
   - Quantify physical thickness of bottom Ti adhesion film and top TiN barrier layer against baseline recipe deposition rates.

4. **High-Aspect-Ratio Contact Step Coverage Inspection (FIB-SEM)**:
   - Select witness scribe-line contact test structures (bitline drain contacts / W-plug interfaces, nominal critical dimension $L = 180\text{ nm}$, contact depth aspect ratio $\ge 3:1$).
   - Perform precision cross-sectional FIB (focused ion beam) cut and in-lens SEM inspection at $30\text{k}\times\text{–}100\text{k}\times$ magnification.
   - Measure bottom-wall and side-wall film coverage relative to field nominal thickness: $\text{Step Coverage (\%)} = \frac{t_{\text{bottom}}}{t_{\text{field}}} \times 100\%$.

5. **Data Logging & Run-to-Run SPC Gating**:
   - Transmit measured thickness, $R_s$, and step coverage data into the line Statistical Process Control (SPC) database. Flag out-of-control limits before advancing lot to Al-0.5% Cu or pure Al interconnect metallization deposition.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Engineering Unit | Tolerance / Limit | Metrology Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Bitline Contact CD & Topology Alignment** | Access Transistor $L = 180$ | $\text{nm}$ | Target dimension matching cell layout | In-line CD-SEM |
| **Interconnect Metallization Baseline** | Post-barrier Al Metal-1 target $= 350$ | $\text{nm}$ | $\pm 5\%$ ($\pm 17.5\text{ nm}$) | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / XRF |
| **Sheet Resistance Stability ($R_s$)** | Pre-condition boundary for downstream metallization post-anneal ($400^\circ\text{C}$, 30 min forming gas) | $\Omega/\text{sq}$ | Downstream stack $R_s < 0.08$ | Dual-config 4-Point Probe |
| **PVD Deposition Base Vacuum Integrity** | Process chamber base pump-down | $\text{Torr}$ | $< 2 \times 10^{-6}$ | Ionization Vacuum Gauge |
| **Sputter Process Gas Pressure** | High-purity Ar ($99.999\%$) | $\text{mTorr}$ | $3\text{ to }5$ | Capacitance Manometer |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **Source: Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects**:
  - *Base Pressure*: $< 2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$ prior to sputter deposition.
  - *Working Gas & Pressure*: Ar $99.999\%$ at $3\text{ to }5\text{ mTorr}$.
  - *Interconnect Metallization Target*: Metal-1 film thickness target is $350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$.
  - *Post-Anneal Sheet Resistance Target*: $R_s < 0.08\ \Omega/\text{sq}$ after forming gas anneal ($\text{N}_2/\text{H}_2\ 95/5$ at $400^\circ\text{C}$ for $30\text{ minutes}$).
- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - *Unit Cell Geometry*: Access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$, shared bitline contact over tungsten plug (W-plug).
- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**:
  - *Interconnect Pitch & Integration*: Bitline and wordline pitch approximately $360\text{ nm to }400\text{ nm}$, establishing geometric constraints for contact barrier conformality.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: In integrating the Ti/TiN barrier metrology with downstream 350 nm Al-0.5%Cu interconnect metallization, inline 4-point probe (4PP) sheet resistance measurements must decouple the native sheet resistance of the underlying diffusion/silicon substrate from the Ti/TiN bilayer. Furthermore, physical cross-section metrology via FIB-SEM must correlate bottom contact via step coverage (AR > 2.5:1) with contact resistance (R_c) extraction from TLM structures, ensuring that contact resistance does not exceed 10 Ohm per contact pad across 150mm/200mm wafer topography.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: A 180nm DRAM node requires Ti (adhesion/ohmic contact, ~15-20 nm) and TiN (diffusion barrier, ~30-50 nm) bilayers. PVD magnetron sputtering step coverage inside deep contact vias drops drastically at bottom corners; without collimated or ionized PVD, bottom coverage can plummet below 15-20%, leading to aluminum spiking into active silicon during the 400°C forming gas anneal. Non-destructive XRF or spectroscopic ellipsometry must be calibrated against cross-sectional TEM/HR-SEM for accurate bilayer thickness deconvolution.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Target consumption and availability for 5N (99.999%) purity Titanium targets and reactive sputter high-purity N2/Ar gas blends introduce supply variability. Sourcing specialized four-point probe dual-configuration tips (e.g., KLA Tencor OmniMap) and FIB-SEM grid consumables must be pre-allocated to prevent metrology station bottlenecks from idling back-end metallization lines.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Inline metrology for Ti/TiN must maintain a total inspection cycle time of under 12 minutes per cassette to strictly enforce the downstream 30-minute queue time before Al metallization sputtering. Any hold time exceeding the queue limits forces costly TiN surface de-oxidation sputter etching, risking wafer scrap.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Inadequate Ti/TiN step coverage (<15% at contact bottom corners) causing Al-Si interdiffusion and junction spiking during 400°C post-metal sintering.
1. Atmospheric oxidation of the TiN cap into non-stoichiometric TiOxNy due to Q-time breach, causing dramatic contact resistance degradation on TLM structures.
1. Excessive film stress in the Ti/TiN bilayer (>1.5 GPa compressive) leading to film delamination or micro-voiding at the dielectric boundary prior to Al-0.5%Cu deposition.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-1-1-3-01` | **Dual-Configuration 4-Point Probe Sheet Resistance & Uniformity Mapping** | Dual-configuration 4-Point Probe Resistivity Mapping System (e.g., KLA-Tencor RS-100 / Napson CRESBOX) | 1. Load monitor wafer onto temperature-controlled vacuum chuck at 23.0°C ± 0.5°C. 2. Align wafer notch to 0 degrees. 3. Execute 49-point polar map with 3 mm edge exclusion. 4. Record Sheet Resistance (R_s) in Ohm/sq and calculate 1-sigma standard deviation / non-uniformity percentage. | `Mean R_s = 45.0 Ohm/sq ± 10% (40.5 to 49.5 Ohm/sq); wafer-level non-uniformity (1-sigma) <= 2.5%.` |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-1-1-3-02` | **Contact Via Ti/TiN Bottom and Sidewall Step Coverage Verification via Dual-Beam FIB-SEM** | Dual-Beam Focused Ion Beam / High-Resolution Field Emission SEM (FIB-SEM, e.g., FEI Helios NanoLab) | 1. Transfer sample coupon into vacuum loadlock (< 5x10^-6 mbar). 2. Deposit protective Pt cap via in-situ gas injection system. 3. Perform 30 kV Ga+ ion beam cross-section cut followed by 5 kV polishing cut across contact center. 4. Acquire in-lens high-resolution secondary electron / backscatter image at 50,000x magnification. 5. Measure field thickness (t_field), bottom thickness (t_bottom), and sidewall thickness (t_sidewall) at lowest 10% via height. | `Bottom step coverage ratio (t_bottom / t_field) >= 20.0%; sidewall step coverage ratio (t_sidewall / t_field) >= 15.0%; total bottom barrier thickness >= 10.0 nm with zero pinholes or delamination.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Class 100 nitrile gloves (double gloving), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses, Static-dissipative cleanroom gown and ESD-safe conductive footwear, N95 particulate respirator during chamber flaking cleaning or dry maintenance
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact: Wash affected skin thoroughly with soap and copious running water for at least 15 minutes. Eye contact: Flush open eyes with isotonic saline or eyewash station stream for 15 minutes; seek ophthalmologic medical evaluation. Inhalation of particulate/fume: Move exposed personnel to fresh air immediately; administer oxygen if respiration is labored. Ingestion: Rinse mouth with water; never induce vomiting in unconscious individuals; call emergency poison hotline.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous cleanroom re-circulated HEPA/ULPA laminar flow airflow with local exhaust ventilation (LEV) on chemical transfer benches maintaining minimum face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM); FIB-SEM chamber turbo-molecular pump exhaust manifold connected to scrubbed fab exhaust.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: All solvent wipes contaminated with isopropanol must be sealed in airtight flammable waste bins for solvent reclamation; spent Ti targets, cleavage fragments, and dummy wafer debris must be segregated into solid heavy-metal recycle containers per RCRA guidelines.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Titanium (sputter target & deposited film)** | `7440-32-6` | 5N (99.999%) | `100.0%` |
| **Titanium Nitride (sputtered film)** | `25583-20-4` | Electronic Grade Thin Film | `100.0%` |
| **Isopropanol (wafer cleaning/wipe)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI / Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Argon Process Gas** | `7440-37-1` | UHP Grade 5.0 (99.999%) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-metal clean (100:1 dilute HF dip / Ar plasma soft etch) verified hydrophobic with contact angle > 65 deg and native oxide thickness < 0.5 nm.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Passivated, stoichiometric TiN surface free of particulate defects (>0.2 um count < 10) ready for immediate Al-0.5%Cu metallization under high vacuum.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding 30 minutes in ambient cleanroom air causes spontaneous atmospheric oxidation of Ti/TiN, generating an uncontrolled high-resistivity TiOxNy surface layer that spikes specific contact resistivity (rho_c) beyond the 1x10^-6 Ohm*cm^2 ceiling and leads to Al adhesion peeling.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Complete metrology validation of the PVD Ti/TiN adhesion and diffusion barrier stack on 180nm DRAM test structures, verifying blanket sheet resistance, within-wafer uniformity, and high-aspect-ratio via step coverage compliant with back-end metallization specifications.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `ti_tin_sheet_resistance_map_TC-01.csv`
- [ ] `contact_via_step_coverage_fib_sem_TC-02.tiff`
- [ ] `ti_tin_barrier_metrology_signoff_report.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Blanket Ti/TiN bilayer sheet resistance on 4PP 49-point map** | `45.0 Ohm/sq` | ± 4.5 Ohm/sq (10%) | Dual-configuration 4-point probe mapping with 3 mm edge exclusion |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Bottom via step coverage at aspect ratio 2.7:1 contact vias** | `22.5%` | >= 20.0% absolute | Dual-beam FIB-SEM high-resolution cross-sectional metrology at 50,000x |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Ti/TiN bilayer thickness on planar field oxide (20 nm Ti / 30 nm TiN)** | `50.0 nm` | ± 3.0 nm (6%) | Calibrated spectroscopic ellipsometry cross-verified by X-ray Reflectivity (XRR) |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher exit condition requires all 49-point sheet resistance measurements to fall within 40.5-49.5 Ohm/sq with non-uniformity < 2.5%, cross-sectional SEM confirming bottom step coverage >= 20.0% with zero observable voiding or delamination, and full automated artifact generation logged prior to releasing the lot for Al-0.5%Cu sputtering within the 30-minute air Q-time limit.

nodes.primary_metric: Sub-milestone of M1/M2 Metallization Sputtering & Ti/TiN Barrier Deposition Recipe Execution
nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Al-0.5% Cu DC Magnetron Sputtering & In-Situ Stage Heating

**Level / Node**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > Interconnect Sputtering & Die Packaging Probe Station > M1/M2 Metallization Sputtering & Ti/TiN Barrier Deposition Recipe Execution > Al-0.5% Cu DC Magnetron Sputtering & In-Situ Stage Heating  
**Technology Generation**: Gen 2 (180 nm / µm)  
**Action Type**: Make  

---

### 1. Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Base Vacuum Pumpdown  │
│  (< 2 x 10^-6 Torr)    │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Substrate In-Situ    │
│     Stage Heating      │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Ar Gas Admission     │
│    (3 to 5 mTorr)      │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  DC Magnetron Plasma   │
│   (1.5 to 3.0 kW)      │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Al-Cu Deposition M-1  │
│   (350 nm ± 5%)        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Post-Metal Anneal    │
│  (400°C, 30 min, F.G.) │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Substrate Loading & High-Vacuum Chamber Pumpdown**:
   - Transfer wafer (with Ti/TiN barrier layer prepared) onto the PVD chuck.
   - Engage cryopump or turbomolecular pumping system.
   - Pump down the vacuum chamber until the base pressure reaches **below $2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$** to suppress residual oxygen and water vapor incorporation.

2. **In-Situ Substrate Heating**:
   - Energize the substrate heater to warm the wafer stage in-situ.
   - Maintain stage heating to facilitate surface adatom mobility and step coverage over bitline and interconnect contacts prior to and during sputtering.

3. **Process Gas Stabilization**:
   - Introduce ultra-high-purity Argon (**Ar 99.999% / 5N purity**).
   - Adjust the downstream throttle valve / MFC to maintain working process pressure strictly between **3 to 5 mTorr**.

4. **Target Sputtering & Deposition Recipe Execution**:
   - Ignite DC magnetron plasma over the 5N Al-0.5% Cu target.
   - Ramp and stabilize DC power within the operating window of **1.5 to 3.0 kW**.
   - Sputter at a calibrated deposition rate of **50 to 100 nm/min**.
   - Deposit for the calculated duration to achieve the target Metal-1 nominal thickness of **350 nm**.

5. **Post-Metal Anneal (PMA)**:
   - Transfer wafer to the annealing furnace.
   - Perform forming gas anneal under **$\text{N}_2/\text{H}_2$ ($95\%/5\%$)** at **$400^\circ\text{C}$** for **30 minutes** to stabilize film morphology, sinter grain boundaries, and minimize contact resistance.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value & Tolerance | Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Chamber Base Vacuum Pressure** | $< 2 \times 10^{-6}$ | $\text{Torr}$ | In-situ Bayard-Alpert ion gauge / vacuum transducer |
| **Ar Working Process Pressure** | $3\text{ to }5$ | $\text{mTorr}$ | Capacitance manometer gauge |
| **Metal-1 Film Thickness** | $350 \pm 5\%$ ($332.5\text{ to }367.5$) | $\text{nm}$ | Spectroscopic ellipsometry / surface profilometry |
| **Sheet Resistance ($R_s$)** *(post-PMA)* | $< 0.08$ | $\Omega/\text{sq}$ | Four-point probe (4PP) resistivity measurement |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **Source**: *Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects*
  - Vacuum pumpdown limit: $< 2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$ (turbomolecular/cryopump).
  - Process gas: High-purity Argon (99.999% Ar) at $3\text{ to }5\text{ mTorr}$ working pressure.
  - Power & Deposition Rate: $1.5\text{ to }3.0\text{ kW}$ DC magnetron power; $50\text{ to }100\text{ nm/min}$ deposition rate.
  - Film Thickness & Target: Metal-1 thickness target $350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$.
  - Post-Metal Anneal & Sheet Resistance: Forming gas $\text{N}_2/\text{H}_2\text{ }95/5$ at $400^\circ\text{C}$ for $30\text{ min}$; $R_s < 0.08\text{ }\Omega/\text{sq}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: In-situ stage heating to 250-350°C during DC magnetron sputtering creates severe thermal management trade-offs: radiation heating of the vacuum chamber shields promotes outgassing, degrading the base pressure from 2x10^-6 Torr to >5x10^-5 Torr during deposition if cryopump baffles become saturated. Furthermore, substrate chuck temperature non-uniformity across 150mm/200mm platen directly induces grain boundary size variations and localized thickness gradient exceeding the ±5% specification.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Cu segregation at grain boundaries during deposition and subsequent forming gas sintering is critical for electromigration suppression in 180nm pitch structures. However, exceeding 350°C during in-situ heating accelerates the formation of θ-phase Al2Cu precipitates at the contact interfaces rather than uniform grain boundary distribution, which causes non-uniform wet or dry metal etch rates, severe contact resistance spikes, and Al hillock formation puncturing inter-metal dielectric (IMD) layers.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring 5N (99.999%) purity Al-0.5wt% Cu targets in Southeast Asia faces stringent lead-time delays (12-16 weeks) and backing plate bonding certification requirements (diffusion bonded copper vs. indium bonded elastomer, where indium melts at 156.6°C and cannot survive in-situ high-power sputtering). Local alternative suppliers often provide 4N targets with iron and silicon impurity spikes exceeding 15 ppm, directly compromising film sheet resistance R_s and junction leakage.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scheduling multi-wafer runs across in-situ heated PVD requires balancing pre-heating ramps (15 min) and active cool-down under vacuum/N2 (45 min) to avoid thermal shock breakage or uncontrolled oxidation upon chamber loadlock venting. This reduces tool availability from 6 wafers/hour to fewer than 1.5 wafers/hour, presenting a major project bottleneck for Gen 2 wafer lot throughput.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal expansion mismatch inducing Al hillock growth and micro-voiding during in-situ stage heating, leading to inter-metal dielectric (IMD) shorts or open bitlines.
1. Base pressure degradation due to heated platen outgassing, causing oxygen and water vapor incorporation into the Al film that elevates sheet resistance R_s > 0.08 Ohm/sq and promotes unetchable Al2O3 inclusions.
1. Incomplete step coverage and micro-trenching at the base of 180nm contact vias due to inadequate directional sputtering and substrate temperature variance, causing metal continuity open circuits.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-1-2-01` | **Al-0.5% Cu Film Thickness Uniformity and Sheet Resistance (Rs) Verification** | KLA-Tencor Alpha-Step D-500 Stylus Profilometer, CDE ResMap 178 4-Point Probe, Turbomolecular PVD Chamber Vacuum Gauge Array | 1. Load wafer into DC magnetron sputtering chamber and clamp onto electrostatic/mechanical chuck with back-side Ar gas conduction. 2. Ignite DC magnetron plasma on Al-0.5% Cu target at 2.0 kW power; stabilize Ar working pressure at 3.5 mTorr. 3. Sputter for 240 seconds to target 350 nm nominal film thickness. 4. Transfer wafer to vacuum cooling station until platen temperature drops below 80°C. 5. Measure film thickness across 49-point diameter scan using stylus profilometer. 6. Sinter wafer at 400°C for 30 minutes in forming gas (N2/H2 95/5). 7. Execute 49-point sheet resistance map using 4-point probe. | `Total thickness must be 350 nm ± 17.5 nm (within ±5% tolerance); Thickness non-uniformity across wafer (1-sigma) < 3.5%; Post-sinter sheet resistance R_s < 0.080 Ohm/sq across all 49 measurement points.` |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-1-2-02` | **Contact Step Coverage and Ideality Factor Characterization on Discrete PN Test Structures** | Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FE-SEM), Keithley 4200-SCS Semiconductor Characterization System with probe station | 1. Deposit 350 nm Al-0.5% Cu with stage at 300°C per calibrated sputtering recipe. 2. Perform forming gas sintering at 420°C for 20 minutes. 3. Cleave wafer across contact via test array, cross-section with FIB/mechanical polish, and image metal step coverage at via bottom and sidewalls under FE-SEM at 50,000x magnification. 4. Land tungsten probe tips on anode and cathode pads of PN junction test structure on Keithley 4200-SCS. 5. Sweep forward bias voltage from 0.0V to 0.8V in 10 mV steps and record forward I-V characteristics. | `FE-SEM bottom via step coverage >= 35% of nominal field thickness (>= 122.5 nm at via base); No observable micro-voids at via perimeter; Measured PN diode forward bias ideality factor (eta) between 0.2V and 0.5V must satisfy 1.05 <= eta <= 1.20.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level C cleanroom PPE including flame-resistant Nomex cleanroom suit, Full face shield over UV/laser safety goggles (absorbance at plasma emission wavelengths), Heavy-duty nitrile gloves over secondary inner nitrile barrier gloves, Thermal heat-resistant Kevlar/Nomex handling gloves for hot platen/shield extraction, P100 particulate respirator equipped with organic vapor/acid gas cartridge during target change and chamber mechanical scrubbing
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For thermal burns from heated chuck (>300°C): Immediately irrigate with copious clean cool water for 20 minutes; do not apply ice directly; cover with sterile non-adherent dressing and seek medical attention. For asphyxiation hazard due to Ar gas leak: Evacuate victim to fresh air immediately; administer artificial respiration or oxygen via trained personnel if breathing has ceased. For pyrophoric/reactive aluminum dust inhalation during shield cleaning: Move to fresh air, irrigate eyes and mucous membranes with saline solution for 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Chamber roughing pump and turbomolecular pump backing lines must vent directly into dedicated toxic/inert process gas house exhaust operating under continuous negative pressure (>0.5 in. w.g.) with minimum 150 CFM flow. Chamber maintenance area requires dedicated local exhaust ventilation (LEV) snorkels (>100 fpm capture velocity) to eliminate airborne Al/Cu particulate inhalation during shield grit-blasting or bead-blasting replacement.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent Al-0.5% Cu targets and vacuum shield flakes containing sub-micron pyrophoric metal particulates must be submerged in mineral oil or wet-collected in aqueous 10% sodium carbonate solution to prevent spontaneous dust deflagration, followed by disposal through hazardous solid waste reclamation certified for heavy metal recovery.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Argon (Compressed Gas)** | `7440-37-1` | Grade 5.0 (99.999% Electronic Grade) | `100%` |
| **Aluminum (Sputtering Target)** | `7429-90-5` | 5N (99.999% metals basis) | `99.5 wt%` |
| **Copper (Alloy Component)** | `7440-50-8` | 5N (99.999% metals basis) | `0.5 wt%` |
| **Forming Gas (Nitrogen/Hydrogen Balance)** | `7727-37-9 / 1333-74-0` | Semiconductor Ultra-High Purity | `95% N2 / 5% H2` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-metal contact vias and Ti/TiN barrier layer must be freshly de-oxidized (dilute HF dip, deionized water cascade rinse to 18 MOhm-cm, spin-dry), verified free of native TiO2 or interfacial oxide under ellipsometry/reflectometry.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Continuous, specular Al-0.5% Cu film (350 nm) with root-mean-square roughness Rq < 4.0 nm, cooled below 80°C under vacuum/N2 to avoid immediate surface blistering or non-uniform native oxide growth prior to passivation or lithography.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air queue time causes native oxide (Al2O3 / TiO2) growth exceeding 2.5 nm at interfaces, which causes non-ohmic contact behavior (ideality factor eta > 1.5), contact resistance excursions (> 50 Ohm/contact), and severe inter-layer delamination during post-metal sintering.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Verifiable delivery of a 350 nm Al-0.5% Cu metallization layer deposited via planar DC magnetron sputtering with in-situ stage heating, achieving post-sinter sheet resistance R_s < 0.08 Ohm/sq, step coverage >= 35%, and ohmic contact ideality factor 1.05 <= eta <= 1.20 on discrete 180nm baseline test diodes.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `ALCU_PVD_350NM_RECIPE_LOG_RUN2026.csv`
- [ ] `RESMAP_49PT_RS_CONTOUR_MAP_RUN2026.pdf`
- [ ] `FESEM_VIA_STEP_COVERAGE_XSEC_50KX.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Film thickness across 150mm wafer must meet target specification** | `350 nm` | ± 17.5 nm (± 5.0%) | 49-point diameter stylus profilometry and spectroscopic reflectometry |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Post-sinter sheet resistance after forming gas anneal (400°C, 30 min)** | `0.072 Ohm/sq` | < 0.080 Ohm/sq maximum limit | Automated 4-point probe mapping system |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Discrete PN junction diode forward ideality factor (eta)** | `1.12` | 1.05 <= eta <= 1.20 | Keithley 4200-SCS automated forward I-V parameter extraction between 0.2V and 0.5V |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher exit sign-off requires: 1) Base pressure verified <= 2.0x10^-6 Torr prior to plasma ignition; 2) All 49 sheet resistance measurement points show R_s < 0.080 Ohm/sq with 1-sigma non-uniformity < 3.5%; 3) FE-SEM cross-section demonstrates >= 35% contact bottom step coverage with zero observable voiding; 4) Parameter extraction on PN test diode yields forward ideality factor 1.05 <= eta <= 1.20 with reverse leakage < 10 nA/cm^2 at -5V.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Al-0.5% Cu Target Sputter Pre-Clean & Base Vacuum Qualification

**Module:** Thin Film Deposition / Back-End Metallization Interconnect  
**Node / Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) — M1/M2 Bitline & Wordline Strapping Metallization  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Purpose & Scope
This SOP defines the sequential vacuum pump-down qualification, process gas stabilization, and shutter-closed target pre-sputtering routine for the Al-0.5% Cu DC magnetron sputtering chamber prior to deposition on active product wafers (M1/M2 metallization). Pre-cleaning strips native surface oxides and contaminants from the 5N purity target, preventing oxygen incorporation into DRAM interconnect layers.

---

### 2. Equipment & Materials
* **PVD Chamber:** Planar DC Magnetron Sputtering System with automated target shutter.
* **Vacuum System:** Turbomolecular pump (TMP) or Cryopump backed by dry mechanical roughing pump.
* **Process Gas:** High-Purity Argon ($\text{Ar} \ge 99.999\%$ / 5N).
* **Target:** 99.999% (5N) Aluminum-Copper alloy ($\text{Al}-0.5\%\,\text{Cu}$) sputter target.
* **Instrumentation:** Cold cathode / Bayard-Alpert ion gauge, capacitance manometer, mass flow controller (MFC), DC power supply (1.5 to 3.0 kW).

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Procedure

```text
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| 1. High-Vacuum Pump-Down & Base Pressure Verification        |
|    - Cryopump/TMP pull-down; Gauge: Cold Cathode / Ion      |
|    - Interlock: P_base < 2.0e-6 Torr                        |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| 2. Argon Gas Introduction & Working Pressure Stabilization   |
|    - Flow Ar (99.999% 5N) via calibrated MFC                |
|    - Throttle gate valve to 3.0 - 5.0 mTorr                 |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| 3. Substrate Stage Pre-Conditioning & Shutter Confirmation   |
|    - Verify physical shutter is closed over substrate stage |
|    - Isolate product/dummy wafers during burn-in            |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| 4. Plasma Ignition & Target Pre-Sputter Clean               |
|    - Ignite DC plasma; ramp DC power to 1.5 - 3.0 kW        |
|    - Sputter against closed shutter (burn-in oxide layer)   |
|    - Verify stable V-I curve; qualify target for deposition |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 3.1: Chamber Evacuation & Base Vacuum Qualification
1. Close chamber vent valve, seal load lock isolation slit valve, and initiate roughing stage.
2. Crossover to high-vacuum pumping (cryopump or turbomolecular pump).
3. Monitor ion gauge readout until chamber outgassing subsides. 
4. Verify base vacuum pressure achieves **$< 2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$**. If base pressure fails to reach this threshold, halt process to perform leak checking (He leak rate check) and regeneration of cryopump/TMP.

#### Step 3.2: Process Gas Introduction & Pressure Regulation
1. Open ultra-high purity Ar supply line ($\ge 99.999\%$ purity).
2. Set MFC to introduce Ar gas into the magnetron cathode dark space.
3. Regulate downstream throttle valve to maintain chamber working pressure between **$3\text{ mTorr}$ and $5\text{ mTorr}$** as read by the capacitance manometer.

#### Step 3.3: Shutter Interlock & Stage Pre-Check
1. Confirm the target/substrate shutter is in the fully **CLOSED** position between the Al-0.5% Cu cathode and the wafer stage to prevent cross-contamination onto the substrate pedestal.

#### Step 3.4: DC Magnetron Ignition & Pre-Sputter Conditioning
1. Enable the DC power supply interlocks.
2. Strike the Ar plasma and smoothly ramp the DC magnetron power to the operating window of **$1.5\text{ kW}$ to $3.0\text{ kW}$**.
3. Maintain continuous target pre-sputtering onto the closed shutter for the recipe-specified burn-in cycle (typically 3 to 5 minutes) to remove passivated native aluminum oxide ($\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$) and restore fresh metallic Al-Cu grain boundaries.
4. Verify plasma discharge stability (DC voltage and current within $\pm 2\%$ operating window).
5. Ramp down power or transition directly into product wafer deposition sequencing upon completion.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric / Acceptance Limit | Physical Unit | Measurement Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Chamber Base Vacuum Pressure** | $< 2 \times 10^{-6}$ | $\text{Torr}$ | In-situ Ionization Gauge / Cold Cathode Gauge |
| **Sputter Process Gas Purity** | $\ge 99.999$ (5N) | $\%$ | Certified Gas Purity Analysis / In-line Filter Spec |
| **Ar Sputter Working Pressure** | $3.0\text{ to }5.0$ | $\text{mTorr}$ | Capacitance Manometer |
| **DC Magnetron Pre-Clean Power** | $1.5\text{ to }3.0$ | $\text{kW}$ | DC Power Supply Output Telemetry |

---

### 5. Context Citations
* **Base Pressure ($< 2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$)**: *Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects* ("Base pressure must pump down below 2x10^-6 Torr using turbomolecular or cryopump to prevent oxygen incorporation.").
* **Process Gas Purity ($\text{Ar } 99.999\%$) & Working Pressure ($3\text{ to }5\text{ mTorr}$)**: *Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects* ("Sputtering process gas is high-purity Argon (Ar 99.999%) maintained at 3 to 5 mTorr working pressure.").
* **Target Purity ($99.999\%$ / 5N) & DC Power ($1.5\text{ to }3.0\text{ kW}$)**: *Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects* ("Target: 99.999% (5N) Aluminum target driven by DC magnetron power supply at 1.5 to 3.0 kW.").

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Pumping efficiency and ultimate base vacuum directly govern baseline background partial pressures; if the turbomolecular/cryopump pump-down curve fails to achieve base pressure below 2.0E-6 Torr, subsequent Al-0.5% Cu sputtering will suffer significant oxygen and moisture getter incorporation, degrading thin-film resistivity and increasing bulk defect density.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Sputter pre-cleaning of the Al-0.5% Cu target must strip native passivation oxides (Al2O3) with shutter closed at 1.5 to 2.0 kW DC power under 3 to 5 mTorr Ar until cathode discharge voltage stabilizes within ±1.5% and RGA mass peaks 18 (H2O), 28 (CO/N2), and 32 (O2) decay below baseline thresholds, otherwise oxide cross-contamination transfers onto substrate interfaces.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Target alloy homogeneity is crucial; sourcing certified 99.999% (5N) Al-0.5 wt% Cu planar targets requires verified metallurgical batch analysis (ICP-MS) and backing plate indium-bond integrity checks to prevent local target delamination, copper precipitation voids, or sudden arcing during extended DC magnetron pre-burn cycles.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Target conditioning and base vacuum qualification must not exceed a 45-minute setup window to maintain process throughput; any outgassing delays or prolonged target pre-sputtering consume costly high-purity argon inventory and reduce target campaign life prior to active M1 metallization runs.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Incomplete target native oxide stripping causing catastrophic micro-arcing, target nodule formation, and particle fallout onto wafer surfaces during initial metallization.
1. Chamber vacuum leak or cryopump regeneration saturation leading to base pressure hang above 2.0E-6 Torr and oxygen getter-induced film embrittlement.
1. Shutter cross-talk or mechanical shutter gap leakage depositing contaminated pre-sputtered Al-Cu debris onto loadlock transfer stages or idle substrates.

Initiate high-vacuum pump-down and record chamber total pressure versus time curve over 60 minutes. 2. When pressure drops below 5.0E-6 Torr, power on the RGA filament. 3. Re-open gate valve and confirm ultimate base vacuum recovery. | `Chamber base pressure must reach P_base <= 2.0E-6 Torr within 45 minutes; RGA partial pressure ratio P(18)/P_total < 0.60 and P(32)/P_total < 0.05; chamber pressure rise rate during 120-second isolation <= 1.5E-7 Torr/sec.` |

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved, cleanroom-grade), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses or full-face shield during target view-port inspection, Class 100 / ISO 5 full cleanroom bunny suit with ESD-safe conductive footwear, Dielectric insulating safety gloves when servicing high-voltage DC magnetron cathode connectors (interlocked)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Argon is a simple asphyxiant: If dizziness, hypoxia, or unconsciousness occurs, immediately remove victim to fresh air, administer supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored, initiate CPR if breathing stops, and contact emergency medical response. For high-voltage shock, secure power breaker, perform electrical lockout/tagout, check vital signs, and seek urgent medical evaluation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous vacuum roughing pump line vented into scrubbed facility house exhaust with fail-safe check valves; gas cabinet and chase equipped with continuous oxygen depletion sensors (alarm trip threshold < 19.5% O2) linked to automatic argon shutoff valves.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Target erosion shavings, spent Al-Cu target remnants, and chamber shield wipe particulates must be segregated into sealed, labeled metallic hazardous solid waste containers for metal recovery and toxic solid reclamation according to local industrial waste regulations.

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`

- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time allows atmospheric moisture and oxygen re-adsorption onto chamber walls, target surfaces, and incoming wafer Ti/TiN barrier layers, inducing interfacial titanium oxide formation and high contact resistance (> 100 Ohm per contact via).

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full qualification and signoff of the Al-0.5% Cu target pre-clean and chamber base vacuum state, ensuring that the PVD deposition environment achieves base pressure <= 2.0E-6 Torr, low residual moisture/oxygen background, and stable target discharge prior to opening the shutter for active 180nm DRAM interconnect metallization.
