# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: SOP-PKG-MET-001  
**Title:** Manual Analytical Die Probe Station & Multi-Pin Probe Card Procurement & Acceptance  
**Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) | Architecture & Integration > Interconnect Sputtering & Die Packaging Probe Station > Manual Analytical Die Probe Station & Multi-Pin Probe Card Procurement  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Purpose & Scope
This SOP defines the technical procurement, configuration, and verification steps for a manual analytical die probe station and custom multi-pin probe card assembly. The system performs characterization, parametric extraction, and wafer/die-level electrical verification (leakage current, bitline precharge, sense amplifier differential readout margin) for the 180nm open-source DRAM architecture.

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                           PROCUREMENT & VERIFICATION FLOW                         |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  [Step 1] Mechanical & Thermal Specification Review (180nm pitch, 85°C chuck)     |
|                                       v                                           |
|  [Step 2] Probe Card & Low-Noise Triaxial / Coaxial Interface Configuration       |
|                                       v                                           |
|  [Step 3] Instrument Docking, Triaxial Calibration & Shielding Verification       |
|                                       v                                           |
|  [Step 4] Parametric Metrology & Acceptance Testing (Leakage, Margin, Retention)  |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 1: Tool Specification & Dimensional Sizing
1. Specify an anti-vibration manual analytical probe station equipped with a high-planarity vacuum chuck supporting bare die and wafer coupons up to 150/200 mm.
2. Ensure thermal chuck integration capable of steady-state heating to **85°C** (required for elevated-temperature retention and sub-threshold leakage validation).
3. Confirm high-magnification optical stereo/compound microscope optics capable of resolving metal pad pitches corresponding to 180nm design rules (interconnect pitch scaling from line/contact pitch of ~360 nm to 400 nm).

#### Step 2: Multi-Pin Probe Card & Manipulator Tooling Configuration
1. Design multi-pin probe card / cantilever or vertical needle array matched to die pad layout (pads for $V_{DD}$, $V_{SS}$, Wordline, complementary Bitlines $BL$ and $/BL$, and Sense Amplifier control signals $SAN$/$SAP$).
2. Require triaxial cabling and guarded needle fixtures for low-current measurement paths to isolate sensitive access-transistor sub-threshold and junction leakages.
3. Configure coaxial RF/high-speed lines for transient differential signal readout and pulse-based precharge testing ($V_{DD}/2$).

#### Step 3: Mechanical & Electrical Installation Calibration
1. Level the manual chuck to ensure planar contact across multi-pin probe tips with probe scrub mark depth not exceeding top-metal stack limits.
2. Connect triaxial shields to common instrument guards; verify that residual system floor noise with needles lifted is $\le 10\text{ fA}$ at ambient conditions.
3. Verify microscope illumination and micromanipulator $X\text{-}Y\text{-}Z$ backlash control (< 1 µm precision) to avoid pad tearing during touchdown.

#### Step 4: Physical Acceptance Run on Test Structures
1. Load a baseline 180nm test coupon containing access transistor arrays ($W = 220\text{ nm}$, $L = 180\text{ nm}$) and 1T1C storage capacitor test elements.
2. Heat the chuck to **85°C** and run sub-threshold/junction leakage sweep down to target levels.
3. Execute differential readout margin extraction on test cells with cell capacitance $C_s \approx 25\text{ fF}$ to $28\text{ fF}$ and bitline capacitance $C_{BL} \approx 250\text{ fF}$ to verify precharge and readout behavior.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Physical Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Chuck Thermal Stability** | $85.0 \pm 1.0$ | °C | Integrated RTD/thermocouple surface measurement on heated vacuum chuck |
| **System Leakage Measurement Floor** | $< 1.0$ | fA/cell | Direct picoammeter / SMU measurement with triaxial guarding at 85°C chuck temperature |
| **Cell Capacitance Parametric Extraction** | $25.0 \text{ to } 30.0$ | fF | Quasi-static / high-frequency C-V meter sweep on 1T1C stacked capacitor structures |
| **Sense Readout Differential Voltage Margin ($\Delta V$)** | $100 \text{ to } 150$ | mV | Oscilloscope / SMU pulse measurement across $BL$ and $/BL$ at precharge $V_{DD}/2$ |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

The physical parameters and operating conditions in this SOP are directly grounded in the provided literature:

1. **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
   - Access transistor dimensions: $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
   - Capacitance budget: Minimum $28\text{ fF}$ per cell (dielectric $\kappa > 15$).
   - Leakage target: Sub-threshold and junction leakage $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
2. **Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout**:
   - Precharge condition: Equalized to $V_{DD}/2$.
   - Readout network dynamics: For cell capacitance $C_s = 25\text{ fF}$ and bitline capacitance $C_{BL} = 250\text{ fF}$, differential readout signal $\Delta V = 100\text{ mV}$ to $150\text{ mV}$.
3. **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**:
   - Storage capacitance bounds: $25\text{ to } 30\text{ fF}$ per cell to ensure data retention $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Interconnect scale: Bitline and wordline pitch of $360\text{ nm to } 400\text{ nm}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The procurement specification for the manual analytical probe station and multi-pin probe card must resolve mechanical isolation and stage vibration damping (<0.5 µm amplitude under 10-100 Hz floor noise) on an optical floating table. Integrating multi-pin probe cards (epoxy cantilever or vertical cobra type) onto a manual X-Y-Z-Theta chuck requires precise platen planarity adjustment (<3 µm across 150mm chuck area) and controlled Z-overdrive repeatability (±1 µm) to avoid micro-cracking the 180nm DRAM passivation (Si3N4/SiO2) or tearing underlying M1/M2 metallization during touch-down.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For 180nm open-source DRAM electrical parameter verification, probe card pin layout must account for parasitic capacitance (<1.5 pF per needle) and trace inductance (<5 nH) to accurately capture wordline write pulses, bitline sense-amplifier precharge levels, and low-level retention leakage (<10 fA/cell). Tungsten-rhenium (WRe) or beryllium-copper (BeCu) cantilever needles must maintain scrub marks within 20% of the 60 µm x 60 µm Al/Cu bond pads without punch-through into inter-layer dielectric (ILD).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom multi-pin DRAM probe cards with tight pitch requirements have an 8 to 12-week lead time and single-source supplier exposure. Procurement must secure spare probe cards, needle alignment and planarization jigs, ceramic blade replacement kits, and standardize chuck interface to dual-purpose 100mm/150mm wafers to avoid single-vendor lock-in and production halting upon needle bending or mechanical fatigue.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The capital expenditure and delivery schedule for the analytical station must align with the post-sputtering metallization tape-out milestone. Acceptance testing (FAT/SAT) requires immediate execution upon delivery; delays in vendor sign-off on optical microscope resolution, micro-positioner drift, or triaxial BNC/SMA low-leakage dark box cabling will block initial wafer-level parametric sorting and Gen 2 cell array characterization.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Probe needle excessive scrub or Z-overdrive punch-through cracking the thin inter-layer dielectric (ILD) under DRAM bond pads, causing wordline/bitline short circuits.
1. Excessive electrical leakage (>100 fA) and parasitic capacitance in the station platen/triaxial wiring, masking low-current DRAM cell retention degradation.
1. Vibrational or thermal chuck drift exceeding 1.5 µm during 4-point probe test sequences, causing needle slip off the pad and physical scratch shorts across adjacent 180nm metal lines.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-2-01` | **Probe Platen Planarity and Multi-Pin Contact Resistance Uniformity** | Mitutoyo digital dial indicator (0.1 µm resolution), Keithley 4200A-SCS Parameter Analyzer, Au-coated calibration wafer with 60 µm x 60 µm pitch array, Mitutoyo FS-70 optical microscope. | 1. Mount the Au-coated test substrate onto the 150mm vacuum chuck and engage vacuum at -80 kPa. 2. Sweep the dial indicator across chuck extremities (X=0 to 150mm, Y=0 to 150mm) to record physical platen tilt. 3. Adjust Theta and planarity micrometer screws until total indicator reading (TIR) across chuck is minimized. 4. Lower multi-pin probe card to initiate contact at first electrical touch on all pins. 5. Apply 50 µm Z-overdrive. 6. Execute 4-wire Kelvin resistance measurement across all test pins using the Keithley 4200A-SCS at 10 mA forced current. 7. Disengage probe card and inspect scrub mark dimensions under 50x optical magnification. | `Total chuck platen tilt across 150mm diameter must be <= 3.0 µm. Contact resistance on all probe card channels must be <= 1.2 Ohms with standard deviation <= 0.15 Ohms. Scrub mark length on pads must be between 8 µm and 15 µm with zero dielectric punch-through.` |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-2-02` | **Chuck Isolation and Low-Current Residual Triaxial Leakage Verification** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer with High-Resolution SMUs (HRSMU), Triaxial Low-Noise Cabling, Faraday Dark Box Enclosure, Agilent 34401A DMM. | 1. Connect triaxial force, sense, and guard lines from HRSMU 1 to probe needle 1, and HRSMU 2 to the chuck isolated conductive base. 2. Lift probe card needles 1000 µm above chuck surface into ambient dark box atmosphere. 3. Close and latch Faraday cage door, turning off all internal illumination. 4. Force voltage sweep on Needle 1 from -5.0 V to +5.0 V in 100 mV increments, holding 1.0 s per step. 5. Measure residual leakage current across 10 independent channels. 6. Repeat voltage ramp with chuck biased at +100 V DC to measure chuck-to-ground isolation resistance. | `Open-circuit background leakage current on all probe channels must be <= 20 fA across the full -5.0 V to +5.0 V range. Chuck-to-ground isolation resistance at 100 V DC bias must exceed 1.0 x 10^13 Ohms.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloving), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV and impact-resistant safety glasses, Anti-static ESD lab coat with continuous wrist grounding strap, Cleanroom bouffant cap and ESD-rated conductive safety shoes
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin/eye contact with IPA solvent during chuck cleaning: Flush affected eyes or skin immediately with copious deionized water for at least 15 minutes at the emergency eyewash station. For probe needle puncture or skin laceration: Cleanse wound immediately with antiseptic wash, apply pressure to stop bleeding, and seek immediate medical evaluation for potential metal sliver contamination. For N2 asphyxiation risk: Move victim immediately to fresh air; administer oxygen or CPR if breathing has stopped.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Localized chemical exhaust hood (minimum 100 CFM face velocity) during manual chuck solvent wipe-down. Continuous cleanroom laminar flow hood (Class 100 / ISO 5) over probe station stage with oxygen deficiency monitoring system (<19.5% O2 alarm threshold for N2 pneumatic lines).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Dispose of IPA-saturated cleanroom wipes and lint-free swabs into designated, grounded, fire-rated stainless steel flammable solid waste cans. Empty solvent wash bottles collected for licensed chemical waste incineration. Decommissioned probe needles collected in dedicated puncture-resistant sharps biohazard/metal containers.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI/Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (N2 Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (Grade 5.0) | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Sputtered Al-0.5%Cu or TiN/Al-Si-Cu top metallization with patterned and cured Si3N4/SiO2 passivation openings; pad surface clean, dry, and free of native oxide film build-up (>2 nm) or organic resist residues.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Electrically probed die pads exhibiting controlled mechanical scrub impressions (<15 µm length, <0.2 µm depth) without exposed underlying barrier metal, particulate debris, or moisture condensation.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air exposure limits causes native aluminum oxide (Al2O3) growth (>3.5 nm) on bond pads, driving contact resistance >10 Ohms and inducing probe needle chatter, micro-arcing, and erroneous sense amplifier open-circuit failures.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full site acceptance, mechanical calibration, and electrical qualification of the manual analytical probe station and custom DRAM multi-pin probe card, demonstrating platen planarity <=3 µm, per-channel leakage <=20 fA, and repeatable Kelvin contact resistance <=1.2 Ohms across 180nm DRAM test pads.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `PROBE_STATION_FAT_SAT_ACCEPTANCE_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `MULTI_PIN_CONTACT_RESISTANCE_KELVIN_MATRIX.csv`
- [ ] `NEEDLE_SCRUB_OPTICAL_MICROSCOPY_INSPECTION.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Vacuum chuck mechanical planarity across 150mm active wafer area** | `2.5` | +0.5/-1.0 µm | Dial indicator surface profilometry sweep across X/Y orthogonal axes with -80 kPa vacuum engaged. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Dark box channel-to-channel baseline electrical leakage current at 5V DC bias** | `15.0` | +5.0/-10.0 fA | Triaxial parameter analyzer (Keithley 4200A) multi-channel current-voltage ramp test in sealed dark box. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Four-wire Kelvin contact resistance per probe card needle on Au/Al test pads** | `0.95` | ±0.25 Ohms | Automated 4-wire Kelvin measurement under 50 µm calibrated Z-overdrive across all 32 multi-pin card channels. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 3 quantitative assertions verified with zero non-conformances; contact resistance standard deviation <=0.15 Ohms across all needle channels; dark box leakage <=20 fA at ±5V; scrub mark inspection confirming <20% pad area deformation without barrier layer breach; signed acceptance by Lead Metrology Researcher and Systems Engineer.

critics.systems_engineer: The procurement specification for the manual analytical probe station and multi-pin probe card must resolve mechanical isolation and stage vibration damping (<0.5 µm amplitude under 10-100 Hz floor noise) on an optical floating table. Integrating multi-pin probe cards (epoxy cantilever or vertical cobra type) onto a manual X-Y-Z-Theta chuck requires precise platen planarity adjustment (<3 µm across 150mm chuck area) and controlled Z-overdrive repeatability (±1 µm) to avoid micro-cracking the 180nm DRAM passivation (Si3N4/SiO2) or tearing underlying M1/M2 metallization during touch-down.
critics.domain_expert: For 180nm open-source DRAM electrical parameter verification, probe card pin layout must account for parasitic capacitance (<1.5 pF per needle) and trace inductance (<5 nH) to accurately capture wordline write pulses, bitline sense-amplifier precharge levels, and low-level retention leakage (<10 fA/cell). Tungsten-rhenium (WRe) or beryllium-copper (BeCu) cantilever needles must maintain scrub marks within 20% of the 60 µm x 60 µm Al/Cu bond pads without punch-through into inter-layer dielectric (ILD).
critics.supply_chain: Custom multi-pin DRAM probe cards with tight pitch requirements have an 8 to 12-week lead time and single-source supplier exposure. Procurement must secure spare probe cards, needle alignment and planarization jigs, ceramic blade replacement kits, and standardize chuck interface to dual-purpose 100mm/150mm wafers to avoid single-vendor lock-in and production halting upon needle bending or mechanical fatigue.
critics.laya_pm: The capital expenditure and delivery schedule for the analytical station must align with the post-sputtering metallization tape-out milestone. Acceptance testing (FAT/SAT) requires immediate execution upon delivery; delays in vendor sign-off on optical microscope resolution, micro-positioner drift, or triaxial BNC/SMA low-leakage dark box cabling will block initial wafer-level parametric sorting and Gen 2 cell array characterization.
critical_failure_modes: Probe needle excessive scrub or Z-overdrive punch-through cracking the thin inter-layer dielectric (ILD) under DRAM bond pads, causing wordline/bitline short circuits.
Excessive electrical leakage (>100 fA) and parasitic capacitance in the station platen/triaxial wiring, masking low-current DRAM cell retention degradation.
Vibrational or thermal chuck drift exceeding 1.5 µm during 4-point probe test sequences, causing needle slip off the pad and physical scratch shorts across adjacent 180nm metal lines.

testcases.title: Probe Platen Planarity and Multi-Pin Contact Resistance Uniformity
testcases.instrumentation: Mitutoyo digital dial indicator (0.1 µm resolution), Keithley 4200A-SCS Parameter Analyzer, Au-coated calibration wafer with 60 µm x 60 µm pitch array, Mitutoyo FS-70 optical microscope.
testcases.pre_conditions: Pneumatic vibration isolation table floated at 4.5 bar N2. Dark box sealed, temperature stabilized at 25°C ± 0.5°C. Multi-pin probe card mounted and coarse leveled.
testcases.procedure: 1. Mount the Au-coated test substrate onto the 150mm vacuum chuck and engage vacuum at -80 kPa. 2. Sweep the dial indicator across chuck extremities (X=0 to 150mm, Y=0 to 150mm) to record physical platen tilt. 3. Adjust Theta and planarity micrometer screws until total indicator reading (TIR) across chuck is minimized. 4. Lower multi-pin probe card to initiate contact at first electrical touch on all pins. 5. Apply 50 µm Z-overdrive. 6. Execute 4-wire Kelvin resistance measurement across all test pins using the Keithley 4200A-SCS at 10 mA forced current. 7. Disengage probe card and inspect scrub mark dimensions under 50x optical magnification.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Total chuck platen tilt across 150mm diameter must be <= 3.0 µm. Contact resistance on all probe card channels must be <= 1.2 Ohms with standard deviation <= 0.15 Ohms. Scrub mark length on pads must be between 8 µm and 15 µm with zero dielectric punch-through.

testcases.title: Chuck Isolation and Low-Current Residual Triaxial Leakage Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer with High-Resolution SMUs (HRSMU), Triaxial Low-Noise Cabling, Faraday Dark Box Enclosure, Agilent 34401A DMM.
testcases.pre_conditions: Probe station enclosed in grounded Faraday cage (shield resistance < 0.1 Ohm to earth). Vacuum chuck empty and clean. Ambient relative humidity controlled at 45% ± 5%.
testcases.procedure: 1. Connect triaxial force, sense, and guard lines from HRSMU 1 to probe needle 1, and HRSMU 2 to the chuck isolated conductive base. 2. Lift probe card needles 1000 µm above chuck surface into ambient dark box atmosphere. 3. Close and latch Faraday cage door, turning off all internal illumination. 4. Force voltage sweep on Needle 1 from -5.0 V to +5.0 V in 100 mV increments, holding 1.0 s per step. 5. Measure residual leakage current across 10 independent channels. 6. Repeat voltage ramp with chuck biased at +100 V DC to measure chuck-to-ground isolation resistance.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Open-circuit background leakage current on all probe channels must be <= 20 fA across the full -5.0 V to +5.0 V range. Chuck-to-ground isolation resistance at 100 V DC bias must exceed 1.0 x 10^13 Ohms.

ppe_required: Class 100 Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloving)
ANSI Z87.1 certified UV and impact-resistant safety glasses
Anti-static ESD lab coat with continuous wrist grounding strap
Cleanroom bouffant cap and ESD-rated conductive safety shoes
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: For skin/eye contact with IPA solvent during chuck cleaning: Flush affected eyes or skin immediately with copious deionized water for at least 15 minutes at the emergency eyewash station. For probe needle puncture or skin laceration: Cleanse wound immediately with antiseptic wash, apply pressure to stop bleeding, and seek immediate medical evaluation for potential metal sliver contamination. For N2 asphyxiation risk: Move victim immediately to fresh air; administer oxygen or CPR if breathing has stopped.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Localized chemical exhaust hood (minimum 100 CFM face velocity) during manual chuck solvent wipe-down. Continuous cleanroom laminar flow hood (Class 100 / ISO 5) over probe station stage with oxygen deficiency monitoring system (<19.5% O2 alarm threshold for N2 pneumatic lines).
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Dispose of IPA-saturated cleanroom wipes and lint-free swabs into designated, grounded, fire-rated stainless steel flammable solid waste cans. Empty solvent wash bottles collected for licensed chemical waste incineration. Decommissioned probe needles collected in dedicated puncture-resistant sharps biohazard/metal containers.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Sputtered Al-0.5%Cu or TiN/Al-Si-Cu top metallization with patterned and cured Si3N4/SiO2 passivation openings; pad surface clean, dry, and free of native oxide film build-up (>2 nm) or organic resist residues.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Electrically probed die pads exhibiting controlled mechanical scrub impressions (<15 µm length, <0.2 µm depth) without exposed underlying barrier metal, particulate debris, or moisture condensation.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding air exposure limits causes native aluminum oxide (Al2O3) growth (>3.5 nm) on bond pads, driving contact resistance >10 Ohms and inducing probe needle chatter, micro-arcing, and erroneous sense amplifier open-circuit failures.

expected_result.summary: Full site acceptance, mechanical calibration, and electrical qualification of the manual analytical probe station and custom DRAM multi-pin probe card, demonstrating platen planarity <=3 µm, per-channel leakage <=20 fA, and repeatable Kelvin contact resistance <=1.2 Ohms across 180nm DRAM test pads.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Vacuum chuck mechanical planarity across 150mm active wafer area
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Dial indicator surface profilometry sweep across X/Y orthogonal axes with -80 kPa vacuum engaged.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Dark box channel-to-channel baseline electrical leakage current at 5V DC bias
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Triaxial parameter analyzer (Keithley 4200A) multi-channel current-voltage ramp test in sealed dark box.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Four-wire Kelvin contact resistance per probe card needle on Au/Al test pads
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Automated 4-wire Kelvin measurement under 50 µm calibrated Z-overdrive across all 32 multi-pin card channels.

expected_result.signoff_criteria: All 3 quantitative assertions verified with zero non-conformances; contact resistance standard deviation <=0.15 Ohms across all needle channels; dark box leakage <=20 fA at ±5V; scrub mark inspection confirming <20% pad area deformation without barrier layer breach; signed acceptance by Lead Metrology Researcher and Systems Engineer.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
**Document Code:** `SOP-180DRAM-MET-007`  
**Title:** Interconnect Contact Resistance & Wafer-Level Electrical Die Probing (EDP)  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm) / 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip  
**Module:** Interconnect Sputtering & Die Packaging Probe Station [Back-End Packaging / Metrology]  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### Process Flow Overview
```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Wafer Loading &     │
│       Alignment        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   TLM 4-Point Kelvin   │
│        Probing         │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│       Parameter        │
│  Extraction: Rc, Rs,   │
│         rho_c          │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   EDP Die Functional   │
│    Screen & Leakage    │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Electronic Wafer Map  │
│        Binning         │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Wafer Alignment & Probe Card Setup:**
   - Mount the 180nm DRAM processed wafer onto the motorized thermal vacuum chuck of the automatic electrical probe station.
   - Adjust chuck temperature setpoint to $85^\circ\text{C}$ for hot-carrier and junction retention screening.
   - Perform optical two-point pattern recognition on the wafer alignment fiducials and planarize the probe needle tips onto the on-chip test structure pads ($100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ aluminum square bond pads and TLM test arrays).

2. **Transmission Line Measurement (TLM) Probing:**
   - Step the probe tips onto the inline scribe-line TLM structure arrays consisting of identical rectangular contact pads (pad width $W = 100\,\mu\text{m}$, pad length $L_{\text{pad}} = 50\,\mu\text{m}$) spaced at progressively increasing gaps:
     $$d \in \{5\,\mu\text{m},\, 10\,\mu\text{m},\, 20\,\mu\text{m},\, 40\,\mu\text{m},\, 80\,\mu\text{m}\}$$
   - Apply a 4-point Kelvin DC current sweep through adjacent pad pairs and record total loop resistance $R_T$ across each gap $d$.

3. **Contact Parameter & Resistivity Extraction:**
   - Execute a linear regression fit of measured total resistance $R_T$ against gap spacing $d$ based on the transmission line formulation:
     $$R_T = 2 R_c + \left(\frac{R_s}{W}\right) d$$
   - Extract the slope $m = R_s / W$ to calculate diffusion sheet resistance $R_s$.
   - Extract the Y-intercept at $d = 0$ to calculate twice the contact resistance ($2 R_c$), yielding contact resistance $R_c$.
   - Extract the negative X-intercept $-2 L_T$ to obtain transfer length $L_T$.
   - Compute specific contact resistivity:
     $$\rho_c = R_c \cdot W \cdot L_T = R_s \cdot L_T^2 \quad [\Omega\cdot\text{cm}^2]$$

4. **Electrical Die Probing (EDP) Functional & Leakage Screening:**
   - Step the multi-pin probe card to each active DRAM die (access transistor channel length $L = 180\,\text{nm}$, width $W = 220\,\text{nm}$ with stacked capacitor over bitline / W-plug drain contact).
   - Perform capacitance parametric validation on the stacked capacitor structure to ensure the effective dielectric constant ($\kappa > 15$) yields the required cell storage capacitance.
   - Measure cell leakage current (sub-threshold and drain-substrate junction leakage) at $85^\circ\text{C}$ across memory cell arrays.
   - Generate an Electronic Wafer Map (EWM) classifying Known Good Die (KGD) ready for subsequent die sawing, silver-filled conductive epoxy die attach, and ultrasonic wedge / gold ball wire bonding.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                    ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
                    │░░                                │
   Leakage (<1.0 fA)┤░░                                │
                    │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                           │
      Die Void (<5%)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                           │
Bond Pull (>=4.0 gf)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓                            │
                    │▓▓▓▓▓▓                            │
    C_cell (>=28 fF)┤██████████████████████████████████│
                    │██████████████████████████████████│
                    └┬───────┬────────┬───────┬───────┬┘
                     0       7       14      21      28 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Physical Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cell Storage Capacitance ($C_{\text{cell}}$)** | $\ge 28.0$ | $\text{fF/cell}$ | Multi-frequency C-V parameter analyzer on stacked capacitor test macro |
| **Junction & Sub-threshold Leakage** | $< 1.0$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Sub-picoamp precision parametric electrometer on bitline/cell array |
| **TLM Contact Pad Geometry & Array Gaps** | $W = 100 \pm 0.5$, $L_{\text{pad}} = 50 \pm 0.5$; gaps $d = 5, 10, 20, 40, 80$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Optical inline metrology / calibrated probe station displacement |
| **Downstream Wire Bond Pull Strength** | $\ge 4.0$ (span break mode) | $\text{gf}$ (grams-force) | Calibrated wire bond pull tester (Mil-Std-883 Method 2011) |

---

### Verified Context Citations
1. **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:**
   - Confirms unit cell dimensions ($L = 180\,\text{nm}$, $W = 220\,\text{nm}$), stacked capacitor over bitline via tungsten plug (W-plug), effective dielectric constant $\kappa > 15$, minimum storage capacitance budget of $\ge 28\,\text{fF/cell}$, and maximum leakage current limit $< 1\,\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
2. **Transmission Line Measurement (TLM) for Specific Contact Resistivity:**
   - Establishes TLM contact pad dimensions ($W = 100\,\mu\text{m}$, $L_{\text{pad}} = 50\,\mu\text{m}$) and spacing set ($d = 5, 10, 20, 40, 80\,\mu\text{m}$), linear regression equations ($R_T = 2R_c + (R_s/W)d$), transfer length derivation ($L_T$), and specific contact resistivity formula ($\rho_c = R_c W L_T = R_s L_T^2$).
3. **Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging:**
   - Establishes pad dimensions ($100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ Al pads), wire diameter ($25\,\mu\text{m}$), wire bond pull strength acceptance threshold ($\ge 4.0\,\text{gf}$ per Mil-Std-883 Method 2011), and die attach acoustic void area threshold ($< 5\%$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Contact resistance (Rc) and sheet resistance (Rs) extracted via the TLM array must maintain strict parametric decoupling from the wafer prober's chuck parasitic resistance and probe needle contact resistance (R_probe < 0.5 Ohm). For 180nm COB DRAM architectures, any uncalibrated contact resistance at the tungsten bitline plug interface directly degrades sense amplifier sensing margins, causing false read-disturb bit flips during low-voltage (1.8V VDD) activation cycles.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Specific contact resistivity (rho_c) for Ti/TiN/W plug contacts to n+ active diffusion must satisfy rho_c <= 5.0e-7 Ohm*cm^2. When extracting transfer length (L_T) and contact end resistance via linear regression of R_T vs. gap spacing (d = 5, 10, 20, 40, 80 um), probe scrub marks must not exceed 15% of pad area (W = 100 um, L_pad = 50 um) to prevent mechanical punch-through into underlying inter-layer dielectric (ILD-1 BPSG/TEOS).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom multi-pitch Kelvin cantilever/vertical probe cards for 180nm DRAM test structures feature lead times of 12-16 weeks and rely on precision tungsten-rhenium (WRe) needles. To mitigate localized supply bottleneck risks in Southeast Asia, the EDP station must implement dual-source qualification for ceramic-blade cantilever probe heads and maintain an in-house inventory of alumina abrasive cleaning pads (grit size 1 um to 3 um) to extend needle tip MTBF beyond 500,000 touchdowns.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: EDP throughput directly determines back-end turnaround time. Probing 5-point TLM structures across 24 test-element group (TEG) sites on a 200mm wafer must execute within 180 seconds total chuck stepping and indexing time. Failure to automate Kelvin switching matrix routing will stall lot progression into dicing and die-attach stages.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dielectric punch-through and micro-cracking beneath contact pads caused by excessive probe overdrive (> 45 um) or needle tip misalignment, causing substrate short circuits.
1. Native oxide re-growth (> 1.2 nm SiO2) on unpassivated test pads due to Q-time violation prior to probing, leading to non-linear Schottky-like I-V behavior and invalid TLM linear regressions.
1. Probe tip contamination and aluminum/tungsten pick-up causing elevated contact resistance (delta R_probe > 1.5 Ohm) across sequential wafer maps.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-3-01` | **4-Wire Kelvin TLM Specific Contact Resistivity (rho_c) and Sheet Resistance (Rs) Extraction** | Semi-automatic 200mm cryogenic-shielded wafer probe station (MPI/FormFactor), Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer with high-resolution SMUs (B1517A), 4-point Kelvin tungsten-rhenium probe tips (tip radius 12 um). | 1. Step probe station to TLM TEG macro at center die (Die 0,0). 2. Land Kelvin force/sense probes onto Pad 1 and Pad 2 (d = 5 um). 3. Force DC current sweep from -1.0 mA to +1.0 mA in 50 uA increments; record differential voltage V_sense to confirm Ohmic linearity (R^2 > 0.999). 4. Repeat 4-point resistance measurement across sequential gaps: d = 10 um, 20 um, 40 um, and 80 um. 5. Perform least-squares linear regression of total resistance R_T vs. d: extract slope (Rs / W) and Y-intercept (2 * Rc). 6. Calculate transfer length L_T = |X-intercept| / 2 and specific contact resistivity rho_c = Rc * W * L_T. 7. Execute across 9 standardized wafer zones (center, 4 mid-radius, 4 edge). | `Ohmic linearity R^2 >= 0.9990 for all current sweeps; Specific contact resistivity rho_c <= 5.0e-7 Ohm*cm^2; Diffusion sheet resistance Rs = 35.0 +/- 4.0 Ohm/sq; Extracted Rc <= 8.5 Ohm; Transfer length L_T between 0.35 um and 0.85 um across >= 95% of tested sites.` |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-3-02` | **Wafer-Level Electrical Die Probing (EDP) Bitline-to-Substrate Isolation & Contact Leakage** | Keysight B1505A / B1500A Parameter Analyzer with ultra-low leakage SMU (femtosecond current resolution), automated thermal probe chuck set to 85.0 +/- 0.2 °C. | 1. Step to EDP cell array test macro across 100% of functional die reticles. 2. Land probe array on bitline contact pad and adjacent p-well tap. 3. Apply V_stress = 2.2 V (120% nominal VDD) between bitline contact plug and p-well substrate for 500 ms. 4. Measure steady-state DC leakage current I_leak at V_nominal = 1.8 V for a sampling integration period of 200 ms. 5. Record leakage across 1,024 parallel bitline contact chains. 6. Generate wafer-level binning map classifying dies by leakage current bands. | `Array bitline contact leakage current at 85 °C must be <= 1.0 fA per individual DRAM cell contact node (equivalent to <= 1.024 pA per 1,024-contact chain test macro). Catastrophic dielectric breakdown (I_leak > 1.0 uA at 2.2 V) must be 0% across prime functional zones.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Class 100 (ISO 5) nitrile gloves with electrostatic discharge (ESD) dissipative coating, ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact-resistant safety glasses with side shields, Conductive ESD lab coat with grounded heel straps, Vapor respirator (half-mask with organic vapor/acid gas cartridge) during solvent cleaning of chuck
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Flush eyes immediately with copious amounts of tempered water at eyewash station for >= 15 minutes while holding eyelids open. Skin contact: Wash affected dermal areas with mild non-abrasive soap and water. Inhalation: Relocate personnel immediately to fresh air; administer oxygen if breathing becomes labored. Ingestion: Do not induce vomiting; rinse mouth thoroughly with water and seek emergency medical attention immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Probe station enclosed in laminar airflow hood (HEPA filtered, face velocity 0.45 +/- 0.05 m/s). Solvent wipe staging bench connected to local dedicated VOC chemical exhaust maintaining minimum capture duct velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM). Chuck thermal purge venting routed to scrubbed cleanroom exhaust.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent solvent-saturated wipes (IPA/acetone) must be disposed of in dedicated airtight, self-closing FM-approved flammables waste receptacles with grounding wires. Flammable liquid residues collected in marked DOT-approved polyethylene drums for hazardous solvent incineration. Zero drain disposal permitted.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic / Semiconductor Grade (VLSI) | `>= 99.9%` |
| **Acetone** | `67-64-1` | Electronic / Semiconductor Grade (VLSI) | `>= 99.5%` |
| **Nitrogen (Gas, Cryogenic Boil-off)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity Grade 6.0 | `>= 99.9999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly completed metallization/contact etch-and-sputter (Ti/TiN barrier and W/Al metallization), with post-CMP surface cleaned and dried, free of slurry residues and native oxide thickness < 0.5 nm.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Electrically probed pads exhibiting controlled scrub marks (< 15% pad area), passivated under dry N2 flow, free from metallic probe debris, ready for final passivation layer deposition or wafer dicing.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive atmospheric exposure causes native oxide formation (> 1.5 nm SiO2) on open contact vias and pad metallization oxidation, producing non-Ohmic contact behavior, false TLM contact resistance failures, and irreversible aluminum pad corrosion.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full wafer-level parametric characterization and electrical validation of contact resistance (Rc), specific contact resistivity (rho_c), diffusion sheet resistance (Rs), and bitline leakage across 180nm DRAM test vehicles, providing statistical baseline certification for DRAM Foundation VN lot signoff.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `EDP_TLM_Parametric_Extraction_Report_Lot180.pdf`
- [ ] `Wafer_Map_Contact_Resistivity_Distribution_Raw.csv`
- [ ] `Probe_Scrub_Mark_Optical_Inspection_HighRes.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Specific contact resistivity rho_c extracted from 4-wire TLM linear regression across the wafer** | `3.5e-7 Ohm*cm^2` | <= 5.0e-7 Ohm*cm^2 maximum limit | Automated Keysight B1500A 4-point Kelvin I-V sweep across 5-gap TLM structures with least-squares linear fit R^2 >= 0.9990. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Extracted n+ diffusion sheet resistance Rs from TLM slope parameter** | `35.0 Ohm/sq` | +/- 4.0 Ohm/sq (31.0 to 39.0 Ohm/sq) | Regression slope extraction (Slope = Rs / W, where W = 100 um) calculated across 9 sites per wafer. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Individual DRAM cell node leakage current under 1.8V VDD at 85 °C chuck temperature** | `0.45 fA/cell` | <= 1.0 fA/cell maximum threshold | Triaxial-shielded ultra-low-current SMU sampling of 1,024-node bitline contact test macro scaled per unit cell. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> A minimum of 95% of tested dies on the 200mm wafer must meet rho_c <= 5.0e-7 Ohm*cm^2, Rs within 31.0 - 39.0 Ohm/sq, and per-cell leakage <= 1.0 fA at 85 °C, with all raw .csv and summary .pdf deliverables archived and signed off by the Lead Metrology Engineer and Systems Integration Council.

Perform least-squares linear regression of total resistance R_T vs. d: extract slope (Rs / W) and Y-intercept (2 * Rc). 6. Calculate transfer length L_T = |X-intercept| / 2 and specific contact resistivity rho_c = Rc * W * L_T. 7. Execute across 9 standardized wafer zones (center, 4 mid-radius, 4 edge).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Ohmic linearity R^2 >= 0.9990 for all current sweeps; Specific contact resistivity rho_c <= 5.0e-7 Ohm*cm^2; Diffusion sheet resistance Rs = 35.0 +/- 4.0 Ohm/sq; Extracted Rc <= 8.5 Ohm; Transfer length L_T between 0.35 um and 0.85 um across >= 95% of tested sites.

testcases.title: Wafer-Level Electrical Die Probing (EDP) Bitline-to-Substrate Isolation & Contact Leakage
testcases.instrumentation: Keysight B1505A / B1500A Parameter Analyzer with ultra-low leakage SMU (femtosecond current resolution), automated thermal probe chuck set to 85.0 +/- 0.2 °C.
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer loaded onto temperature-controlled hot chuck at 85 °C. Chuck dark shield sealed to eliminate optical carrier generation. Triaxial cables calibrated with open-circuit zero-offset compensation (< 10 fA residual baseline).
testcases.procedure: 1. Step to EDP cell array test macro across 100% of functional die reticles. 2. Land probe array on bitline contact pad and adjacent p-well tap. 3. Apply V_stress = 2.2 V (120% nominal VDD) between bitline contact plug and p-well substrate for 500 ms. 4. Measure steady-state DC leakage current I_leak at V_nominal = 1.8 V for a sampling integration period of 200 ms. 5. Record leakage across 1,024 parallel bitline contact chains. 6. Generate wafer-level binning map classifying dies by leakage current bands.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Array bitline contact leakage current at 85 °C must be <= 1.0 fA per individual DRAM cell contact node (equivalent to <= 1.024 pA per 1,024-contact chain test macro). Catastrophic dielectric breakdown (I_leak > 1.0 uA at 2.2 V) must be 0% across prime functional zones.

ppe_required: Cleanroom Class 100 (ISO 5) nitrile gloves with electrostatic discharge (ESD) dissipative coating
ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact-resistant safety glasses with side shields
Conductive ESD lab coat with grounded heel straps
Vapor respirator (half-mask with organic vapor/acid gas cartridge) during solvent cleaning of chuck
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: Eye contact: Flush eyes immediately with copious amounts of tempered water at eyewash station for >= 15 minutes while holding eyelids open. Skin contact: Wash affected dermal areas with mild non-abrasive soap and water. Inhalation: Relocate personnel immediately to fresh air; administer oxygen if breathing becomes labored. Ingestion: Do not induce vomiting; rinse mouth thoroughly with water and seek emergency medical attention immediately.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Probe station enclosed in laminar airflow hood (HEPA filtered, face velocity 0.45 +/- 0.05 m/s). Solvent wipe staging bench connected to local dedicated VOC chemical exhaust maintaining minimum capture duct velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM). Chuck thermal purge venting routed to scrubbed cleanroom exhaust.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Spent solvent-saturated wipes (IPA/acetone) must be disposed of in dedicated airtight, self-closing FM-approved flammables waste receptacles with grounding wires. Flammable liquid residues collected in marked DOT-approved polyethylene drums for hazardous solvent incineration. Zero drain disposal permitted.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## PCM Contact Kelvin & Cross-Bridge Resistor Test Structure Probe Card Alignment

**Process Module:** Metrology / Back-End Packaging  
**Level:** Gen 2 (µm) / 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip  
**Equipment:** Automatic Wafer Prober Station & Multi-Contact Kelvin/Cross-Bridge Probe Card  

---

### 1. Process Flow Overview

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Wafer Loading &     │
│   Vacuum Chuck Clamp   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Optical Pattern     │
│  Recognition & Theta   │
│    Skew Correction     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Planarization      │
│       Planarity        │
│     Verification &     │
│   Z-Contact Sensing    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Kelvin Force-Sense &  │
│      Cross-Bridge      │
│       Structure        │
│      Registration      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Contact Overdrive &   │
│    Electrical Scrub    │
│      Verification      │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Chuck Mount & Thermal Equilibrium**:
   - Transfer the 180nm processed DRAM wafer onto the prober vacuum chuck.
   - Engage vacuum clamp (verify vacuum pressure $\ge 80\text{ kPa}$). Maintain chuck temperature stabilization at the test baseline ($25^\circ\text{C}$ or elevated temperature qualification up to $85^\circ\text{C}$ per DRAM retention and leakage testing context).

2. **Optical Global & Pattern Recognition (PR) Alignment**:
   - Position the dual-magnification microscope camera over the primary wafer alignment fiducials / notch.
   - Execute automatic pattern recognition across scribe line targets to correct rotational theta ($\theta$) skew ($\Delta\theta \le \pm 0.002^\circ$).

3. **Probe Tip Planarity & Z-Reference Touchdown**:
   - Perform probe card planarity mapping across all tungsten carbide / cantilever probe tips (tip radius: $50\text{–}100\ \mu\text{m}$).
   - Set optical $Z_0$ clearance height and perform electric contact sensing against the alignment dummy pad to establish the $Z$-reference plane across all probes.

4. **Kelvin & Cross-Bridge Pad Structure Registration**:
   - Index the stage to the Process Control Monitor (PCM) scribe-line test insert containing:
     - 4-terminal Kelvin contact resistance structures (dedicated force/sense terminals for W-plug and interconnect contacts).
     - Cross-bridge sheet resistor structures ($R_s$ metrology).
   - Align the probe tips concentric with the landing pads to eliminate pad boundary scrub damage.

5. **Z-Overdrive & Electrical Scrub Verification**:
   - Apply recipe-specified vertical stage overdrive ($\Delta Z = 35\text{–}55\ \mu\text{m}$) to penetrate native oxide and achieve stable scrub marks.
   - Inject DC test current ($I = 1.0\text{ mA to } 10.0\text{ mA}$) between outer force terminals and verify potential measurement $V$ across sense terminals to validate contact integrity before triggering automated parametric testing.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value & Tolerance | Physical Unit | Measurement Method / Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Probe Tip Radius Range** | $50 \text{ to } 100$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Optical Metrology / High-Mag Inspection |
| **Wafer Chuck Test Temperature** | $85 \pm 0.5$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Integrated Chuck RTD / Temperature Controller |
| **Kelvin DC Excitation Current Range** | $1.0 \text{ to } 10.0$ | $\text{mA}$ | Parametric SMU Constant Current Source |
| **Scrub Mark Center Travel Alignment** | $\le \pm 5.0$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Automated Post-Touchdown Optical Image Analysis |

---

### 4. Verified Context Citations

- **`Four-Point Collinear Probe Metrology for Semiconductor Sheet Resistance`**:
  - Probe tip material and geometry: Tungsten carbide tips with radius $50\text{–}100\ \mu\text{m}$.
  - Operating principle: Constant DC current excitation of $I = 1\text{ mA to } 10\text{ mA}$ applied to force paths while inner floating potential difference ($V$) is recorded to resolve sheet resistance $R_s = 4.5324 \times (V / I)\ [\Omega/\square]$.
- **`180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench` & `Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering`**:
  - Interconnect and contact metallurgy: Tungsten plug (W-plug) contact integration.
  - Temperature validation: $85^\circ\text{C}$ thermal target established for DRAM cell junction leakage target ($< 1\text{ fA/cell}$) and data retention ($> 64\text{ ms}$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Probe card planarization and multi-pin contact scrub alignment across 100 um x 50 um Kelvin pads require sub-micron stage optical feedback. Mechanical thermal drift of the cantilever epoxy ring or vertical probe assembly between 20 deg C and 25 deg C will cause contact pitch displacement > 1.5 um, inducing edge punch-through on passivation windows and yielding parasitic series resistance errors.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Kelvin contact resistance (Rc) and cross-bridge sheet resistance (Rs) metrology rely on genuine four-terminal sensing where force and sense paths intersect solely at the metallization-diffusion interface. Probe card scrub marks exceeding 25% of the 50 um pad dimension induce mechanical shear damage into underlying Ti/TiN barrier layers, distorting TLM transfer length (LT) and artificially elevating specific contact resistivity (rho_c) by > 15%.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom multi-DUT cantilever or vertical buckling-beam probe cards with tungsten-rhenium (WRe) or beryllium-copper (BeCu) tips configured for Gen 2 (180nm node PCM) have 12-16 week fabrication lead times from tier-1 vendors (e.g., FormFactor, MPI). Procuring off-the-shelf semi-custom ceramic blade probe cards requires immediate qualification of tip radius (50-100 um) and planarity verification tools to prevent production line stoppages.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Alignment calibration protocols must integrate directly into wafer prober test executive recipes without introducing > 45 seconds of setup overhead per wafer. Total cost of ownership requires tip cleaning abrasive pad refresh schedules to be strictly locked at 250 touchdowns to prevent re-probing delays and schedule slippage across the pilot 180nm open-source wafer run.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Tip scrub overdrive (> 8 um) puncturing the thin aluminum/copper contact pad and cracking underlying inter-metal dielectric (IMD) oxide.
1. Probe planarity delta (> 6 um across card tips) causing open circuits on sense terminals while force terminals experience severe contact over-pressure.
1. Aluminum probe tip buildup/oxidation resulting in high contact resistance variability (> 2.0 Ohm contact jump) mimicking process-induced contact resistivity degradation.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-3-1-01` | **Probe Card Planarity and Optical X-Y Scrub Alignment Verification** | Semi-automated 200mm Wafer Prober (MPI TS200-SE / FormFactor Summit 12000) with motorized theta stage, down-looking optical camera (0.1 um resolution), contact height sensor (LVDT gauge), and precision tungsten-carbide reference planarization coupon. | 1. Load gold-plated reference planarization coupon onto the vacuum chuck and engage 750 Torr hold-down. 2. Perform three-point auto-focus optical theta alignment of the coupon fiducials. 3. Execute vertical tip touch detection using slow approach speed (10 um/sec) with contact resistance threshold sensing (10 mA DC limit). 4. Record Z-height coordinate of electrical contact for all 24 probe tips across the Kelvin and Cross-Bridge array. 5. Apply 50 um vertical overdrive and measure scrub mark footprint length and lateral scrub trajectory in X and Y via calibrated optical pattern metrology. | `Maximum Z-height deviation (tip-to-tip planarity) across all active probes <= 3.5 um; lateral scrub mark length <= 12.0 um centered within +/- 2.5 um of test pad geometric center; zero probe tips landing outside the designated 100 um x 50 um pad boundaries.` |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-3-1-02` | **Four-Terminal Kelvin & Cross-Bridge Electrical Alignment Linearity Check** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer equipped with 4x High Resolution SMUs (B1517A) linked via low-noise triaxial cabling through the prober manipulator to the aligned probe card. | 1. Step probe chuck to wafer PCM test die containing 180nm diffusion TLM structure (pad spacings d = 5, 10, 20, 40, 80 um) and Cross-Bridge Sheet Resistor. 2. Lower probe card to contact position with verified 50 um overdrive. 3. Force DC current I = 1.0 mA through force terminals (Pad 1 to Pad 4) and measure floating potential difference V across sense terminals (Pad 2 to Pad 3). 4. Reverse polarity to I = -1.0 mA to eliminate thermoelectric offset voltages and record V_rev. 5. Extract R_T for each pad gap spacing d, execute linear regression to extract sheet resistance R_s and intercept 2*R_c, and measure cross-bridge resistance R_bridge = (pi / ln(2)) * (V / I). | `Linear regression coefficient R^2 >= 0.998 across d = 5 um to 80 um TLM array; measured residual contact resistance R_c <= 12.5 Ohm per contact; Cross-Bridge sheet resistance repeatability across 5 consecutive touchdowns with standard deviation sigma <= 0.8%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloving required), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/chemical safety splash goggles, Static-dissipative ESD-safe cleanroom smock and hood, ESD wrist strap connected to 1 MOhm common point ground
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin contact with IPA tip-cleaning solvent, immediately flush skin with flowing water for at least 15 minutes while removing contaminated PPE. In case of vapor inhalation causing dizziness, move personnel to fresh cleanroom plenum air or exterior environment. In case of eye contact, flush eyes at the emergency eyewash station for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek immediate medical evaluation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Prober load port and maintenance cleaning bench must operate under local point exhaust ducting maintaining continuous face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) with laminar downflow HEPA filtration maintaining ISO Class 4 cleanliness.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent solvent cleaning wipes and IPA drain residues must be collected in closed, grounded, explosion-proof hazardous solvent waste carboys labeled 'Flammable Solvent Waste - Isopropanol'; do not vent to municipal acid/base scrubbers or drains.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI / Semiconductor Grade (> 99.9%) | `100%` |
| **Deionized Water (DIW)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type 1 Ultra-Pure (> 18.2 MOhm*cm at 25C) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly patterned and unpassivated aluminum/copper contact pads post-metallization etch and ash, free of organic residues and native oxide thickness < 1.5 nm.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Probe-inspected wafer containing localized, controlled tip scrub depressions (< 25% pad area) without exposed barrier cracks, sealed under inert gas.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Native oxidation and ambient airborne moisture exposure on aluminum contact pads form insulating Al2O3 films exceeding 3.0 nm thickness, causing erratic four-terminal probe tip contact, false high R_c readings, and tip scrub slip.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Verification of probe card planarity, tip alignment, and stable four-terminal electrical Kelvin/Cross-bridge metrology ensuring sub-micron probe positioning, repeatable specific contact resistivity (rho_c) extraction, and zero pad damage across the 180nm DRAM test vehicle.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `PCM_ProbeCard_Planarity_Alignment_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `Kelvin_TLM_CrossBridge_Measurement_Data.csv`
- [ ] `Probe_Scrub_Mark_HighRes_Inspection.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Probe card tip-to-tip vertical planarity delta across all 24 pins** | `2.0 um` | +/- 1.5 um | Multi-point Z-height contact sensing against optical gold planarization block on MPI TS200-SE prober |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Probe scrub mark placement error relative to center of 100 um x 50 um Kelvin pad** | `0.0 um` | +/- 2.5 um | High-magnification automated optical pattern recognition inspection recorded in inspection TIFF artifact |
| `ASSERT-03` | **TLM specific contact resistivity linear fit coefficient of determination** | `0.9990` | >= 0.9980 | Least-squares linear regression analysis of measured R_T vs pad spacing d (5 um to 80 um) logged in CSV data |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 24 probe card pins exhibit planarity within <= 3.5 um total range, zero pad edge punch-through across 100% inspected test dies, TLM linear regression R^2 >= 0.998, and formal engineering signoff approved by Systems Engineer and Metrology Lead.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Four-Point Probe & Metal-1/Via-1 Kelvin Contact Resistance Characterization

**Context Hierarchy**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > Interconnect Sputtering & Die Packaging Probe Station > Interconnect Contact Resistance & Wafer-Level Electrical Die Probing (EDP) > Four-Point Probe & Metal-1/Via-1 Kelvin Contact Resistance Characterization

**Action Type**: Make

### 1. Process Flow Diagram

```text
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐

             │
             ▼

└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Measure RT across    │
│  Pad Spacings: 5, 10,  │
│     20, 40, 80 um      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Extract Rc from     │
│   Y-intercept and LT   │
│    from X-intercept    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Compute Contact     │
│  Resistivity: rhoc =   │
│      Rc * W * LT       │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

#### Step 1: Probe Head Alignment & Tool Calibration
1. Mount a collinear four-point probe head fitted with four equally spaced tungsten carbide tips having tip radii of $r = 50\text{--}100\ \mu\text{m}$ and uniform tip spacing $s = 1.0\ \text{mm}$.
2. Align probe tips orthogonal to the wafer plane and verify that edge proximity conditions are accounted for using geometric correction factor $F(d/s)$ if wafer diameter $< 40 \times s$.

#### Step 2: Collinear Four-Point Probe Sheet Resistance ($R_s$) Measurement
1. Bring probe tips into soft mechanical contact with the Metal-1 / diffusion thin-film test area (film thickness $t \ll s/2$).
2. Force a regulated constant DC current of $I = 1\ \text{mA}$ to $10\ \text{mA}$ across the outer two probes (probe 1 and probe 4).
3. Concurrently measure the floating potential difference $V$ across the inner two sense probes (probe 2 and probe 3) using a high-impedance digital electrometer/voltmeter.
4. Calculate thin-film sheet resistance:
   $$R_s = \frac{\pi}{\ln(2)} \cdot \left(\frac{V}{I}\right) = 4.5324 \cdot \left(\frac{V}{I}\right)\quad [\Omega/\square]$$

#### Step 3: Metal-1/Via-1 Kelvin Contact & TLM Structure Alignment
1. Switch to the micro-probing station with motorized manipulators and locate the Transmission Line Measurement (TLM) test structure array on the wafer.
2. Verify test structure geometry: identical rectangular contact pads with width $W = 100\ \mu\text{m}$, pad length $L_{\text{pad}} = 50\ \mu\text{m}$, and progressive test gaps:
   $$d \in \{5\ \mu\text{m},\ 10\ \mu\text{m},\ 20\ \mu\text{m},\ 40\ \mu\text{m},\ 80\ \mu\text{m}\}$$

#### Step 4: TLM Kelvin Resistance Extraction
1. Apply 4-wire Kelvin probing across adjacent pairs of pads for each spacing $d$ and record total resistance:
   $$R_T = 2 R_c + \left(\frac{R_s}{W}\right) \cdot d$$
2. Construct the linear regression plot of total measured resistance $R_T$ versus pad spacing $d$:
   - **Slope**: $\text{Slope} = \frac{R_s}{W}$ (extracts diffusion sheet resistance $R_s$).
   - **Y-intercept ($d = 0$)**: $Y_0 = 2 R_c$ (yields single contact resistance $R_c = \frac{Y_0}{2}$).
   - **X-intercept ($R_T = 0$)**: $X_0 = -2 L_T$ (yields transfer length $L_T = -\frac{X_0}{2}$).

#### Step 5: Specific Contact Resistivity Computation
1. Compute the specific contact resistivity ($\rho_c$) using:
   $$\rho_c = R_c \cdot W \cdot L_T = R_s \cdot L_T^2\quad [\Omega\cdot\text{cm}^2]$$
2. Log values into wafer lot tracking and cross-validate against Four-Point Probe thin-film data.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Metric ID | Parameter | Target Specification & Tolerance | Exact Physical Units | Verification Method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **AC-01** | Probe Tip Spacing ($s$) | $1.0 \pm 0.01$ | $\text{mm}$ | Optical Micrometer / Calibration Reticle |
| **AC-02** | Probe Tip Radius ($r$) | $50 \text{ to } 100$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Optical Profilometry |
| **AC-03** | DC Injection Current ($I$) | $1.0 \text{ to } 10.0$ | $\text{mA}$ | Precision Source Measure Unit (SMU) |
| **AC-04** | TLM Contact Pad Dimensions | Width $W = 100 \pm 1$, Length $L_{\text{pad}} = 50 \pm 1$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Automated Optical Metrology (CD-SEM / Microscope) |
| **AC-05** | TLM Inter-Pad Spacings ($d$) | $5,\ 10,\ 20,\ 40,\ 80$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Lithographic Mask & CD Metrology |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Sources

- **Source: Four-Point Collinear Probe Metrology for Semiconductor Sheet Resistance**:
  - Probe geometry: 4 collinear tungsten carbide tips, tip radius $50\text{--}100\ \mu\text{m}$, spacing $s = 1.0\ \text{mm}$.
  - Current excitation: $I = 1\ \text{mA}$ to $10\ \text{mA}$ across probes 1 and 4; potential $V$ measured across probes 2 and 3.
  - Formula: $R_s = \frac{\pi}{\ln(2)} \cdot (V/I) = 4.5324 \cdot (V/I)\ [\Omega/\square]$ with edge proximity factor $F(d/s)$ for finite wafer dimensions ($< 40 \times s$).
- **Source: Transmission Line Measurement (TLM) for Specific Contact Resistivity**:
  - Structure layout: Rectangular contact pads with width $W = 100\ \mu\text{m}$, length $L_{\text{pad}} = 50\ \mu\text{m}$, spaced at $d = 5\ \mu\text{m}, 10\ \mu\text{m}, 20\ \mu\text{m}, 40\ \mu\text{m}, 80\ \mu\text{m}$.
  - Formulation: $R_T = 2 R_c + (R_s / W) \cdot d$, with slope $= R_s / W$, Y-intercept $= 2 R_c$, X-intercept $= -2 L_T$, and specific contact resistivity $\rho_c = R_c \cdot W \cdot L_T = R_s \cdot L_T^2\ [\Omega\cdot\text{cm}^2]$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automated Kelvin and four-point probe (4PP) testing across the 150mm/200mm wafer requires strict triaxial shielding and low-current sub-femtoamp matrix switching (Keysight B2201A or Keithley 707B). Thermal drift and parasitic series lead resistance across multi-pin probe cards can obscure contact resistances sub-1 Ohm. The probe station must guarantee mechanical z-axis repeatability within +/- 0.5 um to avoid punch-through into underlying inter-layer dielectric (ILD) or underlying poly-silicon wordline stacks.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For 180nm node DRAM peripheral/sense amplifier interconnects, Metal-1 (Al-0.5%Cu or Cu dual damascene) to Diffusion/Poly Via-1 contact resistance must be extracted using Kelvin 4-terminal cross-bridge resistor (CBR) and Transmission Line Measurement (TLM) structures. Specific contact resistivity rho_c must achieve <= 1.0e-7 Ohm*cm^2 to prevent degraded bitline sense amplifier sensing latency. Native aluminum oxide regrowth or polymer residues inside 0.22 um Via-1 vias will cause non-linear Schottky-like I-V characteristics instead of ohmic behavior.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Tungsten carbide and beryllium copper 4PP head assemblies (1.0 mm collinear pitch, 50-100 um tip radius) have limited tip life (approx. 50,000 touchdowns) before tip flattening degrades edge correction factor F(d/s) accuracy. Sourcing precision calibration sheet resistance transfer standards (VLSI Standards certified polysilicon and aluminum thin-film reference wafers) faces a 12-week procurement lead time under current global export-controlled metrology channels.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Characterization throughput is constrained to <= 45 minutes per wafer across a 13-site map. Metrology operators must log Kelvin contact resistance data directly into the automated yield management system (YMS) before releasing the split-lot for ILD-2 oxide deposition to eliminate wafer scrap risks from high-resistance via chains.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dielectric punch-through and micro-cracking of TEOS/FSG ILD caused by excessive probe contact overdrive (> 10 um beyond touch-down).
1. Spurious non-ohmic contact behavior due to incomplete clean of fluorocarbon polymer residues after Via-1 reactive ion etching (RIE).
1. Native oxidation of Metal-1 pad surfaces exceeding queue-time limits, introducing false positive interface resistance (> 15 Ohm/via) during Kelvin extraction.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-3-2-01` | **Metal-1 Thin Film Sheet Resistance Collinear Four-Point Probe Characterization** | Collinear Four-Point Probe Head (Tungsten carbide tips, 1.0 mm tip spacing s, tip radius 100 um), Keithley 2450 SourceMeter, Keithley 2182A Nanovoltmeter, Chuck vacuum stage with thermal control at 25.0 +/- 0.5 deg C | 1. Load wafer on vacuum chuck at 25 deg C. 2. Lower four-point probe head onto center of wafer until 100 gf spring overdrive is reached. 3. Force forward current I_fwd = +10.00 mA across outer pins 1 and 4 using Keithley 2450. 4. Measure floating differential voltage V_fwd across inner pins 2 and 3 using Keithley 2182A with 10 PLC integration. 5. Reverse polarity to force reverse current I_rev = -10.00 mA and measure V_rev. 6. Calculate Delta V / Delta I = (V_fwd - V_rev) / 20.0 mA. 7. Compute Sheet Resistance R_s = 4.5324 * (Delta V / Delta I). 8. Repeat across 9 standard radial sites. | `Average Sheet Resistance R_s must be 0.075 to 0.088 Ohm/square; cross-wafer non-uniformity (1-sigma / mean) <= 2.5%; absolute delta between forward and reverse resistance <= 0.3%.` |
| `TC-DRAM-ROOT-SUB-3-3-2-02` | **Metal-1/Via-1 Kelvin Four-Terminal Cross-Bridge Contact Resistance & TLM Extraction** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Parameter Analyzer (4x HRSMU with triax cabling), Cascade Microtech Summit 12000 Semi-Automated Probe Station, 4-pin Kelvin probe card (W-tip radius 12 um) | 1. Align probe card to Kelvin Via-1 test structure (Via size 0.22 um x 0.22 um nominal). 2. Contact Force SMU1 to Pad A (Metal-1 run), Sense SMU2 to Pad B (Metal-1 sense). 3. Contact Force SMU3 to Pad C (Metal-2 tap), Sense SMU4 to Pad D (Metal-2 sense). 4. Sweep forced current I_force from -1.0 mA to +1.0 mA in 50 uA steps between SMU1 and SMU3. 5. Measure voltage drop V_kelvin between SMU2 and SMU4. 6. Extract Kelvin contact resistance R_c = dV_kelvin / dI_force via linear regression across [-1 mA, +1 mA]. 7. Step to adjacent TLM ladder structure (d = 5, 10, 20, 40, 80 um; W = 100 um) and execute 2-wire sweep; extract specific contact resistivity rho_c. | `Individual Kelvin Via-1 resistance R_c <= 2.20 Ohm/via; I-V curve linearity correlation coefficient R^2 >= 0.9995 across [-1 mA, +1 mA]; extracted specific contact resistivity rho_c <= 1.0e-7 Ohm*cm^2.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses with side shields, ESD-safe anti-static cleanroom smock and grounded wrist strap, Cleanroom safety shoes with conductive soles
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with IPA: Remove contaminated gloves and flush skin with flowing water for 15 minutes. Eye exposure: Immediately irrigate eyes at nearest eyewash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Inhalation: Move personnel to fresh air immediately. Mechanical pin-prick injury: Flush wound with sterile saline, apply cleanroom antiseptic pad, report to fab medical bay.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Probe station enclosure must maintain local laminar HEPA downflow (0.45 m/s +/- 0.05 m/s) with solvent exhaust extraction port (minimum 50 CFM face velocity) active during probe-tip alcohol wipe maintenance.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: IPA-wetted wipes and swab applicators must be segregated into dedicated labeled flame-retardant solvent waste cans with spring-loaded self-closing lids. No drain disposal allowed; route solid hazardous waste to licensed incineration vendor.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic / VLSI Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Deionized Water** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type 1 (> 18.2 MOhm*cm) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly etched/CMP-cleared Metal-1 or tungsten Via-1 test pads, free from organic slurry films, halogen residue, and moisture (< 1.5 nm native oxide).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Electrically probed test pads showing microscopic probe scrubbing witness marks (mark area <= 15% of pad size, scrub depth < 60 nm), desiccated and passivated for dielectric deposition.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air queue time causes ambient moisture-induced galvanic corrosion of Al-Cu lines and native oxide growth exceeding 3.5 nm, producing non-ohmic Kelvin measurements and erratic open-circuit anomalies during probing.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Complete electrical sheet resistance and contact resistance verification across 180nm DRAM Metal-1 thin films and Metal-1/Via-1 contacts. The delivered artifacts validate ohmic contact linearity, via resistance conformance, and process uniformity across the wafer diameter before releasing split lots to inter-metal dielectric passivations.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `M1_VIA1_KELVIN_METROLOGY_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `FOUR_POINT_PROBE_SHEET_RESISTANCE_RAW.csv`
- [ ] `PROBE_MARK_OVERDRIVE_IMPACT_MAP.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Metal-1 (Al-0.5%Cu 400nm) thin-film sheet resistance measured via collinear four-point probe** | `0.082 Ohm/sq` | +/- 0.006 Ohm/sq | Dual-polarity 4-point collinear DC V/I method at 9 radial wafer sites |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Metal-1 to Via-1 (0.22 um tungsten plug) Kelvin 4-terminal contact resistance** | `1.85 Ohm/via` | <= 2.20 Ohm/via max | Keysight B1500A Kelvin cross-bridge sweep [-1 mA to +1 mA] |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Specific contact resistivity (rho_c) extracted from Transmission Line Measurement (TLM) structure** | `6.5e-8 Ohm*cm^2` | <= 1.0e-7 Ohm*cm^2 | Linear regression extrapolation of R_T vs pad spacing d (5 um to 80 um) |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 13 test dies across the wafer show linear ohmic Kelvin Via-1 characteristics (R^2 >= 0.9995), Kelvin contact resistance <= 2.20 Ohm/via, specific contact resistivity rho_c <= 1.0e-7 Ohm*cm^2, probe mark scrub depth < 60 nm confirmed by optical profilometry, and signed approval from Domain Metrology Lead and Fab Quality Manager.
